title: Private (incognito) windows with an in-memory container and a visible mark
spec: Chrome: Ctrl+Shift+N (Cmd+Shift+N) opens an incognito window. Its tabs share one off-the-record profile that is never written to disk: no history, cookies, closed-tab or session entries survive. Closing the last incognito window wipes it, and the window is clearly marked. Today wubble has nothing like this: no code names private or incognito. Build it on the existing model. A private window is a Main window (`wubble_core::window::Shown::Space`) showing a private Space. Add a `SpaceKind`-style flag beside `Space::agent` in crates/wubble-core/src/space.rs and an `ephemeral` container in `Container`. Add `Command::NewPrivateWindow` in model.rs and model/windows.rs. While it is open, a private window is locked to its Space: SwitchSpace and Space switcher entries are refused, and new tabs, popups and links land in it. Tabs cannot move between private and normal Spaces (tabdrag `MoveToWindow`, MoveTab, the Move to Space and Window menu rows). Closing the window closes its tabs and deletes the Space and its container (`Profiles::close`). The engine opens an ephemeral container with `SharedProfile::new(runtime, None)` in crates/wubble-engine/src/storage.rs (`Profiles::get`). Under CEF's Chrome runtime that is an off-the-record profile, and `storage::forget` must never touch it. Several things skip private Spaces, the way agent Spaces are skipped today (`self.agents.spaces()`, `closes_into_recent`, `visit_to_record` in host.rs): persist::save and wubble-store/src/session.rs write_spaces, history visits, favicons, recently closed, archive, per-site zoom writes, the downloads list (the file itself is kept), routing rules, Little windows, MCP sessions and extensions. Add an `Action::NewPrivateWindow` with the default chord Mod+Shift+N in keys.rs and a palette title. Add 'Open Link in Private Window' to menu.rs ROWS. The mark: a derived kit piece (a Private chip in the sidebar header plus a dark tint) goes on docs/fidelity/derived-review.md, and the window title gets a 'Private' suffix.

title: Multiple profiles, guest profile and a profile switcher
spec: Chrome: several profiles, each with its own history, bookmarks, passwords, settings and cookies. A profile menu and picker (Ctrl+Shift+M) opens a window of another profile, a Guest profile is thrown away on close, and `--profile-directory=Name` chooses one. Today wubble has one profile per process, chosen only by `--profile DIR` (crates/wubble/src/profile.rs `Profile::resolve`). The instance socket is already per profile (crates/wubble/src/instance.rs). CEF's `root_cache_path` is process-wide, so each profile runs as its own wubble process. Build: a pure `wubble_core::profiles` module covering the list, names, tint, last used, the default profile and the picker choice, with unit tests. It is stored in one small `profiles.json` in the per-user data dir (`app::user_data_dir`), not in any profile's database. The default profile stays at today's directory so nothing migrates. New profiles go in `<data>/Profiles/<id>`. Opening another profile spawns `current_exe --profile <dir>`, or forwards `Message::Focus` to its live instance. Guest: `--guest` makes a fresh profile under `~/Dev`-independent user data (`<data>/Guest`), never in /tmp, and deletes it at exit and again at the next start. Add a Settings section 'Profiles' (settings.rs `Section`, settings page in wubble-ui) to add, rename, delete (with a confirm) and open profiles. Add a command-bar entry and `Action::SwitchProfile` on Ctrl+Shift+M (Cmd+Shift+M), which opens the picker sheet. The profile name goes in the window title and in a small sidebar footer mark (derived kit piece). The picker at start is shown only when the 'Show on startup' setting is on.

title: Capture each tab's back/forward entries, and the back button history menu
spec: Chrome keeps every tab's navigation stack (URL, title, index). It shows the stack on right-click or long-press of back and forward, and Ctrl/middle-click on back opens that entry in a new tab. Session restore, reopen closed tab and duplicate all carry the stack. Today wubble keeps only `Tab::url`, and nothing reads navigation entries (TODO: 'Undo close tab ... bring back the URL only'). Build the capture half. Read the stack after each committed navigation and before a close or discard. Use `CefBrowserHost::GetNavigationEntries` with a visitor in crates/wubble-engine (nav.rs or view.rs), or CDP `Page.getNavigationHistory` through cdp.rs, reported as a new page event. Keep it in a host-side table keyed by TabId (one owner, out of `Model` so model saves stay cheap), capped at Chromium's 50 entries (`kMaxPersistNavigationCount`). Persist it in wubble-store with a migration: a `tab_history` table (tab id, index, url, title) written with the session, and the same columns for `recently_closed` rows (crates/wubble-store/src/closed.rs `ClosedTab` gains `entries` and `index`). Skip agent and private tabs. UI: right-click or press-and-hold on the back and forward lights (`.wb-nav`) opens a kit menu of entries (`menu.rs` entries style, like `tab_entries`). Choosing one calls CDP `Page.navigateToHistoryEntry` or GoBack/GoForward n times. Ctrl/middle-click on back or forward opens that entry in a background tab. A 'Show full history' row opens wubble://history.

title: Recently closed windows, folders and Spaces, and a recently-closed list UI
spec: Chrome's TabRestoreService keeps tabs, whole windows and tab groups. Ctrl+Shift+T reopens the newest entry of any kind, and the History menu and tab search list 'Recently closed' with titles. Today crates/wubble-core/src/closed.rs and wubble-store/src/closed.rs keep tab entries only, and nothing lists them (`Store::recently_closed` has no caller in crates/wubble). A closed Main window keeps its Space, so it is not remembered at all (model/windows.rs close_window), and a closed folder or deleted Space adds its tabs one by one, if at all. Build: generalize the store row into an entry enum, `Tab | Window { space, geometry } | Folder { name, tabs } | Space { name, tint, icon, container, tabs }`, with a migration. Grouped entries carry child tab rows with url, title, container, place and, once captured, history. Record a Window entry in `close_window` (and a Space entry from `DeleteSpace` and `FolderRow::Close`, when they actually close tabs). Extend the `closed::Event` and `Effect` machine: `Restore` gains a window variant (reopen a Main window on that Space at its geometry, or recreate the Space if it is gone) and a folder or Space variant. Mod+Shift+T and Mod+Z pop any kind. UI: a 'Recently closed' block at the top of wubble://history (pages.rs, history page model), and command-bar rows (bar.rs) listing the entries with titles. Each row reopens its entry and can be deleted on its own. Keep RECENTLY_CLOSED_MAX at 25 entries. Agent and private tabs stay off the list.

title: Startup, home page and quit settings
spec: Chrome's 'On startup' setting offers: open the New Tab page, continue where you left off, or open a specific set of pages. There is a Home page (Alt+Home / Cmd+Shift+H), a 'Restore pages?' offer after a crash, and on macOS 'Warn before quitting'. The design's settings (pages/settings.tsx row `startup`: 'When Wubble opens', Start page | Last session) have the first two. wubble has no such setting: it always restores the stored session (wubble-store session.rs load_session). Build: settings rows in crates/wubble-core/src/settings.rs. `startup.mode` is a Select of Last session (default), Start page, or Specific pages. `startup.pages` is a list editor of URLs, shown only for Specific pages. `home.url` is empty for the start page. `quit.warn` (macOS default on) requires a second Cmd+Q or a hold. At start, in crates/wubble/src (where the loaded Model is handed to the host): with Start page, keep Spaces, pinned tabs and folders, but open a start tab in each window. The unpinned tabs of the last session go to the archive or recently closed, following Chrome's 'new tab page' semantics: they are not restored. Pinned tabs always stay. With Specific pages, open those pages as new tabs. Record a clean-exit flag in the store. When the last run did not exit cleanly and the mode is not Last session, show a kit banner 'Restore pages?' that restores the saved session. Add `Action::GoHome` (Alt+Home on Linux/Windows, Cmd+Shift+H on macOS) and a palette title 'Home'. Add a command-bar row 'Open pages from last session'.

title: Window state in the session: maximized, fullscreen, display and popup windows
spec: Chrome stores each window's bounds, its show state (normal, maximized, minimized, fullscreen) and its display, and restores popup and app windows too. wubble saves `Geometry { width, height, pos }` for Main windows only (crates/wubble-core/src/window.rs, wubble-store/src/session.rs write_windows/load_windows). Little and Popup windows are dropped, and a maximized or fullscreen window comes back as a plain window of its last size. Build: add `WindowState { Normal, Maximized, Fullscreen, Minimized }` to `Geometry` (or beside it), and add the monitor name where winit gives it. Store them in the `windows` table with a migration. Feed them from the host's winit events (crates/wubble/src/host/window.rs, Command::ResizeWindow). On load, apply them through winit (`set_maximized`, `set_fullscreen(Borderless(monitor))`, `set_outer_position` where not Wayland). Clamp a position that is off every current monitor (Chrome's `WindowSizer::AdjustBoundsToBeVisibleOnDisplay`). Keep Popup windows (`Shown::Popup`) in the session as windows of their tab, the way Chrome restores TYPE_POPUP windows. A Little window's tab stays a normal tab, as now. Restore the windows' focus order (the stored position column) so the last focused window comes up on top. A new window (Mod+N) takes the focused window's size, offset by Chrome's cascade (10 px) where positions are known. Unit tests for the store round trip and the clamp go in wubble-core and wubble-store.

title: Tab tear-off: new window at the drop point, drop into a window at a row
spec: Chrome: a tab dragged out of the strip becomes a live window following the pointer. Released, it stays where it was dropped, at the source window's size. Dropped onto another window's strip, it goes in at the hovered position. wubble's `tabdrag` machine (crates/wubble-core/src/tabdrag.rs) decides `Effect::MoveToWindow { to: WindowTarget::New | Existing }`. But `Model::move_tab_to_window` (model/windows.rs) creates the new window with `geometry: None` (the platform default place and size), and always puts the tab last (`index: usize::MAX`) in the target Space. Build: carry the drop point and the source window's size into `WindowTarget::New { geometry }` and `Geometry.pos` on X11, macOS and Windows, so the window opens under the pointer, offset by the grab point within the row. For `Existing(w)`, hit-test the target window's tab list: add `list` rects of other windows to `Targets.windows` in crates/wubble/src/host/tab_drag.rs `other_windows`. Pass a `Dest` (pinned, normal or folder index) so the tab lands at the hovered row, and the target window's rows show the gap while hovering (`tabs::TabRows`). Also move whole folders and split groups when their header or a split pane is dragged out (Chrome moves a whole group). Unit tests go in tabdrag.rs and model/tests.rs. On Wayland positions stay unknown: see wayland-tab-drag.

title: Wayland: drag tabs between windows and live tear-off via the data device
spec: Chrome on Wayland drags tabs between windows with a real wl_data_device drag. With `xdg_toplevel_drag_v1` (KWin, Mutter 46+, wlroots) the torn-off window itself follows the pointer. wubble cannot do either today. tabdrag.rs states that on Wayland a release outside the window is always `Outside` (a new window), and `other_windows` is empty there. Build: when a tab drag leaves the window on Wayland, start a data-device drag from the platform worker behind the `Aux` trait (crates/wubble/src/wl/wayland.rs, which already does drags out, `drag_file.rs`) with a private MIME type `application/x-wubble-tab` carrying the profile's instance id and the TabId. Every wubble window's surface already receives data-device enter, motion and drop. Map an offer of that type to `DropTarget::Window(id)` with a local point, and feed motion into the tabdrag machine of the target window so its list shows the gap. Drop then runs `MoveTabToWindow { Existing }` with the row from tear-off-fidelity. If the compositor advertises `xdg_toplevel_drag_manager_v1` (wayland-protocols staging), create the new window at drag start, attach it with `xdg_toplevel_drag_v1.attach` at the grab offset, and move the tab into it at once, so the window travels with the pointer and is placed where it is dropped. Otherwise keep today's open-on-release behaviour. A cancelled drag (Esc, or a drop on another app) returns the tab, or keeps the new window under xdg_toplevel_drag. Refuse offers from another profile or process.

title: Tab groups parity for folders: colour, new tab in group, move, save, keyboard
spec: Chrome tab groups have a name and one of nine colours, collapse, 'New tab in group', 'Ungroup', 'Close group', 'Move group to new window', and saved groups that come back after closing. Tabs join through 'Add tab to group > existing / New group', and the group's colour marks its tabs. wubble's folders (`space::Folder { id, name, tabs, collapsed }`, `tabmenu::FOLDER_ROWS`: Rename, Collapse, Ungroup, Close) cover name, collapse, ungroup and close. Build: `Folder.tint: Option<Rgb>` from `space::swatches()`, stored in wubble-store session.rs write_folders with a migration, and drawn through the kit folder-row (crates/wubble-ui/ui/kit/chrome, components/folder-row.slint binding only), with a colour row in the folder menu. 'New tab in folder' appends a start tab inside it (a `Dest::Folder` index). 'Move folder to' lists other Spaces plus 'New window' and moves all its tabs with their order (reuse MoveTab/MoveTabToWindow, as one Command). The Close entry records a folder entry on the recently closed list (see recently-closed-full). 'Save folder': a saved folder stays as a bookmark folder (wubble-store bookmarks.rs) and can be reopened from the folder menu and the command bar. Tab-menu rows 'Add to folder' with each folder and 'New folder' exist through `Row::Folders`; keep them. Unit tests for the model commands go in model/tests.rs, and the tabmenu tests cover the new rows.

title: Select several tabs (Ctrl/Shift+click) and act on the selection
spec: Chrome: Ctrl/Cmd+click adds a tab to the selection, Shift+click selects a range. The tab menu then acts on all selected tabs: close, pin, mute, move to a new window, add to a group, reload, duplicate, bookmark. Dragging moves them together. wubble has `Command::CloseTabs(Vec<TabId>)` but no selection: Shift+click on a tab row is the peek (`Glance`) and Ctrl+click is a background tab only for links. Build: a pure selection state in wubble-core (a new `tabselect` module or inside `tabs`), owned once: the anchor and the set, cleared on activation of an unselected tab, on a Space switch and when tabs close. Unit tests come with it. The tab row (kit/chrome/tab-row.slint) reports the modifiers on press (a callback argument, no new drawing). The selected look uses the row's existing hover or selected state from the kit, or a derived piece put on the review sheet. In crates/wubble-core/src/tabmenu.rs `entries` takes the selection: labels read 'Close 3 tabs', 'Pin tabs', 'Move tabs to new window', 'New folder with 3 tabs', 'Mute tabs', and `Run` gets list variants that the host maps to one Command each (CloseTabs, a new PinTabs/MoveTabs/FolderWithTabs). Dragging a selected row moves the whole selection in order through tabdrag (reorder, onto a Space, into a split edge with exactly two, tear-out). Pinned and normal tabs are kept apart, as Chrome does. Escape clears the selection.

title: Tab search (Ctrl+Shift+A): all open and recently closed tabs in one list
spec: Chrome's Tab Search (Ctrl+Shift+A, Cmd+Shift+A) is a popover that lists every open tab of every window, most recent first, with favicons, titles, sites and a close button per row. It fuzzy-filters as you type, Enter switches to the tab and its window, and a 'Recently closed' section follows, with groups shown as groups. wubble's command bar already matches open tabs (crates/wubble/src/bar.rs `open_tabs`, omnibox.rs `Kind::OpenTab`), but only mixed with history and only once you type. Build a tab-search mode of the command bar. `Action::SearchTabs` gets the default chord Mod+Shift+A in keys.rs and the palette title 'Search tabs'. The empty query lists all open tabs across Spaces: the active Space first, then others by `Tab::last_active_ms`, each row showing its Space name. Agent tabs are left out and private tabs show only in their private window. Recently closed entries follow from the store (`Store::recently_closed`, see recently-closed-full). Typing filters with the same matcher omnibox uses, so the rows come from one pure function in wubble-core/src/omnibox.rs with tests. Enter or a click runs `Command::ActivateTab` plus a window focus or Space switch for a tab of another Space (reuse `Target::OpenTab`). A per-row close (kit list row's trailing button, as in the history page rows) closes the tab without leaving the list. Up/Down and Delete work from the keyboard.

title: Mute site, and the Chrome tab and link menu rows still missing
spec: Chrome's tab context menu offers 'New tab to the right', 'Mute site' or 'Unmute site' (a per-site sound content setting that survives restarts and applies to every tab of the site), 'Move tab to new window', 'Close tabs to the right' and 'Close other tabs'. Its link menu has 'Open link in new window' and 'Open link in incognito window'. wubble's `tabmenu::ROWS` (crates/wubble-core/src/tabmenu.rs) has a per-tab mute (`Run::ToggleMute`), Close others, Close below and the window entries. menu.rs ROWS deliberately leave out 'Open Link in New Window' ('one window'), which is no longer true since Main windows exist. Build: 1) `Row::NewTabBelow`, a start tab placed right under this one (`Command::NewTab` with an index, or a new `Dest`). 2) `Row::MuteSite`, a site sound rule stored like the other per-site settings (a `sound.muted_sites` list in settings.rs, the same shape as `sleep.never_sites`). The host applies it with `CefBrowserHost::SetAudioMuted` on every view of the site on commit, and with CEF's content setting `CEF_CONTENT_SETTING_TYPE_SOUND` through `CefRequestContext::SetContentSetting` per container. Settings > Privacy lists the sites. `tabmarks::Marks` shows muted for them. 3) A link-menu row 'Open Link in New Window' in crates/wubble/src/menu.rs (`Command::NewWindow` with a URL, opening in a new or free Space), and 'Open Link in Private Window' once private-windows lands. Update the menu tests.

title: Chrome keyboard shortcuts wubble does not bind yet
spec: Compared with Chromium's `chrome/browser/ui/accelerator_table.cc` (already a cited source of keys.rs DEFAULTS), these are missing from crates/wubble-core/src/action.rs `Action`, `FIXED`, `PALETTE` and keys.rs `DEFAULTS`. Ctrl+Shift+PageUp/PageDown moves the tab up or down (`Action::MoveTabUp/Down` via `Command::MoveTab`, staying inside pinned/normal/folder). Cmd+Shift+[ and Cmd+Shift+] select the previous and next tab on macOS; Cmd+Alt+Left/Right stays NextSpace. Ctrl+Shift+Delete (Cmd+Shift+Backspace) is `ClearBrowsingData` (exists, unbound). Ctrl+S is Save Page As (the menu row exists in menu.rs; add `Action::SavePage`). Ctrl+O opens a local file through the file chooser and opens file:// in a new tab. Ctrl+Shift+J and Cmd+Alt+J open DevTools on the Console. Ctrl+Shift+V / Cmd+Shift+Alt+V is paste as plain text (CEF frame `PasteAndMatchStyle`, through the Edit-command path). F7 toggles caret browsing (Chrome pref `settings.a11y.caret_browsing.enabled` via `CefRequestContext::SetPreference`, with Chrome's confirm). Ctrl+E focuses the address with a search prefix. Cmd+M minimizes the window on macOS. Cmd+` and Cmd+Shift+` cycle wubble's windows (`Action::NextWindow` with `Command::FocusWindow`), and Ctrl+Shift+Tab-style window cycling uses Alt+F6-free chords on Linux. In the address and command bar: Alt+Enter opens the result in a new tab, Ctrl+Enter adds www. and .com, Shift+Enter opens in a new window (bar.rs and omnibox.rs submit get a disposition). Keep each row `PageFirst` or `Shell` as Chromium does. Add keymap tests for conflicts and the editor labels.

title: Command bar: inline autocomplete and Chrome's omnibox keys
spec:
Chrome finishes a typed address inside the field. Type 'git' and it shows 'github.com/' with the added part selected. Right or End accepts it, Backspace drops it, Enter goes to the completed URL. Only a history entry whose host or URL starts with the typed text and whose typed_count is above 0 (or that has a high visit_count) is offered. wubble has no inline completion. CommandHead (crates/wubble-ui/ui/kit/chrome/command-head.slint) handles only Up, Down, Enter and Escape, and omnibox::rank (crates/wubble-core/src/omnibox.rs) returns rows only.

Add a pure fn `inline_completion(query, &[HistoryEntry], &[Bookmark]) -> Option<String>` to wubble-core/omnibox.rs, ported from Chromium's HistoryURLProvider and ShortcutsProvider inline rules (BSD-3, behaviour only). It returns the suffix, which is never offered for a query that ends in a space or right after a deletion. Make rank's first row the completed URL when there is one. Add an `inline` property to CommandHead and set the selection with TextInput.set-selection-offsets.

Add Chrome's keys there, passed up as new callbacks:
- Tab and Shift+Tab move between rows.
- Shift+Delete on a History row removes it: HistoryClear::Url through host/pages.rs history_deleted, then re-rank.
- Alt+Enter (Option on macOS) opens in a new tab: BarMode::NewTab in bar.rs target_command.
- Shift+Enter opens a new window.
- Ctrl+Enter wraps a bare word as www.<word>.com before classify.

Wire it in crates/wubble/src/bar.rs and the host's command-bar handling. Add unit tests in omnibox.rs for the completion rule and Ctrl+Enter.

title: Command bar: local calculator and unit conversion answers
spec:
Chrome's omnibox answers '12*7+3', 'sqrt(2)', '5 km in miles' and '70 F to C' as a row above the search. Chrome gets these from the server; wubble must compute them on the device with no request. Today omnibox::Kind (crates/wubble-core/src/omnibox.rs) has OpenTab/History/Bookmark/Search/Action and there is no answer row.

Add a pure module wubble-core/src/answer.rs with:
- a small expression parser: + - * / ^ %, parentheses, unary minus, constants pi and e, the functions sqrt, sin, cos, tan, log, ln, abs and round, and percent-of. Write it new or port an MIT/Apache crate such as `meval` (licence check, source comment, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry).
- a units table as data: length, mass, volume, temperature, speed, area, data size and time, with the forms '<n> <unit> in|to <unit>'.
- number formatting that trims trailing zeros.

Add Kind::Answer and Target::Copy(String). Choosing the row copies the result through crates/wubble/src/clipboard.rs and shows a toast. Map Kind::Answer to a new CommandKind `answer` in crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/model.slint and kit command-row.slint, reusing an existing glyph (equals/calculator from kit gen icons if present, else note it on derived-review.md). In rank, the answer goes first when the query parses as math with at least one operator, and second, under the search intent, for unit forms. A query that is only a number gives no answer. No currency: it would need a network rate source. Unit tests for parsing, precedence, division by zero (no row) and each unit family.

title: Search engines: more built-ins, custom engines with keywords, management in Settings
spec:
Chrome keeps a list of search engines, each with a name, a keyword and a URL with %s. You can set any of them as the default, add and edit your own, and site searches are picked up from pages. wubble has only `ENGINES: [EngineInfo; 2]` (Google, DuckDuckGo) in crates/wubble-core/src/omnibox.rs, chosen by the `search.engine` Select in settings.rs.

1. Extend ENGINES with Bing, Brave Search, Ecosia, Startpage, Qwant, Kagi and Wikipedia (search and suggest templates from Chromium's prepopulated_engines.json, BSD-3), each with a default keyword. Never rename the shipped ids.
2. Add a setting `search.custom` as a list setting (the list-editor kind with columns_of in pages.rs: name, keyword, URL with %s or {q}). Validate it in a pure fn: exactly one placeholder, http(s) only, unique keyword.
3. Let the default be any built-in or custom engine. Replace the SearchEngine enum where it is used (bar.rs, suggest.rs suggest_url, the start page capsule, menu.rs search_label) with an `EngineRef` resolved from settings. Live suggestions stay behind `suggest.live`, and only for engines with a suggest URL.
4. OpenSearch discovery: a page script reads <link rel=search type=application/opensearchdescription+xml>. Fetching the OSDD (crates/wubble-engine/src/fetch.rs) happens only behind a new setting `search.discover_sites`, off by default. Discovered engines are listed as inactive in Settings, never made the default.

The Settings section shows the default engine, the built-in list and the custom list editor. Unit tests for the template checks and engine resolution.

title: X11: page drags out to other apps and drops in of links, HTML and text (XDND)
spec: Chrome on X11 lets a link, a text selection, an image or an HTML draggable leave the window and drop into other apps (text/uri-list, _NETSCAPE_URL, text/x-moz-url, text/html, UTF8_STRING, the image as a file), and it takes drops from other apps of files, links, HTML and text. In wubble under X11, `crate::clipboard::Clipboard` is `wayland::Wayland`, whose worker never opens, so `Host::aux()` (crates/wubble/src/host/drag.rs) falls back to `crate::wl::Null`. `drags_out()` is false, so a page drag that leaves the window ends at `Over::Elsewhere`. Drops in arrive only as winit's `HoveredFile`/`DroppedFile`, which means files only: a link or text dragged from another app into a page or onto the tab list does nothing. To build: add `crates/wubble/src/wl/x11.rs`, one worker on its own x11rb connection (MIT/Apache) that implements `crate::wl::Aux`. As drag source: own XdndSelection, an XDND source loop with XdndEnter, Position and Drop, offers built from `wubble_core::dnd`'s tables (add `_NETSCAPE_URL` for X11, as Chromium's `ui/base/x/x11_drag_drop_client.cc` does), the picture through `drag_file.rs`, and the drag image in a shaped ARGB override-redirect window that follows the pointer. On drop end it delivers `AuxEvent::DragEnded`. As drop target: set XdndAware on each window in `add_window`, read the offer with `dnd::plan`, and deliver `DropEnter/DropMove/Dropped/DropLeave`. `drop_action` answers XdndStatus. Pick X11 over Wayland in `clipboard.rs` (and drop winit's file drops for windows the worker serves) when `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is unset. Cite Chromium's x11_drag_drop_client.cc (BSD-3) and add a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md entry.

title: Page drags between wubble windows, and an OS drag coming back in
spec: In Chrome, a link, a selection or an HTML draggable dragged from a page in one window and dropped on a page or the tab strip of another window behaves exactly like a drop inside one window. The target page gets the source's full DropData, custom types included, and the operations the source allows. Today `Host::drag_target` (crates/wubble/src/host/drag.rs) only knows the source window (`drag_window`). Outside it, a drag becomes the OS's (Wayland, macOS) or ends at `Over::Elsewhere` (X11, Windows). When the Wayland OS drag re-enters any wubble window, it comes back through `AuxEvent::DropEnter` as a foreign offer. Its data has been re-read through pipes, its custom types are gone, the source's `allowed` ops are gone, and a move of editable text becomes a copy. To build: (1) On X11, Windows and macOS, resolve the pointer's screen position against every window of the process (winit outer positions in `crate::instance`/window registry), with z-order from the last focus order. Hand the drag to the other window's host as `Over::Page`/`Over::Shell`, using `DragPhase::EnterFrom(held)` from the source view's `held_drag()`. The `wubble_core::drag` and `pagedrag` machines get a `window` field on `Over`. (2) On Wayland and macOS, recognise an offer whose source is the process's own running drag (the worker keeps the `WlDataSource` and macOS the session). Treat it as the page drag (EnterFrom(held), the source's ops) instead of an external drop. Then `pagedrag::Input::OsEnded` reports the real drop operation to the source. Pure machine changes go in crates/wubble-core/src/pagedrag.rs with unit tests.

title: An HTML draggable's custom dataTransfer types (and DownloadURL) reach other apps
spec: In Chrome, `dataTransfer.setData('application/x-trello-card', ...)` and other custom types on a draggable go out with the OS drag as Chromium's web custom data: Linux `chromium/x-web-custom-data`, macOS `org.chromium.web-custom-data`, Windows "Chromium Web Custom MIME Data Format", each a base::Pickle of string16 pairs. Another Chromium app (Chrome, Electron, VS Code) then sees the same types. On Windows, `DownloadURL` (mime:name:url) becomes a virtual file. CEF 156's CefDragData has no getter for custom data, so `DragData` (crates/wubble-engine/src/page.rs) and welding's `DragPayload` carry none. Today custom types only survive between wubble views (welding change 54 clones the held DropData). To build without an engine patch: a helper content script (crates/wubble-helper/src, alongside clipboard.js, composed in main.rs `compose` on welding's context-script channel) adds a trusted `dragstart` listener on window in the bubble phase, after page handlers. While still in dragstart, it reads `e.dataTransfer.types` and `getData` for every type other than text/plain, text/uri-list and text/html, caps the total size, and posts them on a new `FrameChannel::Drag`. The engine attaches them to the next `DragData` as `custom: Vec<(String, String)>`. `wubble_core::dnd` gains a pure `web_custom_data_pickle(&[(String,String)]) -> Vec<u8>` (Chromium `ui/base/clipboard/custom_data_helper.cc` format, BSD-3, unit-tested) and adds the platform type to `offers`/`pasteboard`. wl/wayland.rs and wl/macos.rs offer it (X11/Windows once those exist). Agent drags stay home (decisions.md).

title: Drag a finished download to another app
spec:
In Chrome a finished download in the bubble or on chrome://downloads can be dragged out as a file: to the desktop, a file manager, a mail composer or a chat app. wubble's rows cannot be dragged. wubble already starts OS drags of page content: Wayland in crates/wubble/src/wl (wl_data_source with text/uri-list), macOS in wl/macos.rs (AppKit dragging session), with the type table in wubble_core::dnd.

What to build: (1) wubble_core::dnd: a pure `fn file_offer(path) -> Vec<(mime, bytes)>` giving `text/uri-list` (file:// URI, RFC 3986 escaped), `text/plain` (the path) and, on macOS, `public.file-url`, with unit tests. (2) UI: the popover row (kit/overlay/a/a-download-row.slint) and the page row (download-row.slint) report a press-and-move past the drag threshold on a complete, not-removed row as a `drag-out(id, x, y)` callback. Use the existing pointer-threshold logic if the kit has one (tab drag uses wubble_core::tabdrag), else add it to core as a pure helper. (3) Host: start the platform drag with the file offer and the file-type glyph as the drag image, through the same entry point page drags use (host/drag.rs), with the operation copy. Windows stays a stub like the other drags (wl::Null). (4) Dropping back onto wubble's own window is ignored. Linux Wayland and macOS; X11 only if the existing drag path covers it.

title: Windows: drags out of the window and drops in from other apps (OLE)
spec: In Chrome on Windows, links, text, images and files dragged out of a page go to Explorer and other apps, and drops from Explorer come in with every format. In wubble, `crates/wubble/src/wl/mod.rs` `Aux` has a Linux impl (`wayland.rs`) and a macOS one (`macos.rs`); Windows gets `wl::Null` (`host/drag.rs`:776), so `drags_out()` is false and only winit's `DroppedFile` comes in. TODO.md M1 lists "Drag out on Windows (the stub)". To build: `crates/wubble/src/wl/windows.rs`, an `Aux` impl over the `windows` crate. Drag out: a COM `IDataObject` with CF_UNICODETEXT, `UniformResourceLocatorW` + `FileGroupDescriptorW`/`FileContents` for a link (Chromium's `ui/base/dragdrop/os_exchange_data_provider_win.cc`, BSD-3, as the model), CF_HDROP or the virtual-file pair for an image written under the CEF cache (the same as `wl/drag_file.rs`), and `IDropSource` run by `DoDragDrop` on the UI thread from `start_drag`. It reports `AuxEvent::DragEnded(DragOps)`. Drop in: `RegisterDragDrop` on the window's HWND (from raw-window-handle) with an `IDropTarget` that maps formats to `DragData` and posts `DropEnter/DropMove/DropLeave/Dropped` through `wl::deliver`, and `drop_action` sets the effect the page answered. winit's own drag-and-drop on that window has to be turned off (`with_drag_and_drop(false)`, a `WindowAttributesExtWindows` in `wubble-ui/src/window.rs` `attributes`). Copy the shape of `macos.rs`.

title: Agent `drag` carries an HTML draggable drag through the page's drag and drop
spec: TODO line 75. `agent_drag` (crates/wubble/src/host/agent.rs ~2844) presses, glides and releases through pointer events only. A page's HTML `draggable` drag starts CEF's `StartDragging` into the window's own drag loop (`crates/wubble/src/host/drag.rs`, `drag_started`), which the agent cannot drive, so `agent_dragged` cancels it and says so. Fix: when an agent-driven tab starts a page drag (`Routed::Drag` in host/surfaces.rs) while an agent drag is in flight, keep the `DragData` in the agent's pending wait instead of handing it to the OS drag. Then drive the drop inside the same view with CEF's drag-target calls along the glide: `drag_target_drag_enter(data, point, ops)`, then `drag_target_drag_over` per step, then `drag_target_drop` at the end, then `drag_source_ended_at` and `drag_source_system_drag_ended` (welding `drag.rs`; existing `View` methods used by the dnd path). Fence with `Fence::Pointer`, then answer "dragged (HTML drag and drop)". A drop target in another tab or app stays unsupported. Update the `drag` tool text in crates/wubble-mcp/src/tools.rs.

title: Bookmarks: drag reorder with Chrome's drop line between rows
spec: TODO line 159 (and the reorder in line 169). A bookmark dropped onto a folder row lands at its end. Chrome's bookmark manager and bar show a drop line between rows and insert at that position, and reorder by drag. Build: a pure `wubble_core` drop-position helper (like `tabdrag.rs`): given a pointer y over a list of row rects, it returns `Before(i)`, `Into(folder)` (the middle third of a folder row) or `After(last)`, with unit tests. Add a store operation to move or insert a bookmark at an index in a folder (`crates/wubble-store/src/bookmarks.rs`, with a position column if there is none). Drag within the Bookmarks page (`kit/pages/list-row.slint` already composes `DropMark`; show it as a line between rows) and drops from tabs or links onto the page or the sidebar's bookmark rows (crates/wubble/src/host/drag.rs) use it. A drop on a folder row's middle still goes into the folder at its end.

title: Command bar: keyword mode (tab to search) and @tabs/@bookmarks/@history scopes
spec:
In Chrome, typing a keyword and then Tab or Space ('yt', 'w') switches the omnibox into a 'Search YouTube' chip mode. The built-in scopes @tabs, @bookmarks and @history limit results to one source. wubble's rank (crates/wubble-core/src/omnibox.rs) always searches with the default engine across every source.

This depends on engine keywords (feature search-engines-keywords); if that has not landed, build on the ENGINES table with a keyword field. Add a pure parse step `fn scope(query, engines) -> (Scope, &str)`, where Scope is one of Default, Engine(EngineRef) or Only(Kind::OpenTab|History|Bookmark), plus an `Actions` scope for '>' commands. rank takes the scope: an engine scope makes the intent row 'Search <name>' with that engine's template, and an Only scope drops the other candidate lists. Keep the tie-break rules.

In CommandHead (crates/wubble-ui/ui/kit/chrome/command-head.slint), Tab or Space after an exact keyword enters the mode and Backspace on an empty field leaves it. The chip is a kit piece: compose an existing chip or badge in kit/chrome, mark it `// derived:` and add it to docs/fidelity/derived-review.md. The scope lives in the host's command-bar state (one owner) and is passed to bar_rows in crates/wubble/src/bar.rs. When a keyword is typed exactly, a row 'Press Tab to search <name>' is offered, as in Chrome. Unit tests for the scope parse and scoped ranking.

title: Drops on the tab list: on a tab navigates it, files open as tabs, link titles kept
spec: Chrome's tab strip treats a drop on the middle of a tab (`TabStripController::PerformDrop`, `TabDragTarget`) as navigating that tab to the dropped URL, with a down arrow over the tab. A drop between tabs opens a new tab there. Dropped files open as file:// tabs, one per file, in order. In wubble, `pagedrag::shell_drop` (crates/wubble-core/src/pagedrag.rs) maps `Shell::List { index, row }` to `Effect::OpenTab` and ignores `row` (a rest on it only activates the tab). `dropped_text` reads only `link()` or `text()`, so files dropped on the list, the New tab row, the bar or a Space row do nothing. Drops from other apps also lose a link's title: `dnd::plan` (crates/wubble-core/src/dnd.rs) never reads `text/x-moz-url` (url, newline, title) or macOS's `public.url-name`. To build: add `Effect::NavigateTab { tab, url }` for a drop on a row's middle, with the row marked as the drop target (a `DropMarkKind` variant or the existing Box). Add `Payload::files()` and make files produce `OpenTab` for each `file://` URI (`dnd::file_uri`), with the first shown and the rest after it. On the address bar, put the first file's URL in the bar. On the bookmarks page, files are not bookmarks. Read `text/x-moz-url` in the Wayland and X11 plans into `DragData::link_title`. Execute these in `Host::page_drag_effect` (crates/wubble/src/host/drag.rs, using `Command::Navigate`-style model commands). Add unit tests in pagedrag.rs and dnd.rs.

title: Pop-ups: make the allow list work without a click, plus a default and the redirect notice
spec:
Chrome: "Pop-ups and redirects" has a default (Don't allow, or Sites can send) and per-site Allow/Block exceptions. An allowed site opens script pop-ups with no gesture, and a blocked one shows the address bar's blocked-pop-up icon. In wubble, `wubble_core::popup::decide` (crates/wubble-core/src/popup.rs) and the `Permission::Popups` rows in `site.rs` already exist. But Chromium refuses a gesture-less `window.open` in `CanCreateWindow` before the host hears of it, so the no-gesture rows never run and the pill (`popups-blocked` chip in kit/chrome/address-pill.slint) never appears. This is the open TODO item.

Build: when each container's request context comes up (`Profiles::get` in crates/wubble-engine/src/storage.rs / app.rs), call `cef::RequestContext::set_content_setting(None, None, CEF_CONTENT_SETTING_TYPE_POPUPS, CEF_CONTENT_SETTING_VALUE_ALLOW)`. That puts every request through welding's popup path (vendor/welding/src/popup.rs, opened.rs) and lets wubble's table decide. Expose it as `Engine::set_content_setting(container, ...)`. Add the setting `popups.default` (Block|Allow, default Block) to crates/wubble-core/src/settings.rs, under Section::Privacy, and pass it as a new `default: Decision` argument to `popup::decide`. Keep the menu rows `Command::OpenBlockedPopups` / `AllowPopups` in crates/wubble/src/menu.rs, and add a "Manage" row that opens Settings at Sites. Redirects: Blink already blocks gesture-less cross-origin framebusting. When a load is cancelled that way (a console message or OnBeforeBrowse with no gesture), count it in the same pill as a blocked redirect with an "Allow" row that sets `Popups` Allow. Unit-test the new `decide` default rows in wubble-core.

title: Prompt for every permission CEF 156 forwards (protocol handler, window management, file editing, downloads, local network, sensors, ...)
spec:
Chrome prompts for many permission types, and CEF 156 forwards all of them to OnShowPermissionPrompt (include/internal/cef_types.h, cef_permission_request_types_t). welding decodes only 12 bits (vendor/welding/src/permissions.rs `decode`). Every other bit arrives as PermissionKind::Other, and wubble denies it silently (crates/wubble/src/prompt.rs `permission_of` returns None). That rejects these APIs with no prompt: showSaveFilePicker/FileSystemHandle.requestPermission write access (FILE_SYSTEM_ACCESS 1<<24), automatic multiple downloads (MULTIPLE_DOWNLOADS 1<<14), getScreenDetails/window placement (WINDOW_MANAGEMENT 1<<23), camera pan-tilt-zoom (1<<1), Captured Surface Control (1<<3), top-level storage access (1<<5), the legacy quota prompt (DISK_QUOTA 1<<6), local network and loopback access (1<<25..27, Chrome's LNA prompt), sensors (1<<28), web app installation (1<<22), FedCM identity provider and ambient login (1<<10, 1<<29), and AR/VR/hand tracking (1<<0, 1<<9, 1<<21).
Add these as named PermissionKind variants in welding (a `wubble change`, with an entry in WUBBLE_CHANGES.md) and as matching wubble_core::site::Permission variants. Each variant gets a stable `as_str`, an entry in Permission::ALL, and an `ask_text` taken from Chromium's permission_request.cc strings, e.g. "Edit files", "Download multiple files", "Manage windows on all your displays", "Look for and connect to any device on your local network", "Use your motion sensors". Map them in prompt.rs `permission_of`. Keep AR/VR/hand tracking and identity provider explicitly denied, with a comment, because no XR runtime or FedCM UI exists. The unit tests in prompt.rs (`every_engine_kind_maps_or_is_never_prompted`) and site.rs need updating. The Settings Sites list (wubble_core::pages::sites_view) shows the new kinds without further work. No new kit pieces are needed: the existing prompt (kit overlay/a/a-prompt.slint via host/surfaces.rs `permission_view`) shows them.

title: Dangerous and insecure download warnings (Keep / Discard)
spec:
Chrome holds a download it considers dangerous until the user picks Keep or Discard. It uses a file-type policy (chrome/browser/resources/safe_browsing/download_file_types.asciipb, BSD-3: per-extension danger level per platform, e.g. .exe/.msi/.scr on Windows, .dmg/.pkg/.app on macOS, .deb/.rpm/.sh/.desktop/.AppImage on Linux), insecure downloads (an http: file started from an https: page) and downloads started with no user gesture. wubble has none of this: wubble-core/src/download.rs DownloadState has no dangerous state, and host/downloads.rs gives every download its final path at once. Safe Browsing stays out, because it would contact a server.

What to build: (1) Port the policy table as data into a new module, wubble_core::download::danger, with a pure `fn danger(name, url, initiator_url, platform) -> Danger { Safe, DangerousFile, Insecure }` and unit tests. (2) Add `DownloadState::Dangerous(Danger)` plus the events `Keep` and `Discard` to the transition table, and update the exhaustive pair test. (3) In host/downloads.rs `download_event` DownloadRequested: when the file is dangerous, answer CEF with an intermediate path, `Unconfirmed <n>.crdownload`, in the downloads folder, reserve the real name, and keep a `held: Option<PathBuf>` on Inflight. On Finished, go to Dangerous instead of Complete. Keep renames the file to its reserved name and moves to Complete; Discard deletes the file and forgets the entry. (4) Store: a migration in crates/wubble-store/sql for a danger column, read in wubble-store/src/downloads.rs. (5) UI: DownloadStatus.dangerous in model.slint, and a warning line plus Keep and Delete buttons in kit/overlay/a/a-download-row.slint and download-row.slint. This is a derived kit piece and goes on docs/fidelity/derived-review.md. (6) The rows open the popover by themselves, as Chrome's bubble does. All platforms.

title: Autofill entries in the editable-field context menu (manual fallback)
spec: Chrome's right-click on a text or password field offers manual fallbacks: "Passwords" -> "Select password..." (search all saved logins, even when the form was not detected), "Suggest password..." on a password field, and (with addresses and cards) "Fill address"/"Fill payment method". wubble's page context menu (crates/wubble/src/menu.rs, which already knows `menu.editable`) has no autofill entries; the key chip only appears when `autofill::classify` recognised a form. Build: add rows to the editable section of the menu table in crates/wubble/src/menu.rs (data, not code branches): `Select password`, `Suggest a strong password` (password-type field only, needs the field's input type from CEF's context-menu params, `CefContextMenuParams::GetInputFieldType` via welding if not already exposed), and later `Fill address`/`Fill card` when those features land. `Select password` opens the existing `AutofillMenu` popover in a new `Phase::Manual { field }` of `wubble_core::autofill` listing every login for the frame's exact origin first and, under a separator, a search over all logins (filling a login saved for another origin asks for confirmation in the menu, Chrome's cross-domain warning). Filling targets the right-clicked element: the content script (crates/wubble-helper/src/autofill.js) records the last `contextmenu` target id and the host fills through the existing `fill_message`/`Effect::Fill`. Respect `agent::Tainted`/session rules in crates/wubble/src/host/autofill.rs (no manual fill in agent session tabs unless shared). Unit tests for the new phase in autofill.rs.

title: Docked DevTools without the remote debugging port (embedder bridge)
spec: Chrome docks DevTools by default and serves the frontend over an in-process pipe; nothing listens on TCP. In wubble, docking only works while `devtools.remote_port` is set (`wubble_core::devtools::Mode::of`, `settings::DEVTOOLS_REMOTE_PORT`): by default DevTools is detached-only, and the setting's own warning says any local program can then drive every tab. Build a host-owned bridge instead. Load the bundled frontend (`devtools://devtools/bundled/devtools_app.html`, or `inspector.html` from CEF's resources) in the panel view that `crates/wubble/src/host/devtools.rs::open_panel` already opens. Before its scripts run, a document script (`View::set_document_scripts`, `cdp::DocScripts`) defines `window.InspectorFrontendHost` with `sendMessageToBackend`, which calls a `Runtime.addBinding` binding on the frontend view. The host reads `Runtime.bindingCalled` from the panel view's CDP events and forwards each message with `View::cdp`-style raw sends on the inspected tab's DevTools channel (welding `send_devtools_message`). The inspected tab's `on_dev_tools_message` traffic for that session goes back through `View::eval` as `DevToolsAPI.dispatchMessage(...)`. Add an engine API for raw passthrough (`View::devtools_raw_send`, plus a `PageEvent::DevToolsRaw` that a session tag separates from wubble's own `CdpId` replies), so wubble's own calls and the frontend's ids never collide (rewrite ids with an offset). Implement the host methods the frontend needs: `getPreferences`/`setPreference`/`removePreference`, stored as JSON in the profile; `openInNewTab` (the existing `new_tab`); `copyText` (clipboard.rs); `save`/`append` (the save chooser); `bringToFront`; `closeWindow`; `inspectedURLChanged`; `setIsDocked`/`requestSetDockSide`, handed to the dock-sides feature; `loadNetworkResource` through `wubble-engine/src/fetch.rs`. In `wubble_core::devtools`, `Mode::Docked` no longer needs a port: `frontend_url` becomes the bundled URL, and `AskTarget` is only needed for the HTTP path. Keep the port path as a fallback. Unit tests for the id rewriting and the new transition rows go in `wubble-core`.

title: Windows: windowless views on the zero-copy D3D frame path
spec: Chrome renders pages on Windows; wubble cannot. `crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs` `new_producer` under `#[cfg(windows)]` returns "windowless views are not supported on Windows yet", and `crates/wubble-gfx/src/import.rs` `import_device` errors outside Linux and macOS, with `IMPORT_BACKENDS = all()`. The parts below already exist: welding's `windows_cef/` (OnAcceleratedPaint copies CEF's pooled D3D11 texture into a weld-owned shared handle, `NativeFrame` on Windows), `native_frame/dx12.rs` (opens the shared handle on D3D12, `InteropBackend::Dx12`), and the Skia renderer's `wgpu_30_surface/dx12.rs`. To build: (1) wubble-gfx: `IMPORT_BACKENDS = DX12` on Windows, an `import_device` that requests a device with the features dx12 import needs, and the import path for `NativeFrame` D3D textures to `wgpu::Texture`, the same as Linux and macOS; (2) wubble-engine: a `#[cfg(windows)] new_producer` that builds `welding::PlatformCefProducer` with the host `HostWgpuContext` (the signature welding's Windows producer takes); (3) welding `windows_cef/mod.rs`:~810 has no popup frame: add a popup slot and `acquire_native_popup` the way `macos_cef/mod.rs`:508 does (a `wubble change`, listed in WUBBLE_CHANGES.md); (4) go through the view lifecycle (`wubble-engine/src/lifecycle.rs`, hide/show and sleep) and `host/gpu.rs` GpuWatch (sysinfo command lines on Windows) for Windows-only branches. Pacing stays `Pacing::CefTimer` (`wubble_gfx::pacing`). Windows only; check it in CI.

title: wubble.cc: feature section recomposed, readable diagrams and install capsule on phones
spec: TODO lines 25-26. The site in `site/` (plain HTML/CSS/JS, `site/README.md`) shows its feature section as a list: bullets on the left, an image on the right, four times, which leaves empty left columns on wide screens. Recompose it from the owner's design pages (`xuckless/the-wallpaper-project` `src/wubble/pages/`, cloned beside the repo; pull it first). Use alternating or grid feature blocks as the design lays them out, with the same copy (no new sentences: copy is the owner's). Also fix two narrow-screen problems. (1) The inline SVG diagrams' text cannot be read at 360 px: give them a viewBox that scales, larger minimum font sizes under a `@media (max-width: 480px)` rule, or a stacked phone variant of each diagram. (2) The install command is cut off in its capsule: let the capsule scroll sideways (`overflow-x:auto`, `white-space:nowrap`, the copy button pinned) or wrap at the shell separators. Files: `site/index.html`, `site/assets/css/*.css`, the SVGs under `site/assets/`. Keep a 16 px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll at 360 px. Do not deploy: `npx wrangler deploy` is the owner's step.

title: Agent sessions: apply hidden tabs' accessibility updates lazily
spec:
Chrome builds no accessibility tree for a hidden tab unless something reads it. In wubble, with no screen reader running, every tab of an agent session still keeps CEF's tree on, and each tree or location event is parsed and applied at once (`Host::ax_event` in crates/wubble/src/host/ax.rs, `AxValue::from_json` then `PageTree::apply`/`move_nodes`). Ten idle tabs in one session cost 6.6 of the main thread's 8.8 % busy time (TODO Optimization 2a).

To build: in `WebAx` (host/ax.rs), give each tab that is driven only by an agent (`agent_drives(tab) && !self.ax.on`) a queue of raw event strings (`Vec<(String, bool)>`, capped; on overflow, drop the queue and mark the tree for a full re-read). `ax_event` only pushes onto that queue and does no JSON parsing. Replace `ax_tree(&self)` with `ax_tree_mut`/`ax_settle(tab)`, which drains the queue into the `PageTree` the first time a call needs it. Its callers in crates/wubble/src/host/agent.rs (`read_page`, refs, `read_text`, the viewport at ~2396/2511/2562/2583/2885/4657) call it at the start of the call. The navigate wait needs to know that "the new document's tree arrived". Keep that answer cheap: detect a root or document change from the event header without a full parse, or settle the queue only when a waiting call asks. Optional second step: switch CEF's tree off for a session tab that is hidden and that no call has read for N seconds (`View::set_accessibility(false)`), and on again with one fresh full tree on the next call. Unit-test the queue and settle rules as a pure helper (wubble-ax or a small module). Linux and macOS.

title: Command bar: suggestions on open (current URL, most visited, copied link)
spec:
Chrome's omnibox shows suggestions before you type anything: the current page's URL ready to edit, most-visited and recent sites, and 'Link you copied' when the clipboard holds a URL. In wubble, omnibox::rank returns nothing for an empty query (crates/wubble-core/src/omnibox.rs, 'An empty query yields no rows'), so an opened bar is empty.

Add a pure `fn zero_rows(current_url: Option<&str>, clipboard_url: Option<&str>, history: &[HistoryEntry], tabs: &[OpenTab], now_ms) -> Vec<OmniResult>` in omnibox.rs, with frecency from the same history_bonus. It gives:
- the current page (Kind::Search with Target::Url, subtitle 'Current page'), only in BarMode::Navigate
- the clipboard link (a new subtitle 'Link you copied'). Read the clipboard only when the bar opens and only for text that classify() makes a Url.
- up to six most-visited history entries, without the current one.

Call it from bar_rows in crates/wubble/src/bar.rs when the query is blank. The host reads the clipboard once per open through crates/wubble/src/clipboard.rs, and never in agent-session tabs (they have their own clipboard). In Navigate mode the field opens filled with the current URL and selected (take-focus already selects all), as in Chrome. The start page capsule (kit/pages/start.slint) uses the same rows. Unit tests for ordering and dedupe.

title: Wayland: page clipboard carries HTML, images, files and web custom formats
spec: Chrome on Wayland copies a selection as text/plain and text/html. It copies images (Copy image, `navigator.clipboard.write` with image/png) and "web " custom formats, and pastes HTML, images (a screenshot into Gmail or Docs) and copied files (text/uri-list, x-special/gnome-copied-files) as `paste` events with `clipboardData.files`. In wubble the pages' clipboard on Wayland goes through crates/wubble-helper/src/clipboard.js and `PageEvent::Clipboard`/`ClipboardRequest` (crates/wubble-engine/src/page.rs) to the worker in crates/wubble/src/wl/wayland.rs. All of it is text only: `TEXT_TYPES`, `send_selection` refuses other types, and paste is one `insertText`. Images go through `shot_io`'s arboard. TODO.md lists "non-text page clipboard formats; custom MIME to other apps" and "Page copy buttons carry text only". To build: extend the bridge protocol to carry a typed item list. clipboard.js captures `setData` for text/html and custom types on trusted copy/cut, and wraps `navigator.clipboard.write`/`read` (ClipboardItem blobs as base64, capped). The worker stores a multi-type `CopyPasteSource` (text, text/html, image/png, `chromium/x-web-custom-data` from the pickle helper in `wubble_core::dnd`) and on load reads the best types. On paste, clipboard.js dispatches a `paste` event whose DataTransfer holds the HTML and any `File`s (image bytes, or file paths read through the host as Chrome reads them). Unless the page cancels it, the HTML goes in with `insertHTML` (Paste) or plain text goes in (Paste as plain text, cef_id::PASTE_MATCH_STYLE). Move Copy Image onto this path on Wayland so one owner sets the selection. Pure type and priority tables go in wubble-core with tests.

title: Containers: create, rename, delete, and assign from the UI
spec:
wubble's containers are Firefox-style cookie jars (decision "Containers" and "Web storage per container" in docs/decisions.md). `wubble_core::model` already has `Command::NewContainer`, `DeleteContainer`, `SetSpaceContainer` and `ReopenInContainer` (crates/wubble-core/src/model.rs:186-200), and `Engine::forget_container` deletes a container's storage. But only agent sessions and the media smoke call them, so no user can make one (TODO "No way to create, rename or delete a container").

Build:
- Add `Command::RenameContainer { id, name }` to model.rs. Names are trimmed, non-empty and unique case-insensitively, and Default cannot be renamed or deleted. Agent containers are never listed or editable. Write unit tests in model/tests.rs.
- Add a Settings section "Containers" in crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/settings.slint, made only from kit components: a ListEditor with the columns Name, Used by (the Spaces that use it), and adds/rename/remove. Delete asks first through the existing dialog-sheet ("Delete Work? Its cookies, site data and cache are deleted"). Spaces that used it fall back to Default, which model.rs already does.
- Add a Space menu row "Container ▸" listing containers plus "New container…" (crates/wubble-core/src/spacemenu.rs), dispatching SetSpaceContainer.
- Add a tab menu row "Reopen in container ▸" (crates/wubble-core/src/tabmenu.rs) that dispatches ReopenInContainer.
- Wire it in crates/wubble/src/host/settings.rs and menu.rs. Persist through crates/wubble/src/persist.rs, which already stores containers.
- The routing rules' Container column (`routing.rules`) can then name user containers.

title: getDisplayMedia: ask to share the screen, then show a sharing bar with Stop
spec:
In Chrome, getDisplayMedia opens a picker, and while capture runs a bar says "<site> is sharing your screen" with Stop sharing and Hide. In wubble, welding decodes the desktop bits (DesktopAudioCapture, DesktopVideoCapture from decode_media), but prompt.rs `permission_of` maps both to None, so every getDisplayMedia is denied. CEF's media_access_query.cc grants the full primary screen (or the id the page asked for), plus "loopback" system audio when desktop audio is requested. On Linux Wayland, Chromium's PipeWire capturer shows the desktop portal's own source picker after the grant.
Build: (1) Add Permission::ScreenCapture to wubble_core::site, with ask_text "See your screen" (Chromium's string) and an optional system-audio line. Never remember an Allow for it: Chrome asks every time, so the prompt shows no remember toggle for this kind. (2) Map DesktopVideoCapture/DesktopAudioCapture to it in prompt.rs. (3) Start a sharing indicator from the grant. It ends when the page's track stops: extend wubble-helper/src/probes.js, which already reports `capture`, to say `display` separately. It also ends when the tab closes or navigates. The indicator is a kit notice in the pane (overlay/a/a-capsule-bar.slint or a-toast.slint as a derived piece, listed on docs/fidelity/derived-review.md) reading "<site> is sharing your screen", with a "Stop sharing" button and a "Hide" button. Stop runs a page script through View::eval that stops every live display track (the probe keeps a WeakRef list of MediaStreamTracks with displaySurface settings). (4) Agent tabs keep denying, as decided.

title: Automatic (multiple) downloads site permission
spec:
When a page starts a second download with no gesture, Chrome's DownloadRequestLimiter asks "This site is trying to download multiple files" (Allow / Block). The answer is remembered per site, and Site settings has an "Automatic downloads" row. In CEF 156 this arrives as CEF_PERMISSION_TYPE_MULTIPLE_DOWNLOADS (1 << 14) on OnShowPermissionPrompt. In wubble the bit is broken today: vendor/welding/src/permissions.rs does not name it, so it decodes to PermissionKind::Other(16384), and wubble_core::site::Permission denies every request naming an unknown kind. A site's second automatic download is therefore always refused, silently. Separately, welding's `can_download` (vendor/welding/src/handlers.rs ~1081) ignores its url argument.

What to build: (1) In welding, mark the changes `wubble change` and list them in WUBBLE_CHANGES.md. Add MULTIPLE_DOWNLOADS = 1 << 14 and `PermissionKind::MultipleDownloads`, with a decode test. Pass the url and the browser id from can_download through a host hook (a `CanDownload` question answered synchronously from a host-set table), so a per-site Block takes effect before anything starts. (2) In wubble-core/src/site.rs, add `Permission::AutomaticDownloads` (stored name "automatic-downloads") to ALL, with the prompt wording "Download multiple files" and tests. (3) In crates/wubble-engine/src/page.rs, map the new kind in the engine permission mapping. In the host's permission routing, use the existing permission prompt (components/permission-prompt.slint). (4) Add the row to Settings' Sites list, where it can be revoked like the others. (5) Agent-driven tabs keep refusing, as today. All platforms.

title: Passwords: export to CSV
spec: Chrome's Password Manager exports all saved passwords to a CSV with the header `name,url,username,password,note` after OS re-authentication, warning that the file is unencrypted. wubble only imports (`VaultCommand::ImportCsv`, crates/wubble-vault/src/command.rs; parser in crates/wubble-vault/src/import.rs). Build: a pure `wubble_vault::export::to_csv(rows: &[(Meta, username, password, note)]) -> Zeroizing<String>` writing Chromium's exact format (name = host without scheme, url = origin + "/", RFC 4180 quoting, CRLF as Chromium's `password_csv_writer.cc`, BSD-3, credited in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md); a round-trip test through `parse_csv`. `VaultCommand::ExportCsv(PathBuf)` run on the store thread (crates/wubble/src/persist.rs `vault_command`): decrypt every readable row, write with 0600 permissions (create_new, then rename), zeroize buffers, answer `VaultAnswer::Exported(count)`; unreadable rows are listed as skipped. UI: an "Export" ghost button beside "Import CSV" in `PasswordsPage` (crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/pages.slint), a confirm sheet (existing `dialog-sheet.slint`/kit Sheet) saying the file is not encrypted, then the save dialog via `crate::chooser` with `Pick::Save` (as `passwords_import_requested` in crates/wubble/src/host/pages.rs does for open), default name `wubble Passwords.csv`. Gate it behind the OS re-auth from feature `pw-os-reauth` when that exists (call through one trait so this works without it). Linux, macOS, Windows.

title: DevTools dock positions: right, bottom, left, undocked
spec: Chrome's DevTools menu (the three-dot menu, then Dock side) offers dock to right, bottom, left, or undock into a separate window. It remembers the choice per profile, and Ctrl+Shift+D cycles through the positions. wubble docks only at the right edge (`host/devtools.rs`: the `PANEL_TAB` pane, with the `SourceSeam` width from `wubble_core::split::SourceSeam`). Detached means CEF's own native window (`View::open_devtools_at`), which is not a wubble window. TODO M4 lists the bottom dock as needing vertical pane rects. To build: (1) In `wubble-core`, add a `DockSide` enum {Right, Bottom, Left, Undocked} to `devtools::Dock::Open { tab, side }`, and add `DockEvent::SetSide(DockSide)` and `CycleSide` with pure transitions and tests. Persist the side as a hidden setting `devtools.dock_side` (`settings.rs`, `Section::Hidden`). (2) Pane geometry: extend `crates/wubble/src/panes.rs` and `host/panes.rs::pane_layout`/`layout_panes` so the panel can take a horizontal strip at the bottom, with a height seam. `SourceSeam` gets an axis, or a second seam instance owned by `Docked`. (3) Undocked: open a wubble window of a new `WindowKind::DevTools` (`wubble_core::window`) that shows only the panel view, so it works on Wayland and composes with the shell. Its close sends `DockEvent::PanelClosed`. CEF's native window stays only for the no-bridge fallback. (4) The frontend's `requestSetDockSide`/`setIsDocked` (from devtools-pipe-bridge) drive `SetSide`, and the frontend is told the current side through `DevToolsAPI.setDockSide`. (5) Add an `Action::DevToolsCycleDock` with the chord Ctrl+Shift+D (Cmd+Shift+D on Mac) in `keys.rs`, PageFirst, active only while the panel has focus. UI: any new seam handle comes from kit components. Shoot the bottom dock and the undocked window with `--shot`.

title: Windows: agent app config paths and the MCP manifest dir
spec: TODO.md MCP section: "Windows: the agent apps' paths (`agent::harness` lists Linux and macOS only) and the manifest's runtime dir." `crates/wubble-core/src/agent/harness.rs` has `Os::Windows` but every `files`/`detect` table lists only `(Os::Linux, ...)` and `(Os::Mac, ...)` (`LM` at :80). Add the Windows entries per harness, relative to the user profile (`%USERPROFILE%`) or to `%APPDATA%`. Examples: Claude Desktop `AppData/Roaming/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`; VS Code `AppData/Roaming/Code/User/mcp.json`; Claude Code `~/.claude.json`; Codex `~/.codex/config.toml`; Gemini `~/.gemini/settings.json`; opencode `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`; Cursor `~/.cursor/mcp.json`; Windsurf `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`. Check each against the app's own docs before adding it. The harness takes a home path today: if an entry needs `%APPDATA%`, give `Os::Windows` entries a base (Home or AppData) and pass both from the edge (`crates/wubble/src/mcp.rs` or wherever `detected`/`file` are called). Manifest: `instance::private_root` already gives `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on Windows. Check that the manifest writer (`agent/manifest.rs` and its caller) creates `<LOCALAPPDATA>/wubble/mcp/`, sets an owner-only ACL there instead of the Unix 0700 mode, and that the relay (`wubble mcp`, `mcp::hosting_browsers`) reads it there. Unit tests in harness.rs for the Windows rows, as the existing Linux and macOS ones do.

title: Undo close tab and Mod+Shift+T bring back the split and record the tab's navigation entries
spec: TODO line 38. Today `wubble_core::closed` (`Closed { url, closed_at_ms, space, place }`) and the store's `ClosedTab` (`crates/wubble-store/src/closed.rs`: url, title, container, space) restore only the URL. Chrome's TabRestoreService restores the tab's place, its group and its navigation stack. Embedder half: (1) Split. When a tab that sat in a split (`wubble_core::split`) closes, record its partner tab and its side/ratio in `Closed` (an optional `split: Option<SplitPlace>`), keep it in the store row (a new nullable column with a migration in wubble-store), and on `Host::reopen_closed` (crates/wubble/src/host.rs ~2142) re-form the split with the partner if it is still open; else open as a plain tab. Do the same for a whole split pair closed together (Chrome restores a window's tabs together). (2) Navigation entries. On close, collect the view's entries through CEF `BrowserHost::get_navigation_entries` (a `NavigationEntryVisitor` in crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs; URL, title, current index) and keep them in a new `closed_entries` table keyed by the closed row. Show them in the History page's recently-closed rows and the reopen menu as a tooltip/second line (for example "and 4 earlier pages"). Actually rebuilding the back/forward stack needs the engine patch (feature `nav-history-restore-patch`); until then the reopened tab loads the current entry only. Tests stay out; transition logic stays in `closed::transition`.

title: Content-driven frame rate in wubble_gfx::pacing
spec:
Chrome paints a page only when it has new content and never more than once per display refresh. A still page sends no frames, a video paints at its own rate, and input or animation paint at vsync. In wubble, CEF's rate is fixed at the display's refresh (`pacing::view_frame_rate`, set by `View::set_frame_rate` in crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs:876 from host.rs:1136/3641). Under `Pacing::Shell`, the begin-frame driver (`BeginFrames`, `transition`) sends a frame on every vsync until the page has left 4 unanswered (TODO Optimization 1b and "Content-driven frame rate").

To build: a pure lifecycle in crates/wubble-gfx/src/pacing.rs, `enum ContentRate { Still, Video { fps }, Interactive { until } }`, with `fn content_transition(state, ContentEvent) -> (state, Vec<RateEffect>)`. The events are FrameArrived { damage share, at }, Input, ShellMotion, VideoPlaying { fps }, VideoStopped and Tick(now). The effects are SetRate(u32) for CEF's timer, or Hold/Resume begin frames for Shell pacing. Video fps comes from a page script that reports `requestVideoFrameCallback` intervals. Add it to the existing media probe in crates/wubble/src/host/media.rs or videos.rs, through `View::eval` or the helper channel. Interactive lasts for a short window after input or shell motion and then falls back to whatever the content shows. Still drops CEF's timer to 1 fps (CEF's minimum) or stops sending begin frames. The host also presents at most one page frame per refresh: when several arrive between renders, only the newest is shown. Wire it per view next to the existing `view_frame_rate` calls in host.rs, and keep `--measure` counters for each state. Unit tests for the transition. All platforms.

title: Address field context menu: Paste and go, Paste and search, copy and edit rows
spec:
Right-clicking Chrome's omnibox gives Undo, Cut, Copy, Paste, 'Paste and go to <url>' or 'Paste and search for "text"', Delete, Select all, and 'Always show full URLs'. In wubble, the command bar field (kit/chrome/command-head.slint) and the address pill (kit/chrome/address-pill.slint) have no menu. Chrome's paste-and-go is missing entirely, and Shift+Insert paste in shell fields is an open TODO.

Add a shell menu for the command field and the pill, built as Menu::Shell entries in crates/wubble/src/menu.rs, like the tab row menu:
- one table of rows
- the paste row's label from classify() over the clipboard text (crates/wubble/src/clipboard.rs): 'Paste and go to <elided url>' for Intent::Url, 'Paste and search for "…"' for Search, disabled when the clipboard is empty
- choosing it runs bar.rs target_command in the bar's mode

The pill's menu adds Copy address (Action::CopyUrl), Edit address (open the bar filled) and Paste and go. Add Action::PasteAndGo to action.rs (FIXED table and PALETTE) so the command bar and keymap can reach it; Chrome has no default chord, so leave it unbound. Add a setting `ui.full_urls`, off by default. When on, the pill shows scheme and full path instead of wubble_core::chrome::address_parts' host and path; feed it from shell.rs. Shift+Insert pastes in CommandHead's key-pressed. Unit tests for the menu labels in menu.rs.

title: Context menu: the missing link, selection, page and frame rows
spec: Chrome's `RenderViewContextMenu` has rows that wubble's `ROWS` (crates/wubble/src/menu.rs) lacks. Link: "Open link in new window" (now possible: `Action::NewWindow` and `Command::MoveToWindow` exist; the comment above `ROWS` saying one window is stale), "Open link in split view" (wubble has split: `Command::SplitWith`), an "Open link in Glance" equivalent (`ModelCommand::OpenGlance`), and "Copy link text". Selection: "Copy link to highlight", which puts a `#:~:text=` URL on the clipboard, built as Chromium's `shared_highlighting` text-fragment generator does (port the generator to a helper page script, BSD-3, run with `View::run_script_in` in `ContextMenu::frame`), plus a search row for a selected URL that offers "Go to <url>". Frame (when `frame_url` is non-empty and differs from `page_url`): "Reload frame" (script `location.reload()` in the frame) and "View frame source" (view-source: of frame_url via the existing `Action::ViewSource` path, parameterised by URL). Editable: "Emoji" on macOS (`orderFrontCharacterPalette:`) and Windows (the Win+. panel through `CoreInputView`/SendInput), plus "Writing direction" on macOS. Keep the Chromium group order, with dividers from the `row!` group numbers. Add `Command` variants as needed and execute them where the host runs `menu::Command` (crates/wubble/src/host). Unit-test each row's predicate in menu.rs's tests as the existing ones do.

title: Routing rules survive Space/container renames and show broken rules
spec:
Open TODO under Privacy and containers. `routing.rules` (crates/wubble-core/src/routing.rs, Settings ListEditor) names Spaces and containers by display name. Renaming or deleting one silently turns the rule off. Space names are not unique, and a name containing `,` or `->` cannot be written in a rule.

Build:
- Store rules by id (SpaceId and ContainerId) and keep names only for display. Change the serialized form in settings.rs (kind List) to `pattern -> space:<id> [container:<id>]`. Add a migration from the old name form that resolves names once at load and keeps the original text for rows it cannot resolve.
- Add a pure `routing::resolve(rules, model) -> Vec<RuleState>` with the states Active, SpaceGone and ContainerGone. The Settings list shows a broken rule with a mark and the text "Space deleted" (a kit ListEditor row state; if no kit piece fits, a derived piece goes on docs/fidelity/derived-review.md).
- Make Space names unique: `model::Command::RenameSpace` / NewSpace append " 2" etc., like Chrome profile names.
- Change the row label to say that typed addresses and page links are not routed.
- Write unit tests in routing.rs and model tests.

title: Camera and microphone in-use indicators on the tab and address pill
spec:
Chrome shows a red recording dot on a tab that is using the camera or microphone, plus a camera or mic icon in the omnibox. Its bubble says "This page is accessing your camera" and offers to keep allowing or stop. wubble records capture only for the sleep policy (wubble_core::busy Reason::Capture, from wubble-helper/src/probes.js) and shows nothing.
Build: (1) Implement CefDisplayHandler::OnMediaAccessChange(has_video_access, has_audio_access) in welding's three cef_backed.rs display handlers (vendor/welding/src/{linux,macos,windows}_cef/cef_backed.rs, next to on_fullscreen_mode_change). It becomes a new NavigationEvent::MediaAccessChanged { video, audio } (a `wubble change`), which wubble-engine/src/page.rs turns into PageEvent::MediaAccess { camera, microphone }. (2) Keep the state on the tab in wubble-core (one field beside audible/muted in tab.rs), with a pure update and unit tests. (3) Show it in the tab row's indicator slot (kit/chrome/tab-row.slint, as the audible mark is drawn) and as a pill glyph (kit/chrome/address-pill.slint). The design set has no camera or mic glyph (kit/gen/icons.slint), so the glyphs are derived and go on the owner's sheet. (4) Clicking the pill glyph opens a kit popover (overlay/a/a-popover.slint + a-menu-list.slint): "This page is using your camera/microphone", "Always allow" or "Stop", and "Manage". Stop forgets the decision and runs a page script that stops the live tracks. Manage opens Settings Sites. (5) Agent-driven tabs show the same mark.

title: Resume interrupted downloads after a restart
spec:
Chrome keeps an interrupted download's partial file and its validators: ETag, Last-Modified, received bytes and hash state, in the History DB. After a restart it resumes from there through DownloadManager::CreateDownloadItem. wubble cannot do this. wubble_core::download::lost_all fails every active entry at start ("Failed: Interrupted. Retry starts over"), and Retry restarts from zero through View::start_download. CEF 156 exposes neither the validators nor a way to recreate an item from history.

What to build: (1) A patch, patches/chromium/50-cef-download-history.patch. In libcef's download manager delegate, export a marker symbol `cef_wubble_download_resume_v1` with two C entry points. One reads an item's etag, last_modified, the intermediate (.crdownload) path and the received bytes. The other creates and resumes an item from those fields, through DownloadManager::CreateDownloadItem, then DownloadItem::Resume, routed to the view's DownloadHandler. Follow the header and marker style of 40-cef-touchpad-pinch.patch and list the patch in patches/README.md. (2) Engine: a new crates/wubble-engine/src/download_resume.rs that finds the marker at run time, as ext_api.rs does. On a stock CEF it returns None and today's behaviour stays. (3) Store: add columns for etag, last_modified, partial path and mime in a new migration under crates/wubble-store/sql, filled from the patched item on each Interrupted or Paused save. (4) Core: replace the blanket `lost_all` with `restored(entry, can_resume) -> DownloadState`. An entry with validators and a partial file becomes Interrupted, and Resume can continue it. Without them it stays Failed. Write unit tests. (5) Host: the Resume of a restored entry calls the engine's resume in a live view of the entry's container. The patch cannot be built now; write it so that it applies to CEF 156.0.30. Linux first.

title: Password Checkup: weak and reused passwords, local; compromised behind an off-by-default setting
spec: Chrome's Password Checkup lists compromised, reused and weak passwords with a "Change password" link per site. wubble has nothing of it. Build: (1) a pure module `wubble_vault::check` (or wubble-core if kept free of crypto): `weak(password) -> bool` using the zxcvbn crate (MIT; Chrome uses zxcvbn, score < 2 is weak), `reused(rows) -> groups` by comparing SHA-256 of passwords in memory only, never stored; results as `CheckReport { weak: Vec<RecordId>, reused: Vec<Vec<RecordId>>, compromised: Option<Vec<RecordId>> }`, unit-tested. (2) `VaultCommand::Check` on the store thread decrypts, computes, zeroizes. (3) Compromised: Chrome asks Google; wubble instead may query the Pwned Passwords k-anonymity range API (only the first 5 hex chars of SHA-1 leave the machine, response padding on) through the existing `ureq` dependency, ONLY when a new setting `passwords.check_compromised` (crates/wubble-core/src/settings.rs, Section::Privacy, default false) is on, run on a worker thread, results cached in memory for the session. (4) UI: a "Check passwords" row on `PasswordsPage` (crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/pages.slint) opening a list section with three groups (kit ListCard/ListRow/ListNote), each row with Edit and "Change password" which opens `https://<origin>/.well-known/change-password` (Chrome's change-password URL) in a new tab; an issue count on the page header. Host wiring in crates/wubble/src/host/pages.rs `Passwords` (new `Then::Check`). Re-run on unlock and after edits. All platforms.

title: Inspect-at-point, Console and element picker in the docked panel
spec: In Chrome, the context menu's Inspect opens DevTools docked with the node under the pointer selected. Ctrl+Shift+J opens the Console, and Ctrl+Shift+C opens Elements in element-picker mode. In wubble, `DockEvent::InspectAt` always closes the docked panel and opens CEF's detached window (`wubble_core::devtools::transition`, comment "native-window only"; TODO M4 "Inspect-at-point in the docked panel"). There is also no Console or picker chord (`keys.rs` binds only F12, Ctrl+Shift+I and Cmd+Alt+I to `Action::DevTools`). To build, on top of devtools-pipe-bridge: (1) `InspectAt(tab, point)` opens or keeps the docked panel and emits a new `DockEffect::RevealAt { tab, point }`. (2) The host executes it on the inspected tab's CDP: `DOM.enable` if needed, then `DOM.getNodeForLocation {x, y, includeUserAgentShadowDOM: false}` → `backendNodeId`. The id goes into the frontend's message stream as the event `Overlay.inspectNodeRequested {backendNodeId}`, through the bridge's dispatch, which makes the frontend reveal the node in Elements. A frame's point needs `Page.getFrameTree` and the frame's offset; use the frame id that the context menu already carries (`frame_id`, welding change 42).
