(3) Add `Action::DevToolsConsole` (Ctrl+Shift+J, Cmd+Alt+J) and `Action::DevToolsInspectElement` (Ctrl+Shift+C, Cmd+Alt+C) in `action.rs`/`keys.rs`, with new `DockEvent::Open(tab, Panel)` rows. On open, the host evaluates `DevToolsAPI.showPanel('console')` or `DevToolsAPI.enterInspectElementMode()` in the frontend view. (4) A press of Inspect while a panel is open for another tab switches the panel to that tab. Add pure tests in `wubble-core/src/devtools.rs`, and update the existing test that expects `OpenDetached` for `InspectAt` in docked mode.

title: Windows taskbar and window integration: AppUserModelID, jump list, snap layouts
spec: Chrome on Windows sets an explicit AppUserModelID, so its windows group under the pinned icon and toasts carry its name. Its jump list has Tasks (New window) and recently closed or most visited pages. Hovering its maximize button opens Windows 11 snap layouts. wubble has none of this: the window is frameless on Windows (`wubble-ui/src/window.rs` `NATIVE_FRAME` is macOS only), the shell draws its own buttons, and nothing names an AUMID. To build, in `crates/wubble/src/` behind `#[cfg(windows)]`, one module (`win_shell.rs`): (1) `SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID("wubble.Browser")` in `main` before any window, the same id the installer's shortcut carries (MSI feature); (2) a jump list via `ICustomDestinationList` with a Tasks category ("New window", run as `wubble --new-window`, the switches feature) and a "Recently closed" category from `wubble_core::closed`, rebuilt when that list changes, not per frame. The data is a pure fn in core (`jumplist(&Closed) -> Vec<Item>`) with unit tests; (3) snap layouts: subclass the HWND (`SetWindowSubclass`) and answer `WM_NCHITTEST` with `HTMAXBUTTON` over the shell's maximize button rect. The rect comes from the Slint window-frame component (`ui/components/window-frame.slint`) through a property the host reads, the same way the edge resize zones reach `window.rs`. Nothing is drawn outside the kit.

title: Engine patch: restore a tab's back/forward stack (reopen closed tab, session restore)
spec: TODO line 38, the half that cannot be done in the embedder. CEF 156 has no API to give a new browser a list of navigation entries. Chrome restores the stack through `content::NavigationController::Restore` and `NavigationEntryRestoreContext`. Write `patches/chromium/50-cef-restore-entries.patch` (CEF side, under `#if BUILDFLAG(ENABLE_CEF)`, header What/Why/Applies in, `wubble change` marks; follow `patches/README.md`). Export a C function in the style of `cef_wubble_ext_v1`, for example `cef_wubble_restore_v1(cef_browser_t*, const cef_string_t* urls, const cef_string_t* titles, size_t count, int current)`. It builds `NavigationEntry` objects with `NavigationController::CreateNavigationEntry`, calls `Restore(current, RestoreType::kRestored, &entries)`, then `LoadIfNecessary`. Add a marker like patch 40's. On the wubble side, look the symbol up at run time in `crates/wubble-engine/src/ext_api.rs` (stock CEF lacks it and wubble falls back to loading the URL). Add `View::restore_entries(entries, current)`, and use it from `Host::reopen_closed` and from session restore (`crates/wubble/src/persist.rs`, wubble-store `session.rs`) with the entries recorded by `undo-close-split-entries`. Do not build the engine (there are no Chromium rebuilds now): write the patch and the guarded embedder code so a later engine build picks it up.

title: macOS: opaque window where the shell covers it
spec:
Chrome's macOS windows are opaque, so WindowServer does not blend them. wubble's root window has `background: transparent` (crates/wubble-ui/ui/app.slint:99), so its CAMetalLayer is not opaque. On a 5K display WindowServer then blends the whole window on every present (TODO Optimization 1c and the macOS transparency item). On macOS the window keeps AppKit's frame (`native-frame`, window.rs `NATIVE_FRAME`) and the shell covers every pixel, so nothing needs the transparency.

To build: (1) In app.slint, bind the window background to an opaque ground when `native-frame` is true. To obey the kit rules, the shell file must not hold the token: add a kit property (for example a `WindowGround` value in kit/derived.slint, recorded in docs/fidelity/derived-review.md) that resolves to the scene's ground colour, and keep it transparent elsewhere. (2) In the macOS window setup (crates/wubble/src/host/window.rs, plus crates/wubble-engine/src/mac_app.rs or a new mac helper using objc2 via the raw window handle), set `NSWindow.opaque = YES` and `backgroundColor`, and set `CAMetalLayer.opaque = YES` on the content view's layer. Metal advertises only `PostMultiplied` alpha, so `composite_alpha_mode` in vendor/i-slint-renderer-skia/wgpu_30_surface.rs finds no Opaque mode; making the layer itself opaque is what counts. If the vendored surface needs any change, mark it `wubble change` in WUBBLE_CHANGES.md. (3) Keep the scene's backdrop texture opaque under the sidebar so nothing reads alpha. Put it behind a flag such as `WUBBLE_MAC_OPAQUE=0` for A/B runs. macOS only.

title: Back and forward history list (long press or right-click), middle-click to new tab
spec:
In Chrome, holding or right-clicking Back or Forward opens a list of up to 15 history entries with favicons and titles, plus 'Show full history'. Picking one jumps there, and Ctrl, Cmd or middle click opens it in a new tab. A middle click on Back, Forward or Reload opens that page in a new tab. wubble's NavButtons (crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/nav-buttons.slint) has only clicked, and there is no navigation-entry access (CEF's GetNavigationEntries is not wrapped).

Engine: use the existing CDP channel (crates/wubble-engine/src/cdp.rs, View::cdp). Page.getNavigationHistory returns {currentIndex, entries[id,url,title]} and Page.navigateToHistoryEntry(entryId) jumps. Add View::navigation_history() and View::go_to_entry(id), with the reply mapped in page.rs to a PageEvent::NavigationHistory.

Core: a pure fn in wubble-core (new navlist.rs) splits the entries into back and forward lists, nearest first, capped at 15, each titled by title or URL. It has unit tests.

UI:
- NavButtons gets `pressed-long(id)` and `context(id)` callbacks (a kit hold or press motion from kit/motion/press.slint and controls/hold-button.slint for the 500 ms hold) and `middle-clicked(id)`.
- The host opens a Menu::Shell (crates/wubble/src/menu.rs) under the button with favicon rows (host/favicons) and 'Show full history' (Action::OpenHistory).
- A middle or Mod click on a row, or on Back, Forward or Reload, makes Command::NewTab with that entry's URL (a copy, as Chrome; history is not cloned).

The page context menu's Back and Forward rows keep working. Not for agent-session tabs (agent::may_go still guards the navigation).

title: Find bar: match case, survives reload, prefill from selection
spec: Chrome's find bar stays open with its query across reloads and same-tab navigations and searches again after the load. Ctrl+F with text selected fills the bar with the selection, and otherwise with the last query (shared across tabs: `FindBarState` prepopulate text). Enter/Shift+Enter, F3/Shift+F3 and Ctrl+G/Ctrl+Shift+G step. Esc closes and keeps the active match selected. Chrome has no match-case button, but wubble's TODO asks for one ("a match-case toggle in the find bar"), and the engine already supports it (`FindInput::Start { match_case }`, crates/wubble-engine/src/find.rs). Gaps: `surface::FindBar` (crates/wubble/src/surface.rs) has no `match_case`. TODO.md "Find bar closes on reload (Chromium keeps it)": `Surfaces::view_gone` or the load path resets it. No prefill from the selection. `last` is per tab, not global. To build: add `match_case` to `FindBar::Open` and to `FindEffect::Find`, plus a `FindEvent::MatchCase(bool)`. Add a toggle to `components/find-bar.slint` from kit parts (a derived kit piece if none exists, listed on derived-review.md). On a main-frame load commit keep the bar and re-issue `Find` once the load ends (a `FindEvent::Reloaded`). On `FindEvent::Open` read the selection (CEF `GetSelectedText` via `View`, or `ContextMenu`-style script) and use it if non-empty, else the global last query owned by Host. Extend the existing unit tests in surface.rs.

title: Chrome-style Site settings: defaults per permission, per-site detail, add exceptions
spec:
Chrome's chrome://settings/content lists every permission and content type with a default ("Sites can ask" / "Don't allow") and Allowed/Blocked lists. Each site has a page with a dropdown per kind (Ask/Allow/Block), Reset permissions, and Delete data. In wubble, Settings > Sites (crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/settings.slint, about line 1003) shows only a read-only ListEditor of remembered decisions (Site, Permission, Decision) with remove, and there are no defaults or adds.

Build:
- In wubble-core site.rs, add a default per Permission, stored as settings keys `site.default.<as_str>` (Ask|Block, plus Allow for kinds Chrome allows by default), in crates/wubble-core/src/settings.rs. `SitePermissions::decide` takes the defaults (no row → the default; Ask stays Ask).
- Add a pure view model `site::SiteSettingsView` (per container: kinds → default, allowed origins, blocked origins), with unit tests.
- Shell: Sites becomes a list of kinds. Each row opens a sub-panel with the default dropdown and the Allowed/Blocked ListEditors with `adds` enabled (origin input validated by `site::origin_of`). Add a Site detail panel (one origin, container chooser) with a dropdown per kind, "Reset permissions", and "Delete site data" (reuses `ClearData::Site`). Compose only kit components.
- Host: crates/wubble/src/host/settings.rs writes through the store (wubble-store permissions.rs).
- The command bar action "Site settings" (crates/wubble-core/src/action.rs) opens the detail panel for the visible tab's origin.
Depends on permissions-per-container for the container key.

title: Choose which camera and microphone a site gets
spec:
Chrome's camera/mic prompt and Settings → Site settings → Camera/Microphone have a device dropdown. The default device is stored in prefs, and a site gets that device unless it asked for a deviceId. In wubble, CEF's media_access_query.cc picks the requested device id, else the first device, and the prompt (crates/wubble/src/prompt.rs, kit a-prompt.slint) has no device choice.
Build without an engine change: (1) Add a main-world content script channel `media` to wubble-helper/src (registered in main.rs `compose`, with its browser side in wubble-engine page::FrameChannel). It wraps navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia so that, when the constraint names no deviceId, it adds `deviceId: {ideal: <preferred id>}` for audio and video. The preference is pushed from the browser per frame. After a grant it reports enumerateDevices() (labels are visible then) to the browser. (2) Store `media.camera` and `media.microphone` (a device label plus groupId; ids are per-origin salted, so match by label) as SettingDefs in wubble_core::settings, with Select rows in the Settings Sites/Privacy section built from kit settings controls. The list comes from the last enumeration any page reported. (3) Add a device Select to the permission prompt when the request is camera or microphone and devices are known. (4) Unit-test the pure matching (label to device) in wubble-core.

title: Download speed and time remaining in rows
spec:
Chrome's download rows read "2.1 MB/s · 12 MB of 100 MB, 40 secs left". wubble's DownloadEntry::detail (wubble-core/src/download.rs) shows only the amounts, because welding's DownloadProgress event (vendor/welding/src/handlers.rs on_download_updated) drops CefDownloadItem::current_speed.

What to build: (1) welding: add `bytes_per_second: Option<u64>` to NavigationEvent::DownloadProgress from `item.current_speed()`, as a `wubble change` entry. (2) wubble-engine/src/download.rs and page.rs: carry the speed through DownloadInput::Progress and PageEvent::DownloadProgress, and update their tests. (3) wubble-core/src/download.rs: give DownloadEvent::Progress the speed, store `speed: Option<u64>` on DownloadEntry (not persisted; it is cleared when the download leaves Running), and make detail() return Chromium's format: speed, amount, and the time left from (total - received) / speed. Format the time with a pure port of ui::TimeFormat's short remaining strings ("40 secs left", "3 mins left", "2 hours left", from ui/base/l10n/time_format.cc, BSD) in a new `remaining_text(secs)`, with unit tests. Smooth the speed with an exponential moving average, kept in the entry, so the text does not jitter. (4) Media downloads (host/media.rs jobs) report their own rate the same way, from the bytes the writer has written per tick, so both kinds of row read alike. No UI change: the row already shows `detail`. All platforms.

title: Passwords: notes, per-login details and Chromium-style edit
spec: Chrome's password details show site, username, password, a free-text note, and created/last-used info, editable after re-auth; imports and exports carry the note column. wubble's vault rows (crates/wubble-vault/src/record.rs `StoredRecord`, `NewLogin`) have no note, `LoginView` (crates/wubble-core/src/pages.rs) has `created_ms/last_used_ms/times_used` that the page never shows, and the CSV parser drops `note`. Build: migration crates/wubble-store/sql/017_login_notes.sql adding `note_enc BLOB` to `logins` (AEAD with field "note" bound as associated data like username/password in crates/wubble-vault/src/crypto.rs); `NewLogin.note: Zeroizing<String>`; `VaultCommand::Edit` and `Add` gain `note`; `VaultCommand::RevealNote(id)`; crates/wubble-vault/src/import.rs reads Chromium's and Firefox's `note`/`notes` column (Chromium 2023+ export) and `apply` keeps it; crates/wubble-vault/src/store_adapter.rs and store.rs `MemoryStore` updated. UI: the add/edit sheet in `PasswordsPage` (crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/pages.slint) gets a multi-line note field (kit ListField; if no multi-line kit field exists, it is a derived piece for docs/fidelity/derived-review.md) and a details row showing "Saved <date>, last used <date>, used N times" (formatting in wubble-core with tests). Also show multiple logins for one site grouped under one site row with a count, as Chrome groups credentials (pure grouping in `pages::passwords_list`). All platforms.

title: Remote debugging UI: a wubble://inspect targets page
spec: Chrome has chrome://inspect: lists of pages, extensions, service workers, shared workers and other targets, each with inspect/focus/reload/close. It also has "Discover network targets" with a configurable host:port list (Node at localhost:9229 and so on), "Open dedicated DevTools for Node", and a remote-debugging status section. wubble has only the `devtools.remote_port` Settings row (`settings.rs`, `Section::Privacy`, restart) and no page that lists targets. To build: a new `InternalPage::Inspect` (`wubble_core::pages`, url `wubble://inspect`, a palette entry in `action.rs`), drawn only from kit components in `crates/wubble-ui/ui/` (rows like the Task manager's list). Rows come from the model: tabs, with a pure projection in a new `wubble_core::inspect` module. Extension popups, the DevTools panel and extension service workers come from `Target.getTargets` sent over any open view's CDP channel, or over the browser target that `Target.attachToBrowserTarget` gives. Each row has Inspect, which opens DevTools through `dock_event` for tabs, or a detached frontend attached to the target id for workers (the bridge with a flattened `Target.attachToTarget` session), plus Focus and Close. Show the endpoint's state: port set or off, whether it is bound (the loopback connect check that `open_panel` already does), and a warning line. Network targets: a `devtools.network_targets` List setting (default empty). Each entry is polled at `http://host:port/json/list` through `fetch.rs` only while the page is shown and only when the list is non-empty, so nothing is requested by default. Inspect opens the frontend with `?ws=` pointing at that target's webSocketDebuggerUrl. The state machine for polling goes in core, with tests.

title: Windows packaging: MSI, winget manifest and the updater's Windows install
spec: TODO.md M7 "Packaging: ... MSI/winget". Nothing exists for Windows: `scripts/release/` has package-linux.sh and package-macos.sh only, `wubble_core::update::PLATFORMS` is `[linux-x86_64, macos-aarch64, macos-x86_64]`, and `updater/install.rs` `detect` knows `Os::Linux` and `Os::Mac` only. To build: (1) `scripts/release/package-windows.ps1`, which lays out the bundle (bootstrap `wubble.exe` + `wubble.dll` from the sandbox feature, helper, CEF runtime, `release.json`, notices), zips it as `wubble-<V>-windows-x86_64.zip` (the update archive) and builds a per-user MSI with WiX v4 (MIT-licensed tool, a `.wxs` in `scripts/release/windows/`). The MSI installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\wubble\versions\<V>`, makes a Start menu shortcut carrying the AppUserModelID, writes the HKCU default-browser registration keys (default-browser feature), and has an uninstall entry. (2) `scripts/release/windows/winget/` manifests (version, installer, locale) pointing at the GitHub release asset. (3) Updater: `Os::Windows` in `wubble_core::update::install` (`classify_windows` for the `%LOCALAPPDATA%` layout, with unit tests), `windows-x86_64` in `PLATFORMS`/`PLATFORM`, and an `Install` impl in `updater/install.rs`. Windows has no symlinks, so switching versions means a `current.txt` read by a tiny launcher or a shortcut retarget, and a running exe cannot be replaced, so the swap happens at the next launch (as on macOS). (4) A docs/release.md section. Signing uses a cert from the environment only, as on macOS.

title: Wire the thinking orb into the shell: agent mark, activity header, approval sheet
spec: TODO line 40. The orb is ported (`wubble_core::orb`: `Orb`, `Life`, `transition`; GPU painter `wubble_gfx::orb`; per-window stage in `crates/wubble/src/orbs.rs`) but is shown only by the gallery specimen (`kit/specimen/agent-widgets.slint`). Wire it into the places in docs/research/agent-widgets.md section 5: (1) the agent mark on a driven tab's row and on its Space header, 16 px, animated while that session (`wubble_core::agent` Session) has a call in flight, else a still frame; (2) the agent activity page's header, 32 px, while any session runs; (3) the approval sheet's title, 20 px, in the listening preset while the session is `AwaitingApproval`. Each place is a kit component property (an `Image` slot already in `kit/chrome/agent-mark.slint`, the agent sheet and the activity page kit parts): add an `orb` image input to those kit parts (derived, add a line to docs/fidelity/derived-review.md). orbs.rs gains cells keyed by place (tab id, page, sheet), created and dropped as models change, driven by the session state through `LifeEvent`. Only moving orbs redraw (orbs.rs `frame`). Reduced motion shows the still frame. Keep the existing kit lock rules (no drawing in shell .slint files). The owner's go on the proposal is still open; build it so each place can be switched off in one table.

title: Page fullscreen draws the page alone
spec:
In Chrome, fullscreen video is the page's compositor frame alone. In wubble, page fullscreen already hides the sidebar, frame and seam, and the scene does not step (decisions "Page fullscreen", "Scene follows the run state"). Slint still walks the shell's item tree, the scene's textures and over-layer images stay allocated and bound, and each page frame goes through the full render (TODO Optimization 1d).

To build: in crates/wubble-ui/ui/app.slint, put every shell subtree (sidebar, bars, overlays that are not the page's own: find, prompts and video controls stay) behind `if !root.page-fullscreen` conditionals. The shell file only lays out kit components, so no new visuals are needed. Then only the page `Image` and the page-owned surfaces remain. In crates/wubble/src/backdrop.rs, when `get_page_fullscreen()` turns on, release the scene's output and over-layer images (`set_scene`/`set_over_*` to an empty image) and the page pyramid P (`Renderer::set_pages(vec![])` path in crates/wubble-gfx/src/scene/render.rs). Rebuild them when fullscreen ends, the same way a resize does. In host/panes.rs, a fullscreen pane always takes the in-place damage path (`FramePresenter::present_damaged`), so only the video's rect is marked dirty. Count `fullscreen_frames` in `--measure` so it can be compared with Chromium. All platforms.

title: Reload button turns into Stop while loading; reload menu with hard reload and empty cache
spec:
While a page loads, Chrome's reload button turns into an X (Stop), and back into Reload when the load ends. Shift-click or Ctrl-click does a hard reload. With DevTools open, a right-click or long press gives Normal reload, Hard reload and 'Empty cache and hard reload'. wubble has Action::Stop (Escape, Cmd+.), Action::HardReload (ViewOp::HardReload, reload_ignore_cache in crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs) and an `address-loading` property in app.slint, but NavButtons (crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/nav-buttons.slint) always shows Reload.

Add `in property <bool> loading` to NavButtons, bound from the visible tab's loading state (the same source as address-loading in crates/wubble/src/bind.rs). The fourth button's icon, label and id become Glyph.close / 'Stop' / 'stop' while loading, swapped with a kit crossfade (kit/motion/crossfade.slint). If the kit's icon set has no stop glyph, use close and note it in docs/fidelity/derived-review.md. Add a modifiers argument to `action(...)` so the host maps Shift or Mod on reload to hard-reload. The NavButtons button table stays one table.

Add Action::EmptyCacheHardReload (FIXED table and PALETTE). It sends the CDP call Network.clearBrowserCache through View::cdp (crates/wubble-engine/src/cdp.rs), then ViewOp::HardReload. A right-click on the reload button opens a Menu::Shell (crates/wubble/src/menu.rs) with the three rows; the third is shown only when wubble_core::devtools says DevTools is open for that tab. Unit tests in perform.rs for the plans.

title: Zoom indicator and zoom controls like Chrome's omnibox zoom bubble
spec: In Chrome, when a site's zoom differs from the default, a magnifier icon shows in the address bar. Clicking it opens a bubble with the percentage, −, + and Reset. The app menu has a Zoom row (−, percent, +, fullscreen), and Settings > Appearance > Page zoom lists the per-site levels. wubble has per-site zoom (`wubble_core::zoom::ZoomTable`, `SITE_ZOOM`/`ZOOM_DEFAULT` settings, host `user_zoomed` in crates/wubble/src/host/surfaces.rs), a brief toast after Ctrl +/-/0 (components/toast.slint), and a site-zoom list in settings (`settings-site-zoom`). Nothing persistent shows that a page is zoomed, and there is no pointer path to zoom. To build: a `zoomed` percent property for the visible tab (from `PageEvent::ZoomChanged` against the default), shown as a small kit chip in the address pill (a derived kit piece composing existing kit parts, on the derived-review sheet) only when it is not the default. The chip opens a popover with −, the percent, + and Reset, which perform `Action::ZoomOut`/`ZoomIn`/`ZoomReset`. Add a Zoom row to the page menu (`window_page_entries` or the page's own menu in crates/wubble/src/menu.rs). The popover closes on Esc and on outside click as the other popovers do. A pure fn in wubble-core decides whether the chip shows (percent, default), with tests.

title: Non-prompt content settings: JavaScript, images, sound, insecure content, sensors, downloads, JIT
spec:
Chrome has content settings that are not prompts: JavaScript, Images, Sound, Insecure content (mixed script), Motion sensors, Automatic downloads, Protocol handlers, V8 optimizer (JIT), Intrusive ads, and Auto picture-in-picture. Each has a default and per-site exceptions. wubble has none of them, and the `Permission` enum in crates/wubble-core/src/site.rs covers only prompt kinds.

Build:
- Add `site::ContentSetting` in wubble-core: an enum plus a data table of (stored name, label, Chrome default, CEF `cef_content_setting_types_t`). Exceptions are stored per container and origin, in a new store table or in site_permissions with new kind names.
- Engine: add `Engine::set_content_setting(container, origin: Option<&str>, kind, value)` in crates/wubble-engine/src/app.rs. It calls `cef::RequestContext::set_content_setting(requesting_url, top_level_url, type, value)`, which exists in cef 156.6 bindings, on the container's context from `Profiles::get`. Replay the whole table when each context comes up and on every change.
- Sound: if CEF's SOUND setting does not mute, the host mutes the tab's browser (`set_audio_muted`) when its site is blocked. Put that in a pure function in wubble-core media.rs (`muted = user_mute || site_sound_blocked`).
- Insecure content: the Allow value maps to CEF_CONTENT_SETTING_TYPE_MIXEDSCRIPT for the site.
- UI: rows in the site-settings-page lists and the page-info popover.
- Write unit tests for the table, name round-trips and the mute rule.

title: Site permission decisions per container, not per origin
spec:
TODO.md: "Site permission decisions are per origin, not per container (a camera allowed in one container is allowed in all)". The containers decision (docs/decisions.md) says containers share nothing: one CEF request context each, with its own permission store. wubble's own table (wubble_core::site::SitePermissions, a BTreeMap keyed by (origin, Permission)) is global, and crates/wubble/src/prompt.rs `PermissionRequest::verdict` consults it with no container. Chrome profiles keep separate content settings.
Build: (1) Key the table as (container id, origin, kind). Container ids come from wubble_core::space. Make `decide`, `set`, `forget` and `iter` take the container. Unit tests cover isolation and the external-link keys (wubble_core::external::key stays per scheme and site within a container). (2) Carry the tab's container on PermissionRequest; host/surfaces.rs builds it from the tab's Space/container. (3) Persist: add a container column to the site-permission store in crates/wubble/src/persist.rs, migrating existing rows to every existing container. Copying preserves the previous behaviour; the migration and the decision go in the report. Add a persistence test. (4) Settings Sites shows the container beside each row when more than one exists, and filters to the active Space's container by default. (5) Deleting a container drops its rows. The SavePasswords Block rows stay per container too.

title: Open when done, always open this type, open safe files
spec:
Chrome lets a running download be marked "Open when done". On a finished one it offers "Always open files of this type", stored per extension (download.extensions_to_open) and refused for dangerous types. The design's Settings (ref/the-wallpaper-project/src/wubble/pages/settings.tsx, `openSafe`) also has "Open safe files after downloading". wubble opens a file only on a click of Open (host/downloads.rs download_action DownloadAction::Open).

What to build: (1) wubble-core/src/download.rs: an `open_when_done: bool` on DownloadEntry, a pure `fn opens_on_finish(entry, always_types, open_safe) -> bool` (never for a dangerous type, which comes from the danger table if that feature has landed, else from a small built-in list of executable extensions), and a `DownloadEffect::OpenFile` emitted on the Finished transition when it returns true. Write unit tests. (2) Settings: a `downloads.open_types` list setting (Section::Hidden, edited from the row menu) and a `downloads.open_safe` Bool row, default off, in wubble-core/src/settings.rs, with SETTINGS-table tests. (3) Host: run OpenFile with `opener::open`. Persist open_when_done in a store migration, so it survives a restart for a resumed item. (4) UI: DownloadAction gets `open-when-done` and `always-open-type`. A small row menu on the popover's ADownloadRow and the page's DownloadRow lists Open when done (checked), Always open files of this type, Copy link and Show in folder. Compose it from the kit menu (kit/controls/menu.slint) and put it on derived-review.md. All platforms.

title: Passwords page: never-saved sites list and Manage passwords entry points
spec: Chrome lists sites where you chose "Never" in Password Manager settings ("Declined sites and apps") with a remove button, and its autofill dropdown ends with "Manage passwords...". wubble stores "Never" as `Permission::SavePasswords` = `Decision::Block` in `site_permissions` (crates/wubble/src/host/autofill.rs near line 288, crates/wubble-store/src/permissions.rs) and shows it only inside Settings' generic Sites list; the chip menu (`MenuRow` in crates/wubble-core/src/autofill.rs) has only `Login` and `Generate`. Build: (1) a "Never saved" ListCard section on `PasswordsPage` (crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/pages.slint) fed from `site_permissions` rows of `SavePasswords`/Block, each with a Remove action that clears the decision (existing site-permission revoke path), listed even while the vault is locked since origins are not secret; host in crates/wubble/src/host/pages.rs. (2) `MenuRow::Manage` appended to `rows()` (label "Manage passwords") opening `InternalPage::Passwords` with the page's search prefilled with the site, implemented as a new `Effect::OpenManager { origin }` executed in crates/wubble/src/host/autofill.rs. (3) A "Delete all passwords" hold button (kit `KeyedHoldButton`, as `start-over`) as Chrome's "Delete all data". (4) The `wubble://passwords` page accepts a `?q=` site filter from the omnibox. Unit tests for the new menu row and effect in autofill.rs, and for the never-saved list builder in wubble-core/src/pages.rs. Gallery scene for the page with the new section.

title: DevTools for extension popups, service workers and options pages
spec: In Chrome, the extension card offers "Inspect views: service worker, popup.html", and a right-click on the action offers "Inspect popup", which keeps the popup open while DevTools is attached. wubble has neither. The popup is a windowless view (`crates/wubble/src/host/ext_ui.rs::open_popup`, pane `POPUP_TAB`) that closes on an outside press, and the service worker has no view. To build: (1) In the Settings extensions list and the footer popover row, add an "Inspect" item (kit menu rows) for an extension whose `ext_api::available()` is true. (2) Popup: open CEF's detached DevTools on the popup's view (`View::open_devtools_at(None)`), or the bridge's undocked window. While DevTools is attached, the panel lifecycle (`wubble_core::extensions::shell::panel_transition`) gets a `PanelEvent::Pinned` state in which an outside press or Escape does not close the popup, as in Chrome. (3) Service worker: find its target by `Target.getTargets` (type `service_worker`, url `chrome-extension://<id>/`) over a browser-target session (`Target.attachToBrowserTarget` from any view's DevTools channel), then attach the devtools-pipe-bridge frontend with `Target.attachToTarget {flatten: true}` and route by `sessionId`. If CEF refuses the browser target to its page client, fall back to `devtools.remote_port`'s `/json/list` and say so in the row. (4) Options pages are tabs already, so F12 works there. Add pure tests for the Pinned transition in `extensions/shell.rs`.

title: Default browser: status, a Settings row, and registration on Linux, macOS and Windows
spec: Chrome shows "Default browser" in Settings with "Make default" and the current status. wubble has no code for this (TODO.md M7 "Default-browser registration, URL handlers"). The Linux desktop entry (`assets/icons/linux/wubble.desktop`) lists only text/html, xhtml, http and https. To build: (1) `wubble_core::default_browser`: an enum `Status {Unknown, Checking, Default, NotDefault, Unsupported, Failed}` and a pure `transition(state, Event::{Check, MakeDefault, Answered(..)}) -> (state, Vec<Effect::{Probe, Register}>)`, with unit tests. (2) A trait `DefaultBrowser {fn is_default(&self) -> Result<bool>; fn make_default(&self) -> Result<()>}` in `crates/wubble/src/default_browser.rs`, run on a worker thread, with one impl per OS. Linux: `xdg-settings check/set default-web-browser wubble.desktop`, plus `xdg-mime default` for the scheme handlers. Unsupported inside Flatpak (Chrome's flatpak says so too). macOS: compare `NSWorkspace URLForApplicationToOpenURL:` for `https:` against bundle id `dev.wubble.browser`, and set with `setDefaultApplicationAtURL:toOpenURLsWithScheme:completionHandler:` for http and https (macOS shows its own confirmation). Windows: write the HKCU `Software\Clients\StartMenuInternet\wubble` Capabilities, `RegisteredApplications` and a `wubbleHTML`/`wubbleURL` ProgId, then open `ms-settings:defaultapps?registeredAppUser=wubble` (Windows 10+ forbids setting it silently). (3) Settings General row: status text and a "Make default" button, built from kit parts like the Updates group's "Check now" (`ui/components/settings.slint`:604, `UpdatesView`). (4) desktop entry: Chrome's MimeType set (image/*, svg, pdf, webp, xml) and `Actions=new-window;` with `[Desktop Action new-window] Exec=wubble --new-window`. No request leaves the machine.

title: Thinking orb: port the gravity cursor warp
spec: TODO line 42. The web ThinkingOrb has a `gravity` prop (`ThinkingOrb.tsx`, `gravity.ts` in the design repo `xuckless/the-wallpaper-project` src/wubble): it warps the dots toward the pointer through a sprite. wubble's port (`crates/wubble-core/src/orb/*.rs`, painter `crates/wubble-gfx/src/orb.rs`, cells in `crates/wubble/src/orbs.rs`) leaves it out (listed in docs/fidelity/deviations.md). Port it: a pure `gravity` module in wubble-core/orb that takes the pointer position relative to the orb (logical px, or None) and returns each mark's offset, with the design's falloff and constants exactly (put the constants through `tools/fidelity/extract.mjs` into kit_gen if they are design values). Add a `pointer` input to `Orb`/`Life`, so a pointer moving over an orb with gravity on makes `Life` say it moves (it redraws only while the warp changes, then settles). Feed the pointer from the specimen's TouchArea (`kit/specimen/agent-widgets.slint`) through `orbs.rs`. Add unit tests for the pure warp in wubble-core (new core logic needs them under AGENTS.md; they are no performance tests). Remove the deviation line.

title: Scene renders mark only what the scene shows through
spec:
A scene render (ambience, about 8 to 10 per second during video and scroll) currently returns `Damage::Whole` unless only the start page's card changed (crates/wubble-gfx/src/scene/start.rs `Damage`; crates/wubble/src/backdrop.rs `frame` calls `partial::mark_window`). Slint then redraws the whole window, including the page card, which covers the scene.

To build: extend `Damage` with a region variant, for example `Rects(SmallVec<[Rect; 4]>)`, and make `Renderer::before_rendering` (scene/render.rs) compute it. When only the window-glass ambience was rebuilt, the damage is the window's glass surfaces where they do not lie under an opaque page card. Use `pages::by_layer`, `rect_of` and the `PageRect`s already held; the visible scene is the sidebar, the gaps around the card and any transparent pane (split, bowed edge, start). When over-layer glass was redrawn, the damage is those surfaces' rects. Use Whole only for a palette change, a resize, new textures or a backdrop that moved under everything. Add `Damage::and` merging for the new variant. In backdrop.rs, call `partial::mark_rect` once per rect; Slint's dirty region merges them. Pure unit tests in start.rs and pages.rs for which rects come out, and a `partial_render` test in wubble-ui for a scene frame that does not redraw the page. All platforms.

title: History swipe on macOS and Windows touchpads (and X11)
spec:
In Chrome, two fingers sideways go back or forward on every platform. On macOS that is the NSEvent scroll phases (it is the 'Swipe between pages' gesture), with the arrow bubble following the fingers. wubble's history swipe (crates/wubble-core/src/gesture.rs SwipeInput, crates/wubble/src/host/gesture.rs, chip in components/swipe-chip.slint) is fed only from Wayland through crates/wubble/src/wl. host/gesture.rs says 'Nothing reports a history swipe elsewhere yet (macOS's would be winit's PanGesture)'.

macOS: feed SwipeInput from winit's WindowEvent::PanGesture (phase Started, Moved, Ended), or from MouseWheel with TouchPhase and PixelDelta when the delta is mainly horizontal. Respect the system 'Swipe between pages' preference: read NSEvent.isSwipeTrackingFromScrollEventsEnabled through objc2 in a platform impl of one shared trait, alongside os_motion.rs and os_scope.rs. Phases end the gesture as the Wayland path does, and the PageScrolled give-way stays.

Windows and X11: precision touchpads arrive as horizontal MouseWheel PixelDelta with no phases. Add a pure idle-timeout end (no delta for 150 ms counts as release) to gesture.rs's transition as a new SwipeInput::Idle, with the timer driven by the host's tick.

Add unit tests for the idle end and the phase mapping in gesture.rs. Keep it to one path: the platform code turns OS events into SwipeInput only, and the rule stays in wubble-core.

title: Page window.print() opens wubble's print sheet on every platform
spec: In Chrome, `window.print()` (and a print button inside a page) opens the same print preview as Ctrl+P. It fires `beforeprint`/`afterprint` and blocks the script until the dialog closes. wubble's Ctrl+P and menu Print open the sheet (`wubble_core::print::Sheet`, crates/wubble/src/host/print.rs, PrintToPDF plus `lp`), but welding's `print()` errors on Linux ("requires an embedder-owned print handler", vendor/welding/src/linux_cef/mod.rs). No CefPrintHandler is registered, so a page's `window.print()` does nothing on Linux. On macOS and Windows it would reach Chromium's native dialog in a windowless view, which is not wubble's sheet. To build: register a CefPrintHandler in welding (a `wubble change`, listed in WUBBLE_CHANGES.md; cef 156 has `on_print_start`, `on_print_settings`, `on_print_dialog`, `on_print_job`, `get_pdf_paper_size`). On Linux, `on_print_dialog` holds the callback and emits a new `PageEvent::PrintRequested { tab }` that opens the sheet through `Host::print`. Submitting answers the held callback with cancel, since wubble renders its own PDF, so the page's afterprint fires. On macOS and Windows, a helper content script replaces `window.print` with a call to the same event (keeping beforeprint/afterprint ordering), so every platform shows the one sheet. Add a `print::Event` for a page-started open and test it in crates/wubble-core/src/print.rs.

title: Page info popover from the lock: connection, permissions, cookies, site settings
spec:
In Chrome, clicking the omnibox lock opens Page Info. It shows whether the connection is secure, with a sub-page that has "Certificate is valid". It lists the site's permissions that are not at their default, each with a toggle or dropdown, plus "Reset permissions". It shows cookies and site data in use ("N cookies in use", Manage), a toggle for third-party cookies on this site, "Turn on warnings" when a certificate exception exists, and links to Site settings. In wubble, the lock in kit/chrome/address-pill.slint is not clickable and nothing like this exists.

Build:
- Add an overlay kind `PageInfo` (tab-scoped, exclusive, Escape closes) in crates/wubble-core/src/overlay.rs.
- Add a pure view model `wubble_core::pageinfo` built from the tab's `SecurityLevel`/`SecurityInfo` (security-state feature), the container's SitePermissions and content settings, cookie counts and cert exceptions. Its rows are an enum, and its actions return `Command`s: SetPermission, ResetPermissions, ForgetCertException, OpenSiteSettings, ShowCertificate, ClearSiteData. Unit-test it.
- UI: a popover composed from kit components (popover/card/rows/toggle/select), new file crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/page-info.slint, opened by the pill's lock (`clicked` on the lock element).
- Host: crates/wubble/src/host/ (new pageinfo.rs) fills the model. The cookie count comes from the container's cookie manager visitor filtered by the site's domain (vendor/welding/src/cookies.rs CookieJar). Revoking a cert exception also calls `RequestContext::clear_certificate_exceptions`.

title: Web notifications shown by wubble, with click-to-tab
spec:
In Chrome, once a site is allowed, new Notification() and registration.showNotification() show OS notifications. A click focuses the window, selects the tab and fires the click event. wubble grants the Notifications permission (prompt.rs), but display depends on Chromium's NotificationPlatformBridge inside CEF: on macOS it needs Chrome's alerts helper app, which is not in the bundle. Clicks call WebContentsDelegate::ActivateContents, which Alloy leaves empty, so the tab is never brought forward.
Build repo-side: (1) Add a main-world content script channel `notify` to wubble-helper/src (registered in main.rs `compose`). For a granted origin it replaces window.Notification and ServiceWorkerRegistration.prototype.showNotification from page contexts with a shim. The shim keeps the API shape (permission, requestPermission → the real one, onclick/onclose/onshow, close(), tag replacement, silent, requireInteraction) and posts {id, title, body, icon, tag} to the browser. (2) On the browser side, show the notification in crates/wubble through the `notify-rust` crate (MIT/Apache-2.0; DBus org.freedesktop.Notifications on Linux, the native centre on macOS, toast on Windows), with a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry. On click, raise the window, select the tab and send `click id` back to the shim, which dispatches onclick. Close and replace work the same way. (3) A click on a registration notification focuses the tab and calls the page's notificationclick-equivalent listener only when the page registered one through the shim. Worker-initiated notifications stay Chromium's (push needs FCM, which stays off). (4) Add a Settings row "Show notifications from sites". Icons are fetched only for already-loaded page resources.

title: Downloads settings section with a folder picker
spec:
Chrome's Settings → Downloads has Location [Change] and "Ask where to save each file". The design has a Downloads section with "Save files to" (a folder choice), "Ask where to save each file" and "Open safe files after downloading" (ref/the-wallpaper-project/src/wubble/pages/settings.tsx lines ~55-123). In wubble the downloads folder can only be set on the command line (crates/wubble/src/profile.rs downloads_dir: the CLI, else dirs::download_dir). DOWNLOADS_ASK_WHERE and the media rows sit under Section::General, and there is no Downloads section.

What to build: (1) wubble-core/src/settings.rs: add `Section::Downloads` (title "Downloads"). Move DOWNLOADS_ASK_WHERE and the MEDIA_* rows into it, which changes no stored keys. Add `DOWNLOADS_DIR` (key downloads.dir, empty means the OS default) with a new `SettingKind::Folder`, and update the tests. (2) Settings UI (components/settings.slint, kit pages): a folder row that shows the path and a Change button. It opens the OS folder chooser through crates/wubble/src/chooser.rs (FileChooserMode::OpenFolder, or add that mode). Reuse it for MEDIA_SAVE_DIR, which is a free text field today. (3) Host: Downloads gets `set_dir(Option<PathBuf>)` (host/downloads.rs), applied live from the settings handler (host/settings.rs); a CLI value still wins. The Settings nav gets the section's icon (the design's `download` glyph is already Glyph.download). (4) Settings search finds it ("folder location directory", the design's `find` words). All platforms.

title: OS re-authentication before revealing, copying, exporting or editing secrets
spec: Chrome on macOS and Windows asks for the device password, Touch ID or Windows Hello before showing, copying, editing or exporting a saved password (and before filling a saved card), with a grace period of about a minute; Linux Chrome has no prompt. wubble unlocks the vault through the keyring only (`VaultCommand::Unlock`, crates/wubble-vault/src/command.rs), and Reveal/Copy run without a check (crates/wubble/src/host/pages.rs `Then::Show`, `Then::Copy`). Build: a `trait Reauth { fn ask(reason: &str) -> Result<bool, String> }` in crates/wubble (one shared trait, per-platform impls): macOS `LAContext evaluatePolicy:deviceOwnerAuthentication` via objc2-local-authentication; Windows `UserConsentVerifier::RequestVerificationAsync` (windows crate), falling back to `CredUIPromptForWindowsCredentialsW`; Linux: a no-op that returns true, as Chrome does, with an optional polkit check left out. A pure gate in wubble-core, `reauth::Gate` (one enum: `Fresh{until}`/`Stale`, `fn transition`), decides whether an action needs a prompt (60 s grace, reset on lock and when the page is left). Route Reveal, Copy, Edit (when the password field changes), ExportCsv and card fill through it in crates/wubble/src/host/pages.rs, running the prompt off the UI thread. Setting `passwords.reauth` (crates/wubble-core/src/settings.rs, Section::Privacy, default true on macOS and Windows, hidden on Linux). Unit tests for the gate.

title: Extensions P4: permission requests answered in wubble's UI
spec: In Chrome, `chrome.permissions.request` (with a user gesture) shows a dialog listing the new permissions and resolves true or false. Optional host permissions use the same path, and so do `management.uninstallSelf({showConfirmDialog})` and the re-enable prompt after a permission increase. In wubble, `permissions.request` rejects with "Could not find an active window." (Bitwarden's first-run step; docs/research/extensions.md gap 3; TODO M6 P4). Chromium-side patch, `patches/chromium/50-cef-permission-prompts.patch` (CEF side) and `51-src-permission-prompts.patch`: in `chrome/browser/extensions/api/permissions/permissions_api.cc` (`PermissionsRequestFunction::Run`) and `extension_install_prompt.cc`, under `BUILDFLAG(ENABLE_CEF)`, when the web contents has no `Browser`, call a new delegate entry `permission_prompt(ctx, request_id, extension_id, kind, json_permissions)` in `cef_wubble_ext_delegate_t`. The answer comes through a new table function `permission_answered(request_id, allow)`, which runs the prompt's done callback (`ExtensionInstallPrompt::DoneCallback` with `Result::ACCEPTED`/`USER_CANCELED`). Bump the table to `cef_wubble_ext_v2` with a `size` check, so a v1 engine keeps working. wubble side: `crates/wubble-engine/src/ext_api.rs` adds `ExtRequest::PermissionPrompt { id, extension, kind, permissions }` and `Engine::answer_permission`. Core: reuse `extensions/shell.rs::Prompt` and `prompt_transition` with a new `Prompt::Asking { request, lines }` variant. The words come from the existing `permission_lines`, plus host patterns phrased as Chrome phrases them (`IDS_EXTENSION_PROMPT_WARNING_HOST_*`). Host: `host/ext_ui.rs` shows the same modal kit sheet as the install prompt (Allow / Deny). Granted optional permissions are added to `Extension::permissions` for the Settings list. Uninstall-self confirmation uses the same sheet.

title: macOS: open links and files from other apps, Dock reopen and Dock menu
spec: On macOS, LaunchServices delivers a clicked link or an "Open With" file as an Apple Event, not as argv. wubble handles neither. `crates/wubble-engine/src/mac_app.rs` overrides only `sendEvent:` and `terminate:`, and `wubble-bundle`'s Info.plist (`crates/wubble-bundle/src/main.rs` `add_plist_keys`) has no `CFBundleURLTypes` or `CFBundleDocumentTypes`, so wubble cannot even be picked as the default browser. To build: (1) in `add_plist_keys`, `CFBundleURLTypes` for http and https (role Viewer) and `CFBundleDocumentTypes` for public.html, public.xhtml, com.adobe.pdf, public.svg-image, public.png/jpeg/gif/webp and public.plain-text, with `LSHandlerRank` Alternate. Chrome's Info.plist is the model. (2) In `mac_app.rs`, from `prepare_process` before `finishLaunching`, register `NSAppleEventManager setEventHandler:` for kInternetEventClass/kAEGetURL ('GURL'). Add `application:openURLs:` (files, `file://`) to winit's application delegate class with `class_addMethod`, as `wl/macos.rs` does for winit's view. (3) Each URL goes to the host as `instance::Message::Open` (the same path a second start takes, `instance::listen`'s `deliver`), queued until the first window's host exists, because a cold start's event comes before it. (4) `applicationShouldHandleReopen:hasVisibleWindows:`: with no visible window, open a main window (Chrome's behaviour). (5) `applicationDockMenu:` with "New Window". The menu is built from the action table, so it runs `Action::NewWindow` through `perform.rs`. Compile-check from Linux only. Run nothing on the Mac.

title: Gallery: shoot a Settings section only after the page's jump has landed
spec: TODO line 45. In `--smoke gallery`, a Settings section picked far from where the page sits is shot mid-jump: the settings page scrolls with a spring, and `settings-extensions` on the patched engine shows Filter lists passing. Fix it in the gallery driver (`crates/wubble/src/gallery_smoke.rs`, `crates/wubble/src/host/gallery.rs`). Either wait for the page's scroll spring (the settings page's scroller motion in `wubble_core::scroller` / `motion`) to report it is at rest before the shot, or jump with no animation in the gallery (a `jump_instant` path on the settings nav that sets the scroller's position and velocity directly). Prefer waiting on the spring's settled state, with a bounded wait (for example 2 s) and a log line if it does not settle. No timing assertions.

title: Page damage rebuilds the page blur only within the ambience's reach
spec:
Damage far from any glass, such as a spinner in the middle of the page, still marks P (the page-inclusive blur pyramid) stale. The ambience then rebuilds at 8 Hz, each time as a whole-window frame. This item also covers the TODO item that a page frame should touch the scene and pyramid only while overlay glass or motion is on screen.

To build: in crates/wubble-gfx/src/scene/pages.rs, add an `AMBIENCE_REACH` (about 130 logical px from a pane edge, from the ambience's blur radius) and a pure `fn reaches(damage: Rect, page: &PageRect, overlays: &[Rect]) -> bool`. It is true when the damage lies within the reach band of the pane's edge, or under an overlay-glass rect. Change `Renderer::pages_written` and `set_pages` in scene/render.rs to take the frame's damage: the in-place `Damage` from `FramePresenter::present_damaged` (crates/wubble-gfx/src/import.rs), where a whole frame counts as reaching. Set `pages_stale` only when it reaches. Pass that damage from crates/wubble/src/host/panes.rs (around line 839, next to `mark_rect`) through `Glass::pages_written` in backdrop.rs. In `page_blur`, a stale page with only the ambience on and no overlay keeps its low rate. With no overlay glass over a pane and the ambience at 0, the host skips `set_pages`/`schedule_pages` for page frames altogether. Unit tests in pages.rs. All platforms.

title: History page: row menu (more from this site, remove, delete site), bulk select and delete
spec:
Each row on Chrome's History page has a menu: 'More from this site' (filters to that host), 'Remove from history'. Checkboxes select rows for 'Delete' as a group, and Shift-click selects a range. wubble's history page (crates/wubble/src/host/pages.rs feed_*, history_query, history_deleted; components/pages.slint) has search, a per-row delete and 'Clear history' with ClearRange. The store already has delete_history_site (crates/wubble-store/src/history.rs), but nothing calls it.

Add:
1. A row context menu (Menu::Shell, crates/wubble/src/menu.rs) with Open in new tab, Copy address, More from this site, Remove from history, Delete all from <site>. 'More from this site' sets the query to a host filter: give query_history a `site:` prefix or a host argument. Add HistoryClear::Site(host) in wubble-store, executed in crates/wubble/src/persist.rs. Deleting a site's history also removes its recently-closed entries and orphan favicons, per the 'Clearing history' decision.
2. Selection: a pure set of selected keys in wubble-core/pages.rs, with toggle, range and clear operations and unit tests. It shows as the kit check box in the list row (kit/pages/list-row.slint gains a selectable slot), with a header bar of 'N selected · Delete · Cancel' composed from kit buttons. The delete runs one store call over a list of URLs: add HistoryClear::Urls(Vec).
3. Overlaps the open TODO 'List pages … no select, delete selection': build history first, and keep the selection type generic so Bookmarks, Downloads and Archive can reuse it.

The Archive feed keeps its own delete.

title: Save page as: Webpage, Complete (HTML plus resources folder)
spec: Chrome's "Webpage, Complete" (`content/browser/download/save_package.cc`, BSD-3) serializes the live DOM of every frame (`WebFrameSerializer`). It saves each subresource (images, stylesheets, scripts, frames) into `<name>_files/` and rewrites the references to relative paths. It adds the `<!-- saved from url=(NNNN)... -->` mark-of-the-web comment and reports progress in Downloads. wubble has nothing like it. To build, after save-page-formats provides the chooser and `Action::SavePage`: use CDP through crates/wubble-engine/src/cdp.rs. `Page.getResourceTree` and `Page.getResourceContent` give each resource's bytes from cache, with no new network request. `DOM.getDocument` with pierce and `DOM.getOuterHTML` (or a helper script serializer) gives each frame's current DOM. A pure `wubble_core::savepage::complete` module plans the files from (frame HTML, resource URLs and MIME types): unique safe file names as Chromium's `SavePackage::GetSavableFileName` makes them, a rewrite map for src/href/srcset/url() in inline style and in saved CSS, and the mark-of-the-web line. It is unit-tested on fixture strings. The host writes the files on a worker thread under the chosen folder and reports a downloads-list entry with progress and errors. Resources not in cache are left as absolute URLs (no fetch), and that is documented in decisions.

title: Certificate interstitial: Advanced section, non-overridable errors, per-container exceptions
spec:
Chrome's SSL interstitial hides Proceed behind "Advanced", which also shows the error code and a short explanation. It never allows proceeding for revoked certificates, pinned or HSTS hosts, or blocked interception. Exceptions are per profile and are cleared by "Turn on warnings" and by clear browsing data. wubble has the panel (crates/wubble/src/page_error.rs `PageError::Cert`, crates/wubble-core/src/neterror.rs `CertExceptions`, session-only, per host and code), with Proceed offered for every certificate code.

Build:
- In neterror.rs, add `fn overridable(code) -> bool` (false for ERR_CERT_REVOKED -206, ERR_CERT_KNOWN_INTERCEPTION_BLOCKED -217, ERR_SSL_PINNED_KEY_NOT_IN_CERT_CHAIN -150, ERR_CERT_SYMANTEC_LEGACY, and similar), following Chromium's `ssl_error_handler`/`ssl_blocking_page` (BSD-3-Clause). When the URL's host is an HSTS host (if CEF gives no HSTS bit, treat `CefSSLInfo` cert_status with STRICT_ENFORCEMENT as non-overridable), the panel shows no Proceed. Write unit tests.
- PageError::Cert gains `advanced: bool`, so the panel transition has an Expand step. The kit error panel shows the code name and a "View certificate" link (certificate-viewer feature).
- Exceptions are keyed by container (shared with permissions-per-container), are cleared by the clear-data dialog and page info, and `RequestContext::clear_certificate_exceptions` is called on a revoke so Chromium's cached allow goes too.

title: A working location provider for navigator.geolocation
spec:
In Chrome, a geolocation grant gets a position from the OS provider (Core Location on macOS, Windows Location) or from Google's network provider, which needs an API key. wubble prompts for and grants Geolocation (prompt.rs, site.rs), but CEF has no Google API key. Linux has no system provider in Chromium, so pages get POSITION_UNAVAILABLE. On macOS the bundle needs NSLocationUsageDescription for Core Location to ask at all.
Build: (1) On Linux, add a provider module in crates/wubble (behind a trait with one implementation per OS, per AGENTS.md) that reads GeoClue2 over DBus (the `zbus` crate, MIT). While a tab with a granted geolocation is watching, apply the position to that tab through DevTools Emulation.setGeolocationOverride {latitude, longitude, accuracy} (wubble-engine cdp.rs and View's DevTools call path), and clear it when the grant is revoked or the tab navigates cross-origin. To know when a page is watching, add a small `geo` content-script channel that reports getCurrentPosition/watchPosition calls. (2) On macOS, add NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription to the app's Info.plist (scripts/release packaging and docs/macos.md) so Chromium's own Core Location provider works. (3) GeoClue may ask a network service for Wi-Fi positioning, so add a setting "Use the system location service for sites", off by default as the no-phone-home rule requires. With it off, the prompt still works and the page gets an error. (4) Unit-test the pure part (grant plus watch state → override or clear effects) in wubble-core.

title: Downloads outlive their tab; warn on quit with downloads running
spec:
In Chrome a download keeps going after its tab closes. Quitting while one runs asks "N downloads in progress. Cancel downloads and quit?". wubble cancels instead: host/downloads.rs `downloads_closing` cancels every running download of a closing tab (toast "Download cancelled: its tab closed"), because the CEF download callbacks belong to the view. Quit does not check for running downloads.

What to build: (1) Parked views. When a tab with running downloads (`Downloads::holds`) closes, its wubble_engine::view::View moves out of `self.views` into a `parked: HashMap<DownloadId-owner, View>`: hidden (`was_hidden`), muted, navigated to nothing new, and absent from the model, from extensions and from MCP. The view is closed when its last inflight download ends, which is the one place in `apply_download` where inflight is removed. Pause, resume and cancel reach the parked view through `running()`. The sleep policy and memory reports count it. (2) Quit. Add a pure `wubble_core::download::quit_check(entries) -> Option<usize>`. The quit path (Action::Quit and the window close in host/window.rs, plus Cmd+Q on macOS) opens the existing dialog sheet (components/dialog-sheet.slint, DialogView): "Cancel N downloads and quit?" with Quit and Keep downloading. Media download jobs (host/media.rs) count too. (3) Tests: a unit test for quit_check, and a host test that closing a tab keeps its download's entry Running. All platforms.

title: Save and fill HTTP authentication (Basic/Digest) logins
spec: Chrome's password manager offers saved credentials in the HTTP auth dialog (prefilled username and password for the origin + realm) and offers to save them after a successful answer. wubble's auth prompt (crates/wubble/src/prompt.rs `Auth`, `AuthRequest { realm, .. }`, answered through welding `answer_auth`, crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs) never touches the vault; the vault has no realm (crates/wubble-vault/src/record.rs) although the CSV parser knows an `HttpRealm` column (crates/wubble-vault/src/import.rs). Build: migration 0xx adding `http_realm TEXT` (plaintext, like origin) to `logins`; `NewLogin.http_realm: Option<String>` and `Vault::find_for_realm(origin, realm)`; import keeps `httpRealm` rows from Firefox exports instead of skipping them. In `prompt::auth`'s transition add `Prefill(Candidate)` and `Answered{save: bool}` events with effects `QueryLogins{origin, realm}`/`OfferSave{..}`; the host (crates/wubble/src/host/ owner of the auth prompt) runs them against the vault with `vault_then`. The dialog prefills the first match's username and password (password never shown, kit field in its masked mode); after the page loads with a 2xx status (no new auth challenge for that realm) the existing autofill save prompt (`AutofillMenu` prompt) is shown with Save/Never/Not now, reusing `SaveVerdict` logic from crates/wubble-core/src/autofill.rs. Never save in agent session tabs. Unit tests in prompt.rs and the vault.

title: Extensions: site access controls (on click, on specific sites, on all sites)
spec: Chrome's extensions menu and details page let the user withhold an extension's host permissions: "When you click the extension", "On <site>", or "On all sites". A withheld extension shows a "wants access" request in the toolbar menu, and a click grants activeTab or a runtime host permission. wubble grants everything at load and has no control (`Manifest::permissions` comment: "What it is granted at load (nothing asks first)"). Patch (`52-src-site-access.patch` plus CEF table functions): export `site_access_get(ext_id, url) -> {on_click|on_site|on_all, withheld}`, `site_access_set(ext_id, mode, origin)` over `extensions::PermissionsManager` / `ScriptingPermissionsModifier` (`SetWithholdHostPermissions`, `GrantHostPermission`, `RemoveGrantedHostPermission`), and a delegate notice `site_access_requested(ext_id, browser_id)` from `SitePermissionsHelper` / `ExtensionActionRunner::OnActiveTabPermissionGranted` paths. wubble side: in `ext_api.rs`, add the wrappers and `ExtRequest::AccessRequested`. Core: a pure `extensions::access` module that maps the stored per-extension mode and site list to what to tell the engine at start and on change, with tests. UI: a per-extension "Site access" kit select in the Settings extensions section, and, in the footer popover (`extensions/shell.rs::Panel`), a per-row badge and an "Allow on this site" row for the visible tab's origin. Store the choice in the installed list (`Extension` gains `site_access`).

title: macOS: a native menu bar with every command
spec: Chrome on macOS has a full menu bar (app, File, Edit, View, History, Bookmarks, Profiles, Tab, Window, Help) whose items show their shortcuts and run the same commands as the keys. wubble has only winit's default app menu: there is no NSMenu code anywhere, and decisions.md "Edit commands" says Cmd edit forms run as actions because Blink leaves them to the menu. Without a Window menu there is no Cmd+` window cycling, no Window list, and no Services or Emoji & Symbols. To build: (1) a pure table in `wubble-core` (`menubar.rs`) of menus, each item an `Action` (`wubble_core::action`) with its label and enabled rule, its shortcut read from the user's `Keymap` (`wubble_core::keys`), so rebinding updates the menu. Unit-test that every bound action appears. (2) A macOS edge in `crates/wubble/src/menubar_mac.rs` (objc2-app-kit) that builds `NSApp.mainMenu` from the table at start and on keymap changes. Each item's target forwards its `Action` to the focused window's host and runs it as `perform.rs` does. Set `windowsMenu`, `servicesMenu` and `helpMenu` so AppKit adds Window list, Services, Emoji & Symbols and Help search. (3) Key equivalents: AppKit's `performKeyEquivalent:` reaches the menu before winit, so the host must not run a chord twice. Either route Cmd chords to the menu (and drop the host path on macOS for those), or answer `menuHasKeyEquivalent` false while a page or shell field that owns the chord (`Route::PageFirst`) has focus. Pick one rule, put it in decisions-worthy terms in the report, and keep `input.rs` routing tests green. The app menu covers About, Settings (Cmd+,), Hide, Hide Others, Show All and Quit (through the existing `set_quit_handler`). Compile-check only; macOS only.

title: Page translation: language detection, the offer, rules, state machine and in-page DOM translation
spec: TODO line 56, docs/research/translate.md sections 5-6 (Chrome's Translate bubble, built on-device). (1) Detection: a helper content script (like `crates/wubble-helper/src/*.js`) reports `<html lang>`, Content-Language and about 2 KB of visible text at DOMContentLoaded. Detect with a pure Rust crate (whatlang, MIT, or lingua; licence-checked, with a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry). (2) A new `wubble_core::translate`: `TranslateState` (Idle, Offered, Downloading(pair), Translating(progress), Translated, Failed) and a pure `transition(state, event) -> (state, effects)`, unit-tested. Per-site and per-language always/never/ask rules are a settings table (`wubble_core::settings`, `wubble-store` settings). (3) The offer: a Translate chip by the address pill and a popover (source, target, always/never), built from kit parts (derived pieces go on docs/fidelity/derived-review.md). Context-menu rows "Translate to <lang>" and "Show original" go in `crates/wubble/src/menu.rs`. (4) The in-page walker script: viewport-ordered translation units, kept inline tags, a skip list (code, pre, inputs, contenteditable, translate=no, .notranslate), a WeakMap of originals, a rAF-coalesced MutationObserver, and show-original. Units go to a `TranslateBackend` trait (`backend-bergamot` feature implements it) through `View::eval`/frame messages. No backend is on by default.

title: Hidden tabs and idle glass free their GPU targets
spec: Chrome frees a hidden tab's compositor surfaces. wubble does not need the CEF patch (M6) for its own part of this: (1) Each welding view keeps its last copied frame in its `PendingFrameSlot` (vendor/welding/src/linux_cef/mod.rs `frame_slot`, macos_cef likewise). That is a full-size wgpu texture from `copy_to_owned` (vendor/welding/src/native_frame/mod.rs), held until taken, even after the view is hidden. Add a welding API (mark it `wubble change` and list it in WUBBLE_CHANGES.md) that clears the slot and stops storing copies while the view is hidden. Call it from wubble-engine `View::set_hidden` or wherever views are hidden (crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs). (2) The per-window `FramePresenter` rings (crates/wubble/src/host/window.rs `presenters`, `popup_presenter`, PEEK_SLOT, PANEL_SLOT) keep their two-texture ring after a slot's pane goes away (split closed, peek closed, DevTools closed). Add `FramePresenter::release()` (crates/wubble-gfx/src/import.rs) and call it when a slot is emptied. (3) The scene's page pyramid P and the over-layer textures (scene/render.rs `sz.page`, over images) are dropped after a few seconds with no overlay glass and no ambience. They are rebuilt on demand, as after a resize. (4) Closing a tab drops its snapshot texture (host/snapshots.rs `release`) and its favicon image if nothing else uses it. Count live targets in `--measure` (`gpu_targets`), so the owner's open-10/close-10 run can tell a cache from a leak (TODO Optimization 3 and 4). Linux and macOS.

title: Error panel: full error table, HSTS refusals, details, HTTP error pages, form resubmission
spec:
wubble's error panel (crates/wubble/src/page_error.rs PageError/ErrorText, crates/wubble-core/src/neterror.rs NAMES/describe, components/error-panel.slint) covers about 50 codes. Chrome's net error page and SSL interstitial also do the following, none of which wubble does:
1. Name and describe the rest of net_error_list.h that a page can meet: ERR_ABORTED is skipped; ERR_CACHE_MISS, ERR_BLOCKED_BY_RESPONSE, ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR, ERR_PROXY_CONNECTION_FAILED, ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED, ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR, ERR_QUIC_PROTOCOL_ERROR, ERR_SSL_OBSOLETE_VERSION, ERR_BAD_SSL_CLIENT_AUTH_CERT, ERR_SSL_CLIENT_AUTH_CERT_NEEDED, ERR_CERTIFICATE_TRANSPARENCY_REQUIRED (-214), ERR_CERT_SYMANTEC_LEGACY (-215), ERR_SSL_PINNED_KEY_NOT_IN_CERT_CHAIN, ERR_ADDRESS_INVALID, ERR_DNS_* and the rest. Check each number against cef_errorcode_t.
2. Non-overridable certificate errors. When welding's on_certificate_error gets no callback (HSTS, pinned), the load fails and today shows as Load with 'Reload'. Show a Cert-style panel instead that says the site uses HSTS and cannot be visited now, with no Proceed.
3. A 'Details' disclosure (kit fold, kit/motion/fold.slint) with Chrome's suggestions per class: check the connection, proxy and firewall, DNS, clock wrong for ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID.
4. HTTP errors: welding's LoadEnd carries http_status but the engine drops it. Route it through crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs and page.rs. When the status is 4xx or 5xx and the body is empty (eval document.body.childElementCount == 0 after load), show Chrome's 'This page isn't working · HTTP ERROR 500' as a new PageError::Http.
5. ERR_CACHE_MISS on back or reload to a POST: Chrome's 'Confirm Form Resubmission' with a button that reloads (CEF's Reload reposts).

The transition stays the single machine. Add unit tests in page_error.rs and neterror.rs.

title: Touchscreen input reaches pages as touch (scroll, tap, long-press, pinch)
spec: Chrome on a touchscreen sends pages real touch and pointer events (pointerType touch): one finger scrolls with fling, a tap clicks, a double tap zooms (mobile viewport), a long press opens the context menu or selects a word, and two fingers pinch-zoom. wubble records winit `WindowEvent::Touch` only as an input kind (crates/wubble/src/host.rs `window_event`, `InputEvent::Touch`). Slint's TouchArea then turns the touch into mouse input (crates/wubble/src/input.rs), so a page sees mouse events: no touch scrolling, no pinch, no long press, and `touchstart` never fires. TODO.md "Input gaps: … touch input". The engine can already send touch (`cef::TouchEvent` in crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs for the synthetic pinch fingers; welding `send_touch` in vendor/welding/src/drag.rs). To build: in `window_event`, for a touch whose first contact lands on a page pane (`pane_under`), take the touch sequence for the page. Return `EventResult::PreventDefault` so Slint does not synthesize mouse input, and map winit's Touch id, phase, location and force to `View::touch(id, kind, point, pressure)`. This is a new View method that sends CEF `TouchEvent` with `pointer_type` TOUCH, using the same id mapping and Cancel rules as pinch.rs. Touches on the shell stay Slint's. A pure `wubble_core::touch` (or engine) router owns which sequence belongs to which pane, with tests. Platforms: X11 and Wayland through winit, Windows (WM_POINTER via winit), macOS (no touchscreen).

title: Client certificate selection sheet (mutual TLS)
spec:
Chrome shows "Select a certificate" when a server asks for a client certificate. It lists the subject and issuer of each matching certificate with OK and Cancel, and it auto-selects per the AUTO_SELECT_CERTIFICATE policy or setting. wubble does not handle `CefRequestHandler::OnSelectClientCertificate`, which exists in cef 156.6 bindings, so CEF's default runs and no choice is offered.

Build:
- welding: implement `on_select_client_certificate` in vendor/welding/src/handlers.rs. It returns 1 and holds the `CefSelectClientCertificateCallback` in the held-request table (vendor/welding/src/held.rs, like certificate and auth answers). It emits `NavigationEvent::ClientCertificate { id, host, port, certs: Vec<CertSummary { subject, issuer, not_after, der }> }` and adds `answer_client_certificate(id, Option<index>)` (a wubble change, listed in WUBBLE_CHANGES.md).
- wubble-engine page.rs / view.rs: add `PageEvent::ClientCertificate` and `View::answer_client_certificate`.
- crates/wubble/src/prompt.rs: a new `ClientCertPrompt` enum with a pure transition answering exactly once (the same shape as `Auth`). Remember the choice per (container, host:port) for the session. Agent tabs cancel with no prompt (fail closed, logged).
- UI: a Dialog-kind sheet (overlay `Kind::Dialog`) composed from kit list rows plus sheet buttons.
- Write unit tests for the transition.

title: navigator.registerProtocolHandler and the handlers list
spec:
In Chrome, navigator.registerProtocolHandler('mailto' | 'web+foo', 'https://site/?u=%s') asks "Allow <site> to open all mailto links?". Later navigations to that scheme go to the site's URL, and Settings → Protocol handlers lists the handlers and the default per scheme. CEF delivers REGISTER_PROTOCOL_HANDLER (1<<19) as a prompt bit, but AlloyBrowserHostImpl does not override WebContentsDelegate::RegisterProtocolHandler, so the call does nothing. wubble hands every unknown scheme to the OS (wubble_core::external, host/external.rs).
Build: (1) Add a main-world content-script channel `protocol` (wubble-helper/src, main.rs `compose`). It wraps navigator.registerProtocolHandler and unregisterProtocolHandler, validates them as the HTML spec does (safelisted schemes or web+, https URL of the same origin, containing %s), and posts them to the browser. (2) Add a pure table in wubble-core (scheme → handlers, default) with transitions and tests. Ask through the existing permission prompt as a new Permission::ProtocolHandler (wording from Chromium's register_protocol_handler_permission_request.cc), and persist the table in persist.rs. (3) In host/external.rs and engine nav (PageEvent::ExternalProtocol / NavigationRefused), a scheme with a default handler is rewritten to the handler URL (the %s filled with the encoded URL) and opened in the tab, before the OS question. The denied-scheme list still applies. (4) Add a Settings Sites subsection "Protocol handlers" with the default per scheme (kit Select) and Delete.

title: Download button progress ring and auto-opening bubble
spec:
Chrome's toolbar download button shows a ring that fills with the combined progress of the running downloads. It animates when a download starts or ends, and the download bubble opens by itself on a new download for a few seconds, showing that row. In wubble the sidebar's downloads IconButton (kit/chrome/side-bottom.slint, visible only while there are downloads) carries no progress, and a new download only raises a toast ("Downloading <name>", host/downloads.rs DownloadStarted and add_download_entry).

What to build: (1) wubble-core/src/download.rs: a pure `fn aggregate(entries) -> Option<f32>` (the received/total sum over running entries with a known size, else None for indeterminate) and an `unseen_complete` flag: true after a finish until the popover opens. Unit tests. (2) An app.slint property `downloads-progress` (float, -1 for none) and `downloads-unseen` (bool), set in render_downloads. (3) side-bottom.slint: the download button gets a progress ring and a dot. The design has no ring, so derive it from the kit's progress parts (kit/pages/list-progress.slint, AProgress) and put it on docs/fidelity/derived-review.md. If a new primitive is needed, it waits for the owner. (4) Auto-open: a new download opens the downloads popover (`downloads-open`) anchored to the button. It closes after a few seconds unless hovered, and replaces the toast. The timing is one enum and a pure transition in core. An agent-tab download never opens it. In compact or collapsed sidebar mode, fall back to the toast. All platforms.

title: Address, name, email and phone autofill with an Addresses page
spec: Chrome fills contact and shipping forms from saved addresses (name, organisation, street lines, city, state, postcode, country, phone, email), offers to save an address after a submitted form, and manages them under Settings > Autofill > Addresses and more. wubble has only password autofill (crates/wubble-core/src/autofill.rs classifies password forms; `FieldClass::CreditCard` exists only to skip). Build: (1) content script: extend crates/wubble-helper/src/autofill.js (or a sibling `forms.js` on the same `FrameChannel::Autofill`, crates/wubble-engine/src/page.rs) to report non-password forms: each input/select with type, name, id, autocomplete, label text, placeholder, aria-label, maxlength, and option values for selects; fill `select` by value or text. (2) New pure module `wubble_core::formfill`: a port of Chromium's heuristics `components/autofill/core/browser/form_parsing/` (`name_field.cc`, `address_field.cc`, `email_field.cc`, `phone_field.cc`, autocomplete parsing in `autofill_type.cc`) with the regexes of `autofill_regex_constants.h` (BSD-3, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), English first; one lifecycle enum + `transition` like `AutofillState`; unit tests with fixture forms. (3) Store: migration `addresses` table (guid, fields, use_count, use_date, modified) in crates/wubble-store/sql, plaintext as Chrome's Web Data. (4) Dropdown: reuse `AutofillMenu` rows with a second line (street), filling the whole section on pick, preview on hover is optional. (5) Save-after-submit prompt reusing the save prompt. (6) `InternalPage::Addresses` native page (list, add, edit, delete; kit list parts) linked from Settings, plus `autofill.addresses` setting (default on) in crates/wubble-core/src/settings.rs with a new Section "Autofill and passwords". Also offer email/username suggestions from addresses in login forms. Agent session tabs get no address fill.

title: Extensions shell: popup auto-size, tooltip, action menu, pinning, embedded options
spec: In Chrome, an action popup auto-resizes to its content between 25x25 and 800x600 (`ExtensionPopup`, `EnableAutoResize`). The toolbar button has a tooltip with the action title, and a right-click shows the extension's menu (name, Options, Remove from Chrome, Pin/Unpin, Manage extension, Inspect popup). Actions can be pinned to the toolbar, and `options_ui {open_in_tab: false}` options show in an embedded dialog. The global profile's `chrome.action` popups also work. wubble polls the popup page's size with a script every 150 ms (`host/ext_ui.rs`, `SIZE_SCRIPT`, `SIZE_POLL`). TODO M6 lists the rest as missing: the footer-button tooltip (needs an `Action`), the popup's own pointer origin for `<select>` lists, and global-profile popups. To build: (1) Welding change 58: `CefBrowserHost::SetAutoResizeEnabled(true, min, max)` on the popup view, with `CefDisplayHandler::OnAutoResize` pushed as a `WebEvent::AutoResized(w, h)` into `wubble-engine`. Use it when CEF delivers it for windowless browsers, else keep the script. (2) Tooltip: add an `Action::Extensions` in `action.rs` so the footer button gets the shared tooltip (`host/tooltip.rs`). Per-row tooltips show the action title from `ActionState`. (3) A right-click or long press on a popover row opens a kit menu (`wubble_core::controls::menu`) with Options, Pin to sidebar, Remove, Manage and Inspect popup. A pinned action renders as its own footer icon with its badge. Store the pins as a hidden setting. (4) `<select>` popups in the popup view take the popup pane's origin in `popups.rs`. (5) Options with `open_in_tab: false`: `Manifest` reads `options_ui.open_in_tab`, and the page opens in a kit sheet hosting a view, like the popup card at 800 max width. (6) Popups for the global profile: route its `action_click` popup URL to a view in `ContainerId::DEFAULT`.

title: macOS: Services and Look Up for page and shell selections
spec: In Chrome on macOS, the app menu's Services submenu and the context menu's Services offer system services on the selected text (Search with Google, New Note, Add to Music, translate), and Cmd+Ctrl+D / three-finger tap shows Look Up. wubble's page lives in an off-screen CEF view, so AppKit never asks winit's view for a selection. To build: (1) add `validRequestorForSendType:returnType:`, `writeSelectionToPasteboard:types:` and `readSelectionFromPasteboard:` to winit's NSView class at run time (`class_addMethod`, the technique `crates/wubble/src/wl/macos.rs` uses for `draggingEntered:`). They answer for NSPasteboardTypeString when the focused page has a selection. (2) Selection text: welding's OSR `OnTextSelectionChanged` (in `vendor/welding/src/macos_cef/cef_backed.rs`; if it is not forwarded yet, forward it as a `wubble change`) kept per view as the latest selected text in `wubble-engine/src/view.rs`; shell `TextInput` selections through Slint. (3) Reading back (a service that replaces the text) pastes through CEF's frame `paste` after it writes the pasteboard.
