(4) Register `NSApp.servicesProvider` only if wubble offers its own service ("Open URL in wubble"), with `NSServices` in `wubble-bundle`'s Info.plist. (5) Look Up: `showDefinitionForAttributedString:atPoint:` on the view at the selection's rect, from a "Look Up" row in the page context menu (`crates/wubble/src/menu.rs` rows, macOS only). Compile-check only.

title: Page translation: Bergamot helper process and opt-in model downloads
spec: TODO line 56, docs/research/translate.md 3.1 and 6. Implement the `TranslateBackend` trait (from `translate-detect-offer`) with Mozilla's bergamot-translator (MPL-2.0) in a new utility binary `wubble-translate-helper` (a new crate under crates/, tiny, no network). It is a child of the browser and takes `{pair, units[]}` over a pipe as JSON lines, returning the translated units with their HTML alignment. Build it through `cxx` or a C shim. If the native build stalls, the research's fallback is allowed: Firefox's WASM Bergamot in a hidden wubble page. Models: a per-pair download manager (in wubble-engine or the binary) that fetches Mozilla's published model files with pinned SHA-256 hashes into `<profile>/translate/<pair>/`. It runs only after an explicit user action in the offer popover or Settings. A setting `translate.downloads` is off by default, as AGENTS.md requires no request by default. Show progress through `TranslateState::Downloading`. Settings → Languages: installed pairs, sizes, remove. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entries for the engine and each model's licence. Private profiles keep results in memory only. Linux and macOS first; Windows compiles in CI.

title: Skia resource cache hygiene in the vendored renderer
spec:
Chromium runs a GrCacheController: a bounded resource cache, deferred cleanup of resources unused for a few seconds once idle, and a full purge when hidden or under memory pressure. wubble's Slint Skia renderer (vendor/i-slint-renderer-skia) keeps Skia's default cache (the 256 MiB budget named in TODO M6 and Optimization 4). It only exposes `free_gpu_resources` (lib.rs:713, a no-op on the wgpu surface at lib.rs:1382).

To build, in the vendored renderer (each change marked `wubble change` and listed in WUBBLE_CHANGES.md): on the wgpu 30 surface's `DirectContext` (wgpu_30_surface.rs), set `set_resource_cache_limit` to a wubble value, for example 96 MiB, scaled by window area and DPR as Chromium's `DetermineGraphiteImageProviderCacheLimitFromAvailableMemory`/`GetCacheLimits` do (an idea port with a source comment; BSD). Add `perform_deferred_cleanup(age)` and `purge_unlocked_resources()` behind a public `SkiaRenderer::cache_cleanup(CacheCleanup)` API. In wubble, add a pure policy in wubble-core (`skia_cache::next(state, event)`, unit-tested) with the events Rendered, Idle(Duration), Hidden/Minimised and Pressure(level). It returns effects such as Deferred(5 s), PurgeAll or None. The host executes them from the lifecycle tick and the pressure source (crates/wubble/src/host/memory.rs) and on window hide or minimise. Report Skia's cache bytes in `--measure` memory lines. All platforms.

title: Error panel: auto-reload when the network comes back
spec:
Chrome's NetErrorAutoReloader reloads a page that failed with a network error (ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED, ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED, ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED, ERR_CONNECTION_*, ERR_ADDRESS_UNREACHABLE, timeouts). It retries on an exponential backoff (1 s, 5 s, 30 s, 1 m, 5 m, 10 m), and at once when the system comes back online, but only while the tab is visible. It never retries certificate errors, a POST, or a load the user stopped. wubble's PageError::Load (crates/wubble/src/page_error.rs) stays until the user presses Reload.

Add the retry schedule to the error machine as data: a `retry: Option<Retry { attempt, due_ms }>` inside PageError::Load. New events: Tick(now_ms), Online, Hidden, Shown and UserStopped. A new effect is ErrorEffect::Reload with a flag marking it as automatic. All of it stays pure in transition(), and the host's existing tick drives Tick. The table of retryable codes lives in wubble-core/neterror.rs (a `retryable(code)` fn ported from Chromium's net_error_auto_reloader.cc IsReloadableError, BSD-3, behaviour only).

Online detection makes no request. On Linux, watch NetworkManager's or systemd-networkd's state over D-Bus only if a crate is already in the tree; otherwise rely on the backoff alone. On macOS use SCNetworkReachability or NWPathMonitor. Put each behind one shared trait in a new small module, next to os_scope.rs. Hidden tabs and sleeping or discarded tabs (wubble_core::sleep) do not retry. The panel shows 'Trying again…' while a retry is due. Unit tests for the schedule, the visibility gating and the refusal cases.

title: Touch text selection handles and the quick menu
spec: In Chrome on touch, a long press selects a word and shows two draggable selection handles plus a quick menu (Cut, Copy, Paste, Select all). An insertion handle appears under the caret in a field after a tap. Dragging a handle extends the selection. TODO.md "Text selection handles (touch)". CEF 156 supports this for windowless views: CefRenderHandler `GetTouchHandleSize` and `OnTouchHandleStateChanged` (handle orientation, origin, alpha, enabled), CefBrowserHost touch events moving the handles, and CefContextMenuHandler `RunQuickMenu`/`OnQuickMenuCommand`/`OnQuickMenuDismissed`. welding implements none of them. This feature needs touch-input first. To build: in welding (marked `wubble change`, WUBBLE_CHANGES.md), implement the two render-handler methods and the quick-menu methods, and emit `PageEvent::TouchHandles { start, end, insertion }` and `PageEvent::QuickMenu { request, rect, flags }` (crates/wubble-engine/src/page.rs). The shell draws the handles as a kit piece over the pane (derived, or from the design's touch kit if it has one; check the design repo first) at the reported positions, at the reported alpha. Drags on a handle go back to CEF as touch events with the handle's touch id, as Chromium's `TouchSelectionController` expects. The quick menu reuses the context-menu kit with the CEF quick-menu command ids, answered exactly once, with a lifecycle enum plus a pure transition in wubble-core.

title: Third-party cookie blocking, per-site cookie exceptions, clear on exit
spec:
Chrome's "Third-party cookies" settings offer Allow third-party cookies, Block in Incognito, and Block third-party cookies. There are per-site exceptions: allowed to use third-party cookies (user bypass, with a page-info toggle), Always clear cookies when windows are closed, and Block. A global "Clear cookies and site data when you close all windows" option exists too. wubble has none of these, and Chromium's defaults apply. The blocker's cookie-notice lists are something else.

Build:
- Add settings in crates/wubble-core/src/settings.rs (Section::Privacy): `cookies.third_party` (allow|block, default block, matching Chrome's current Incognito-only default and the privacy brief; the owner can flip it; note it in the report) and `cookies.clear_on_exit` (bool, default false).
- Apply them to every container's request context with `set_preference` (the pattern in crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs:848, moved to an Engine-level `set_profile_pref(container, name, value)`): `profile.cookie_controls_mode` (0/1/2) and `profile.block_third_party_cookies`. Re-apply when each context comes up.
- Per-site exceptions: a `wubble_core::site::CookieRule {Allow, AllowThirdParty, SessionOnly, Block}` per (container, site), stored in the store, applied through `set_content_setting(url, top_url, CEF_CONTENT_SETTING_TYPE_COOKIES, …)`. For third-party allows, use a primary of `*` and a secondary of the site. Unit-test the mapping.
- Clear on exit: at quit (`crates/wubble/src/quit` / run_state.rs, before engine shutdown), delete cookies per site, globally or for SessionOnly sites, through the cookie manager and `Storage.clearDataForOrigin`. A crash is covered by doing the same at the next start before the first navigation.
- UI: rows in Settings Privacy, plus a toggle in page info.

title: navigator.share: a share sheet
spec:
In Chrome on macOS and Windows, navigator.share({title, text, url, files}) opens the OS share sheet. Chromium on Linux has no navigator.share. In wubble's windowless CEF the macOS share picker has no anchor window, and the Linux API is missing.
Build: (1) Add a main-world content-script channel `share` (wubble-helper/src, main.rs `compose`). It defines or replaces navigator.share and navigator.canShare with spec behaviour: a transient user activation is required (navigator.userActivation.isActive), validate the data, reject with AbortError on cancel, NotAllowedError without activation, and InvalidStateError while one is open. It posts the request to the browser. (2) Add a pure machine in crates/wubble (one enum and a transition, like surface.rs Dialog) that answers each share exactly once and closes on navigation or tab close. (3) On macOS, show NSSharingServicePicker anchored at the window's content view (objc2, as crates/wubble already uses for macOS). On Linux and Windows, show a kit popover (overlay/a/a-popover.slint + a-menu-list.slint) with "Copy link" (the clipboard path in crates/wubble/src/clipboard.rs), "Email" (a mailto: built from title, text and url, handed out through wubble_core::external) and "Save files" for shared files. The popover is a derived piece on the owner's sheet. (4) Files arrive as blobs through the channel, up to a size cap; larger ones are refused with DataError.

title: Downloads page and popover rows: Chrome parity
spec:
chrome://downloads groups rows by date. Each row shows the source site as a link, a file whose file was moved or deleted reads "Deleted" with Open turned off, and a header button opens the downloads folder. Each row also has Copy download link, and a click on a finished row opens the file. In wubble, components/pages.slint DownloadsPage and download-row.slint show one flat list with name and detail, a row click does nothing, and a missing file is noticed only when Open fails ("File not found" toast in host/downloads.rs).

What to build: (1) Core (wubble-core/src/download.rs): add `fn groups(entries, today_ms) -> Vec<(label, Vec<id>)>`, with Today, Yesterday, then the date, reusing the History page's day-label helper if one exists in wubble-core. Add `DownloadEntry::removed: bool`, set by the host from a `path.exists()` check when the list renders (cheap, no watcher), and `can_open` returns false when removed. Add the source host for the second line. Unit tests. (2) Store: an end time column in a migration (Chrome shows it), set on Complete. (3) UI: DownloadItem gets `source`, `removed` and `group`. Add an Open downloads folder button in DownloadsPage's header, open on a row click (Enter too) for complete rows, and a Copy link action. Use the page kit's group headers, as the History page already does. (4) Host: DownloadAction `copy-link` (clipboard via crates/wubble/src/clipboard.rs) and `open-folder`. The list keyboard gaps already in TODO stay with that item. All platforms.

title: Payment card autofill with a Payment methods page
spec: Chrome fills credit card forms (cardholder name, number, expiry month/year or combined, optionally CVC) from saved cards, offers to save a card after a submit, masks numbers as "Visa ....1234", requires OS re-auth before filling on macOS/Windows, and manages cards under Settings > Autofill > Payment methods. Nothing in wubble; `FieldClass::CreditCard` (crates/wubble-core/src/autofill.rs) only excludes fields. Build on `address-autofill`'s content-script reporting and `wubble_core::formfill`: port Chromium's `credit_card_field.cc` (number, name, expiry split/combined, CVC regexes from `autofill_regex_constants.h`, BSD-3) plus Luhn and network detection (`credit_card.cc` IIN ranges), unit-tested. Storage: card numbers and CVCs are secrets, so put them in wubble-vault: a `cards` table (migration in crates/wubble-store/sql) with `number_enc`, `cvc_enc` (only when the user opts to save CVC, Chrome's 2024 behaviour, default off), name and expiry in plaintext or AEAD as the vault's threat model in crates/wubble-vault/src/lib.rs says; `VaultCommand::{ListCards, AddCard, EditCard, DeleteCard, RevealCard}`. Fill path: pick in the `AutofillMenu` dropdown -> `pw-os-reauth` gate where present -> decrypt on the store thread -> fill via the existing fill message; never fill into a cross-origin iframe unless it is the field's own frame (Chrome fills payment iframes only for their own origin). Only on https pages (Chrome refuses card autofill on http). Save-after-submit prompt for a new valid card. `InternalPage::PaymentMethods` page and `autofill.cards` setting (default on) in the Autofill section. No card data in agent sessions.

title: Extensions: tabs.getCurrent and getViews for non-tab views (Bitwarden popup width)
spec: In Chrome, `chrome.tabs.getCurrent()` returns undefined in an action popup, and `chrome.extension.getViews({type:'tab'})` does not count the popup. In wubble, the popup and the DevTools panel are windowless views that carry a `SessionTabHelper` id. So `getCurrent` returns `{id, windowId: -1}`, and Bitwarden concludes it is in a tab and lays out 57 px wide (docs/research/extensions.md gap 2; TODO M6). Patch `53-src-non-tab-views.patch`: in `chrome/browser/extensions/api/tabs/tabs_api.cc` `TabsGetCurrentFunction::Run`, and in `extensions/browser/extension_function...`/`chrome/browser/extensions/api/runtime` `GetViews` (`ExtensionHost`/`ProcessManager` view type), consult the registry from `10-cef-tabs-windows.patch` (`cef_wubble_ext` window and tab state). A web contents whose browser id is not in the last `set_state` tab list answers `getCurrent` with no tab, and `getViews` reports `mojom::ViewType::kExtensionPopup` for views wubble marks as popups. Add a table function `mark_view(browser_id, kind)` (popup, devtools, side panel), called by wubble when it opens such a view: `host/ext_ui.rs::open_popup` and `host/devtools.rs::open_panel`. wubble side: wrap it in `crates/wubble-engine/src/ext_api.rs` (`Engine::mark_ext_view(ViewId, ExtViewKind)`), guarded by a table version check, so an older engine just skips it. Acceptance: Bitwarden's popup lays out at its own 380 px.

title: Second start: many URLs, local files, the working directory and the activation token
spec: Chrome opens every URL or file on its command line, resolves relative paths against the caller's working directory, and the running instance's window comes forward, even on Wayland. wubble's CLI takes one optional `page` (`crates/wubble/src/cli.rs`). `instance::Message` carries `Open(String)` or `Focus` (`crates/wubble/src/instance.rs`), the desktop entry's `%U` can pass several URLs, a relative `wubble page.html` is never turned into a `file://` URL, and `host.rs`:887 calls `focus_window()`, which Wayland compositors refuse without a fresh activation token. To build: (1) cli.rs: `page: Vec<String>`. Each argument that names an existing path (relative to the cwd, or absolute) becomes a `file://` URL (`url::Url::from_file_path`), and anything else goes through the omnibox rule as today. Put that in a pure `wubble_core` fn with tests. (2) A wire format v2 in `instance.rs`: `open <url>` lines repeated, then `token <xdg-activation token or DESKTOP_STARTUP_ID>`, then `end`, under `MAX_MESSAGE`. `parse_message` stays strict, an old single line is still accepted, and tests cover both. (3) The primary opens the first URL as today (a Little window) and the rest as tabs in it, or as new tabs in the last focused main window if that is the policy, matching Chrome's "new tab in the last window". (4) Activation: read `XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN`/`DESKTOP_STARTUP_ID` in the second start. On Wayland the worker (`wl/wayland.rs`, on the windows' connection) binds `xdg_activation_v1` and calls `activate(token, surface)`. On X11 send `_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW` with the startup id's timestamp. On macOS and Windows call `NSApp activate` / `AllowSetForegroundWindow` from the second process.

title: Page translation: translate selection and reader-mode translation
spec: TODO line 56, docs/research/translate.md section 5 points 6-7 (Chrome's "Translate selection to <lang>" context row). Add a context-menu row on a text selection (`crates/wubble/src/menu.rs`, `wubble_core` menu model) that sends the selection text through the same `TranslateBackend` (feature `translate-bergamot-backend`), with no page mutation. Show the result in a read-only popover built from kit parts (a sheet or popover with copy). The reader view (`wubble_core::reader`, `crates/wubble/assets/reader.js`) runs the same unit walker on the extracted article after extraction, and remembers the last choice per site in the translate rules table. Reuse the `translate` state machine with a Selection target, no second machine. New core logic gets unit tests.

title: Recover page layout after a GPU process restart
spec:
After Chromium's GPU process exits (seen as a trap, exit 133, right after the gallery's agent scenes call `agents_stop`) and restarts, a page that stays alive lays out again with smaller body text until it is reloaded. In Chrome the renderer gets its screen info again and keeps its scale. wubble's watcher (crates/wubble/src/host/gpu.rs, `gpu_looked`) only counts the restart and calls `View::repaint()` (crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs:1280, `request_repaint`).

To build: (1) On a detected restart, also call CEF `BrowserHost::notify_screen_info_changed()` and `was_resized()` for every view. Add `View::refresh_screen()` in view.rs, using welding's existing host access (`self.send(|host| ...)`), so Chromium asks `GetScreenInfo`/`GetViewRect` again and gets the right device scale factor. Then call `repaint`. Make sure welding's render handler answers `get_screen_info` from the current metrics (vendor/welding/src/linux_cef, macos_cef), not a cached default. Mark any welding change `wubble change`. (2) Make the trap easier to find: log the GPU process's exit status when the watcher sees the pid vanish (wubble_sysmem), and under `WUBBLE_TRACE=1` log the agent teardown steps that ran just before (host/agent.rs `Effect::Release`/teardown order: closing DevTools sessions and views). If teardown closes a DevTools session after its view is gone, reorder it to close sessions first. Keep `wubble_core::gpu::watch` pure. Linux and macOS.

title: Connection security: certificate viewer, Not secure and mixed-content states in the address pill
spec:
Chrome shows a security state for each page: secure, 'Not secure' for http or a form on http, 'Dangerous' or crossed-out https after proceeding past a certificate error, and mixed-content warnings. Its page info bubble opens a certificate viewer with subject, issuer, validity, SHA-256 fingerprints and the chain. In wubble, is_secure (crates/wubble-core/src/chrome.rs) is only a check that the URL starts with https://. welding's on_certificate_error throws away ssl_info (vendor/welding/src/handlers.rs, `_ssl_info`), and there is no viewer.

1. welding, marked as a `wubble change` in WUBBLE_CHANGES.md: read CefSSLInfo's X509 certificate in on_certificate_error into a plain `CertInfo { subject, issuer, valid_from, valid_to, sha256, chain: Vec<..>, der }`. Add a call to read the visible navigation entry's CefSSLStatus (is_secure_connection, cert_status, content_status for displayed or ran insecure content, and its certificate) after load end.
2. wubble-core: a pure `security::level(url, ssl_status, proceeded_exception) -> Level { Secure, None, NotSecure, Dangerous, MixedContent }`, with Chromium's security_state.cc rules (BSD-3, behaviour only) and unit tests. Use CertExceptions in neterror.rs to tell when the user has proceeded past an error.
3. Feed Level into the address pill in place of the `secure` bool (crates/wubble/src/shell.rs, bind.rs, kit/chrome/address-pill.slint), with a 'Not secure' or 'Dangerous' label composed from existing kit text and glyphs.
4. A certificate sheet composed from kit sheet and list rows. It opens from the pill's security glyph and from the certificate error panel's Details, and has an Export (.pem) action through the save dialog.

If a site-info scout covers the pill's permissions bubble, share that surface.

title: Pen and stylus input as PointerEvents (pressure, tilt, eraser, hover)
spec: Chrome sends a pen as PointerEvents with pointerType "pen", pressure, tiltX/tiltY, twist, buttons (barrel button, eraser as button 5), and hover moves before contact. Drawing apps such as Excalidraw and Photopea depend on this. wubble has no pen path: winit 0.30 reports a pen only as Touch (with force) or as a mouse, and Slint turns it into mouse input. To build: read the platform's tablet input in the per-platform `crate::wl::Aux` workers. Wayland: `zwp_tablet_manager_v2`/`zwp_tablet_tool_v2` on the existing worker in crates/wubble/src/wl/wayland.rs (proximity, motion, pressure, tilt, buttons, tool type eraser). X11: XInput2 valuators for the stylus device in the x11 worker (x11-xdnd). Windows: WM_POINTER `POINTER_PEN_INFO` through a subclass of the HWND. macOS: NSEvent tablet point and proximity events in wl/macos.rs. Deliver a new `AuxEvent::Pen { phase, x, y, pressure, tilt, twist, buttons, eraser }`. The host routes it to the pane under it and sends CEF `TouchEvent` with `pointer_type` PEN or ERASER and pressure (CEF's touch struct has no tilt, so tilt is lost, which is documented) for contact. Hover without contact is sent as mouse moves. A pure mapping in wubble-core gets unit tests.

title: See and delete all site data per container
spec:
Chrome's "See all site data and permissions" lists every site that stored something (cookies, local storage, IndexedDB, cache storage, service workers), grouped by registrable domain, with its size. You can delete one site or all of them, and expand a site to see its cookies. wubble can only forget the visible tab's origin (`View::forget_site`, CDP `Storage.clearDataForOrigin`, crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs:1496) or clear whole containers.

Build:
- Engine: add `Engine::list_cookies(container, done)`, which visits every cookie through the container's cookie manager (reuse welding's CookieJar visitor, vendor/welding/src/cookies.rs, or storage.rs's visitor pattern). Add `Engine::site_usage(container, origins, done)` through CDP `Storage.getUsageAndQuota` and `Storage.getCookies`. These need a page of the container: use a live tab, else open a hidden about:blank view in that container (the media downloader's "live page of the same container" rule) and close it after. Add `Engine::forget_site(container, origin)` the same way, plus `delete_cookies(url)` for every scheme.
- wubble-core: add a pure `sitedata::group(cookies, origins) -> Vec<SiteRow { site (eTLD+1 via psl, already a dependency), container, cookies, bytes, origins }>`, with sorting and search. Unit-test it.
- Candidate origins come from the cookies' domains plus the store's history origins for that container.
- UI: a Settings > Sites "Site data" sub-panel with a container chooser, search, a ListEditor (Site, Cookies, Size, remove), "Delete all shown" with confirmation, and a per-site expand list of cookies (name, domain, expiry), each removable.

title: Install a site as an app (PWA) and open it in an app window
spec:
Chrome offers "Install <app>" for a site with a web app manifest (an omnibox icon and a menu item). An installed app opens in its own window with no tabs (display: standalone), gets a launcher entry and icon, and is listed at chrome://apps. Uninstall is there too. wubble has no manifest handling (no matches for `manifest`, `pwa` or `web app` outside the updater), and GetDisplayMode is always browser.
Build: (1) Read the manifest through DevTools Page.getAppManifest (wubble-engine cdp.rs) when a load ends. Parse name, short_name, start_url, scope, display, icons and theme_color in a pure wubble-core module (webapp.rs) with tests, keeping Chromium's installability rules (a name, start_url in scope, an icon of at least 144 px, https). (2) Add an "Install <name>…" row in the page menu (crates/wubble/src/menu.rs) plus a kit confirm sheet (b-sheet-parts.slint). Persist the installed app (id = manifest id or start_url) in persist.rs. (3) An app window reuses wubble's Little/Popup window kind (shell.rs window_space): sidebar hidden, its own Space/container entry, title from the page, navigation outside the scope opens in the main window. Add a `--app <id>` CLI flag (crates/wubble/src/cli.rs) that opens it. (4) Write a launcher entry: an XDG .desktop file plus an icon under ~/.local/share on Linux, and on macOS a small app shim or Dock entry in docs/macos.md terms. (5) Add a Settings section "Apps" with uninstall. Icons come from the page's already-loaded resources only.

title: Download progress on the Dock, taskbar and launcher
spec:
Chrome shows download progress outside the window. On macOS the Dock tile gets a progress bar and the count of running downloads, and the icon bounces once when one finishes. On Windows the taskbar button shows progress (ITaskbarList3::SetProgressValue / SetProgressState). On Linux it uses the Unity launcher API (DBus `com.canonical.Unity.LauncherEntry` signal `Update` with `progress`, `progress-visible`, `count`, `count-visible`), which GNOME's Dash to Dock, KDE's task manager and Plasma read. wubble shows nothing outside its window.

What to build: (1) Core: a pure `fn os_badge(entries) -> OsBadge { count, progress: Option<f64>, finished_since_last: u32 }` in wubble-core/src/download.rs, with unit tests. (2) One shared trait, `trait DownloadBadge { fn show(&mut self, b: &OsBadge); }`, in crates/wubble/src (e.g. a new os_badge.rs). Implement it per platform. Linux: send the LauncherEntry signal on the session bus with the app URI `application://wubble.desktop` (match the .desktop name the installer writes), using the DBus crate souvlaki already pulls in, if any. macOS: NSDockTile with a custom content view drawing the bar, badgeLabel, and requestUserAttention(informational) on a finish, via objc2 (already used by wl/macos.rs). Windows: ITaskbarList3 through the windows crate, behind cfg. (3) Host: call it from render_downloads only when the badge changed. Media jobs count. Nothing is sent while there are no downloads.

title: WebAuthn and passkeys through a shim, with roaming security keys (CTAP2 over USB HID)
spec: Chrome supports `navigator.credentials.create/get({publicKey})` with security keys, platform passkeys, conditional (autofill) UI and its own account-picker and PIN dialogs. wubble's windowless CEF views have no WebAuthn dialog host (docs/research/apple-passwords.md section 0 point 6), so WebAuthn fails or hangs. Build without an engine patch: (1) a main-world document-start script (registered like the other page scripts, crates/wubble/src/pagescripts.rs / crates/wubble-engine/src/cdp.rs `addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`) that replaces `navigator.credentials.create/get` for `publicKey` and `PublicKeyCredential.isUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable`/`isConditionalMediationAvailable`, forwards serialized options over a frame message to the host, and returns a `PublicKeyCredential`-shaped object; the host builds clientDataJSON itself from the frame's real origin (crates/wubble-engine frame info), never trusting the page's. (2) Pure state machine `wubble_core::webauthn` (Idle -> Asking -> PinNeeded -> Touching -> Done/Failed, `transition`, RP ID validation per WebAuthn L2 registrable-suffix rule, unit tests). (3) Transport: Mozilla's `authenticator` crate (authenticator-rs, MPL-2.0) for CTAP1/CTAP2 USB HID on Linux, macOS and Windows, behind a trait so platform authenticators plug in. (4) UI: a sheet (kit Sheet, prompt parts) for "Touch your security key", PIN entry, account choice for discoverable credentials. (5) The same shim answers `navigator.credentials.get({password:true})` (Credential Management API) from the vault after an explicit pick. Setting `passkeys.enabled` default on (no network). Hybrid (phone) transport needs Google's tunnel server: not built.

title: Extensions: install, enable, disable, remove and reload without a restart
spec: In Chrome, installing, toggling, removing and reloading (developer mode's Reload button) take effect at once. wubble applies every change at the next start, because the list becomes `--load-extension` (`wubble_core::extensions` module docs, `engine/app.rs::extension_switches`), and the TODO M6 "install page's restart to apply" is open. Patch `54-cef-ext-management.patch`: add table functions `load_unpacked(profile_path, dir) -> request id`, answered by a delegate `loaded(request_id, extension_id, error)`; `set_enabled(profile_path, extension_id, bool)`; `unload(profile_path, extension_id)`; and `reload(extension_id)`. They are implemented over `extensions::UnpackedInstaller::Create(...)->Load`, `ExtensionRegistrar::EnableExtension`/`DisableExtension(..., disable_reason::DISABLE_USER_ACTION)`, `ExtensionRegistrar::RemoveExtension`, and `ExtensionService::ReloadExtension`, for each loaded profile (each container's request context). Also add `set_file_access(ext_id, bool)` (`util::SetAllowFileAccess`) for Chrome's "Allow access to file URLs". When the extension system was off at start (no extension installed, so `disable-extensions`), live install still needs a restart; keep the restart notice for that case only. wubble side: `ext_api.rs` wrappers, `ExtRequest::Loaded`. Core: an `extensions::apply` pure transition from (running set, desired `Installed`) to effects (Load, Enable, Disable, Unload), with tests. `crates/wubble/src/extensions.rs::change` emits them when `ext_api::available()`, and `unused_copies` deletion waits until an unload is confirmed. UI: Settings rows get a Reload button for unpacked sources and an "Allow access to file URLs" toggle.

title: Command-line switches Chrome users expect
spec: Chrome users script the browser with `--new-window`, `--user-data-dir`, `--app=URL`, `--kiosk`, `--start-fullscreen`, `--start-maximized`, `--window-size=W,H`, `--window-position=X,Y`, `--proxy-server`, `--proxy-pac-url`, `--no-proxy-server`, `--proxy-bypass-list`, `--disable-gpu`, `--disable-extensions`, `--lang`, `--force-device-scale-factor`, `--remote-debugging-port` and `--enable-features`/`--disable-features`. wubble's clap `Cli` (`crates/wubble/src/cli.rs`) accepts only its own flags and rejects the rest. To build: (1) clap args with Chrome's names. `--user-data-dir` is an alias of `--profile`. `--new-window` forces a new main window, also through the instance socket (extend `instance::Message` with a NewWindow line). `--app=URL` opens a Little window (`WindowKind::Little`). `--kiosk`/`--start-fullscreen` start fullscreen with no sidebar. `--start-maximized`, `--window-size` and `--window-position` override `persist`'s saved geometry for the first window (`main.rs`:2140 `factory.open(..., geometry)`). (2) The Chromium pass-throughs (proxy, disable-gpu, lang, scale factor, feature lists) go into `EngineConfig`. A typed `Switches` struct is added in `wubble-engine/src/app.rs` `cef_config` after `CHROMIUM_SWITCHES`. User `enable-features`/`disable-features` are merged into `PageFeatures::switches`' single pair, never given twice (the comment at app.rs:512). `--disable-extensions` empties `config.extensions`. (3) `--remote-debugging-port` maps onto the existing debugging-port setting for this run only, so the MCP refusal rule (decisions.md "Debugging port and agents") still applies. Parse and mapping unit tests sit beside cli.rs's existing ones. `--help` lists them.

title: Live text in images: OCR job machine, image fetch, cache and selectable text layer
spec: TODO line 57, docs/research/ocr.md sections 4-5 (Chrome's "Select text in image"/Lens-less, Safari Live Text). (1) A pure `wubble_core::ocr`: `OcrState` (Idle, Fetching, Recognising, Ready, Failed) with `transition` and effects, plus an LRU keyed by blake3(bytes), engine version and languages, unit-tested. The cache is memory only for private profiles. (2) Pixels: the original image bytes through the engine's own fetch on the tab's request context (`crates/wubble-engine/src/fetch.rs`), with DevTools `Page.captureScreenshot` with a clip for canvas, video frames and CSS backgrounds (`View::cdp`). No frame-texture readback. (3) Presentation: a page script makes an injected closed-shadow-root layer of transparent `<span>`s positioned over the image. It follows the image's box (ResizeObserver, getBoundingClientRect), and takes pointer events only over text, so native selection, copy and find work. (4) Trigger: a context-menu row "Select text in image" on img, canvas or video (`crates/wubble/src/menu.rs`), later a hover trigger behind an off-by-default setting. Recognition goes through an `OcrBackend` trait that `ocr-backends` implements. Nothing touches the network.

title: Content blocker start-up gate holds the first navigation
spec:
With no compiled-engine cache (first run, or after a list change), requests go through unfiltered for several seconds until the lists compile. Chrome extensions such as uBO hold requests at start-up. wubble cannot wait on CEF's IO thread, so the hold belongs at the host. The swap point is `Blocking::swap` around crates/wubble/src/blocking.rs:477-481 (`measure::Stage::BlockerReady`).

To build: a pure lifecycle in wubble-core (for example `blocker_gate.rs`: `enum Gate { Waiting { held: Vec<Held> }, Ready }`, `fn transition(Gate, GateEvent) -> (Gate, Vec<GateEffect>)`). The events are Navigate { view, url } (a main-frame load the host is about to start: restored active tab, typed address, start URL, `wubble <url>` from the instance socket), BlockerReady, BlockerOff, ListsFailed and Deadline. The effects are Load(view, url) and ShowWaiting(view). It is Ready from the start when the cache loaded or the blocker is off (store `BlockerEnabled`). While Waiting, the host creates the view but delays `load_url`, and the pane shows the existing loading state. The gate is bounded by events: blocker ready, compile failure, or a deadline (for example 10 s) that loads anyway and logs it. Page-initiated navigations inside already-loaded pages are not held. Wire it into crates/wubble/src/host.rs where views get their first URL, and send BlockerReady from blocking.rs through the existing UI-thread channel. Unit tests for the transition. All platforms.

title: Internal URLs: chrome:// diagnostics, about: aliases, wubble://about index, wubble://version
spec:
In Chrome you can type chrome://version, gpu, net-internals, net-export, credits, media-internals, webrtc-internals, process-internals, accessibility, histograms, serviceworker-internals, indexeddb-internals, inspect, sandbox and so on. The about:X form maps to chrome://X, and chrome://about lists them all. The decision 'Internal surfaces' already allows Chromium diagnostics as web pages. But omnibox classify (crates/wubble-core/src/omnibox.rs, HIER_SCHEMES) does not take 'chrome', so 'chrome://gpu' becomes a search, and about:version is passed raw.

1. Add 'chrome' to the accepted schemes. Add a pure fn in wubble-core/pages.rs, `resolve_internal(url) -> Resolved { Native(InternalPage) | Chromium(String) | Refused }`, from one data table. Aliases go to wubble's native pages: chrome://settings, history, bookmarks, downloads, newtab, password-manager and about:settings and so on map to the wubble:// InternalPage. The WebUI hosts CEF 156 serves for alloy-style browsers pass through. Pages CEF lacks or that wubble replaces are refused (flags is covered by a separate feature).
2. Add InternalPage::About (wubble://about), a native list of every wubble:// page and the allowed chrome:// hosts, built from PAGE_LINKS and the table with kit list rows (kit/pages).
3. Map wubble://version and wubble://credits to chrome://version and chrome://credits, since CEF fills them with CEF and Chromium data. Settings' About section links them.
4. Agent-session tabs keep refusing chrome: (agent may_go and the 'Agent tabs stay on the web' decision); add a check that resolve_internal is never consulted for them.

The command bar suggests matching internal pages as Action-like rows. Unit tests for the resolver table.

title: X11: touchpad pinch, history swipe and lock keys
spec: Chrome on X11 (with XInput 2.4 gesture events, X server 21.1 and later) pinch-zooms the page on a touchpad pinch and goes back or forward on a two-finger sideways overscroll. wubble does both on Wayland through the worker (`zwp_pointer_gestures_v1`, the axis-source finger swipe in crates/wubble/src/wl/wayland.rs feeding `AuxEvent::Pinch`/`AuxEvent::Swipe` into host/gesture.rs and host/pinch.rs). Under X11 nothing reports them (`Aux` is `wl::Null`), so a pinch arrives as Ctrl+wheel steps (`zoom.js`, a page-zoom step, not Chrome's visual-viewport pinch), and there is no history swipe. Lock keys (`AuxEvent::Locks`) are also unreported there. To build: in the X11 worker introduced by x11-xdnd (crates/wubble/src/wl/x11.rs, x11rb), select XI_GesturePinchBegin/Update/End and XI_GestureSwipe* on each window and map them to `wubble_core::gesture::PinchInput`. Build the history swipe from XI2 smooth-scroll valuators of a touchpad device with no momentum, matching what wayland.rs does with axis frames, and deliver `AuxEvent::Swipe`. Read lock key state from XKB state notify. If the worker exists without x11-xdnd, it must be the same one owner. Pure mapping functions get unit tests in wubble-core gesture.rs.

title: Clear browsing data dialog: time range by kind, per container
spec:
Chrome's Clear browsing data has a time range (Last hour, Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last 4 weeks, All time) and checkboxes: Browsing history, Download history, Cookies and other site data, Cached images and files, Passwords, Autofill form data, Site settings, and Hosted app data. In wubble, `Action::ClearBrowsingData` opens a menu (crates/wubble/src/menu.rs `clear_entries`) that deletes cookies, cache and auth of containers at all time, and forgets one site. History has its own range (`pages::ClearRange`, three ranges).

Build:
- In crates/wubble-core/src/pages.rs, extend `ClearRange` with LastWeek and Last4Weeks. Add a pure `ClearPlan { range, kinds: BTreeSet<ClearKind>, containers }` and `fn effects(plan, now) -> Vec<ClearEffect>`, with unit tests.
- Effects: history and recently-closed through the store's existing range delete; downloads list rows in range (wubble-store downloads.rs); passwords created in range (wubble-store logins.rs); site_permissions and content settings with `decided_at` in range; cert exceptions; cookies created in range through a cookie visitor that deletes when `creation >= from` (`ImplCookieVisitor` with `delete_cookie=1`, in crates/wubble-engine/src/storage.rs); site storage per origin visited in range (Storage.clearDataForOrigin through a page of the container, the site-data-viewer helper); and the HTTP cache. CEF has no ranged cache clear, so the row says "all time" for cache when the range is not All. Use `storage::clear`'s ClearHttpCache.
- UI: a sheet (overlay `Kind::Dialog`) with a range select, kit check boxes, a container choice (This container / All), and "Delete data". It replaces the menu, and the History page's clear opens it preset.

title: Credential Management API for passwords (PasswordCredential) from wubble's vault
spec:
In Chrome, navigator.credentials.get({password: true, mediation}) returns a saved PasswordCredential from the password manager (with an account chooser, and auto sign-in for 'silent'/'optional'). credentials.store(new PasswordCredential(form)) offers to save, and preventSilentAccess() turns auto sign-in off. wubble has its own vault and autofill (wubble_core::autofill, crates/wubble/src/host/autofill.rs, wubble-helper/src/autofill.js), but these calls resolve null, because Chromium's password manager is not wired to CEF.
Build: (1) Add a password-only path to the content script, or a sibling channel `credentials`. It wraps credentials.get/store/preventSilentAccess when `password` is asked, and leaves publicKey and federated requests alone. (2) On the browser side, answer get from the vault entries for the frame's real origin, using the same matching rules autofill uses. With more than one entry, or mediation 'required', show the existing key menu or a kit account chooser. Silent and optional mediation auto sign in only if the user has not called preventSilentAccess for that origin (a per-origin flag stored with the vault). store() goes to the existing save prompt. (3) Agent sessions follow decisions.md "Agent secrets bind on the sheet": no credentials are handed to an agent tab except bound secrets. (4) Unit-test the pure decision (entries, mediation, silent flag → answer, chooser or null) in wubble-core autofill.

title: Retry and Save As from the originating tab with its referrer
spec:
TODO.md: "Downloads: Retry restarts from any tab of the download's container, not the tab it came from (a login-gated file can come back as a sign-in page)". Chrome retries with the original request's referrer and site context. wubble's host/downloads.rs `apply_download` StartAgain calls `view_for_download(container)`, which takes the shown tab or any live tab of the container. It then runs `View::start_download(&url)`, which sends no referrer.

What to build: (1) DownloadEntry (wubble-core/src/download.rs) gains `tab: Option<TabId>` (the tab that started it) and `referrer: String` (the page's committed URL when it started), stored through a migration in crates/wubble-store/sql and wubble-store/src/downloads.rs. (2) Core: a pure `fn retry_view(entry, live: &[(TabId, ContainerId, agent: bool)], shown) -> Option<TabId>` that prefers the origin tab, then a tab of the same container on the referrer's site, then any tab of the container, never an agent-driven tab. Unit tests. (3) Engine: `View::start_download_with_referrer(url, referrer)`. CEF's StartDownload has no referrer, so use a CefURLRequest-free road: DevTools `Page.navigate` of a hidden frame is wrong, so use `Network.setExtraHTTPHeaders` around the start, or `Browser.setDownloadBehavior` plus `Runtime.evaluate` of an `<a download>` click in the origin page, which carries the page's referrer policy. Choose the one that keeps cookies in the container. (4) A retried download keeps its list position, as Chrome does, instead of appearing as a new top row. All platforms.

title: macOS platform passkeys (iCloud Keychain) via AuthenticationServices
spec: Chrome on macOS creates and uses passkeys stored in iCloud Keychain (and Chrome's own profile passkeys). Plug a platform authenticator into the `webauthn-security-keys` trait using public API only: `ASAuthorizationPlatformPublicKeyCredentialProvider` with `ASPublicKeyCredentialClientData` (macOS 13.5+, browser variant that takes the origin, per docs/research/apple-passwords.md section 3), via objc2-authentication-services, driven from the main thread with `ASAuthorizationController` and a presentation anchor of wubble's NSWindow (crates/wubble/src/mac_app.rs-adjacent code in crates/wubble-engine/src/mac_app.rs). Registration and assertion map the shim's options to `createCredentialRegistrationRequest`/`createCredentialAssertionRequest` with clientData built from the frame's real origin; conditional mediation uses `performAutoFillAssistedRequests` where available, surfaced as rows in the autofill dropdown ("Passkey for <site>"). Needs the `com.apple.developer.web-browser.public-key-credential` entitlement and a Developer ID provisioning profile (owner files the request; TODO "Apple Passwords / passkeys entitlement request"): add the entitlement plist entry and the bundling step (docs/macos.md app bundle) behind a build feature `mac-passkeys`, and fail closed (falls back to security keys only) when the entitlement is missing at runtime. `isUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable` answers true only then. Setting row under the Autofill and passwords section. macOS only.

title: Extensions: allow per container and in agent sessions (Chrome's 'Allow in Incognito')
spec: Chrome loads extensions in incognito only when the user ticks "Allow in Incognito" on the details page (`util::SetIsIncognitoEnabled`). wubble has no private windows. Its isolated contexts are containers, including the ones agent sessions create, and every extension loads in every container (decision "Extensions on"). So a password manager or content script runs inside agent-session tabs too. To build, as the analogue: (1) Core: `Extension` gains `containers: ContainerAccess { All, DefaultOnly, Listed(Vec<ContainerId>) }`, plus `in_agent_sessions: bool` (default false, as Chrome's incognito default is off). Serialise both in `to_json`/`from_json`. A pure `extensions::enabled_in(ext, container, is_agent) -> bool` gets tests. (2) Engine: patch (extends ext-live-management's table) `set_enabled_in_profile(profile_path, ext_id, bool)`, implemented with `ExtensionRegistrar::DisableExtension` and a wubble disable reason on that profile only. wubble calls it when a container's request context is created (`wubble-engine/src/app.rs`, where containers get their profile path) and when the setting changes. Without the patch, an agent container's request context could be made with `--disable-extensions`-equivalent... it cannot, so without the patch the toggle is hidden (`ext_api::available()`). (3) Projection: `extensions/projection.rs::project` leaves out tabs of containers where the extension is off. (4) UI: on each Settings extension row, a kit toggle "Allow in agent sessions" and a kit select "Containers".

title: Updater: roll back a build that cannot even load
spec: TODO.md M7 "Release gaps: ... rollback misses a build that cannot load". The rollback in `wubble_core::update::install` (`on_start`, `LaunchRecord`, `on_healthy`) runs inside the new `wubble` binary (`updater::on_launch` in `main.rs` `browse`). If that binary cannot start at all (a missing or incompatible `libcef.so` through RUNPATH, a dyld failure in the app, a bad CPU feature), it never runs its own rollback, and the user is stuck. To build: a launcher that does not link CEF. On Linux, `~/.local/bin/wubble` and the desktop entry's `Exec` point at a tiny `wubble-launch` (a new small crate, or a mode of the release tool that links nothing heavy) placed in `<data>/wubble/`. It reads `updates/launch.json`, execs `current/wubble` with the same args, and if the child exits within a few seconds with a loader failure (exit 127, a signal before `on_launch` wrote its start mark) while a trial is open, it applies `on_switch_failed`/`RollBack` itself (switch `current`, mark the version bad) and execs the previous one. The trial rule stays in `wubble_core::update::install` as pure functions with tests; add a `LoaderFailed` event. On macOS the app bundle's main executable is the stub: either a launcher binary in `Contents/MacOS` that loads the real one, or `Contents/Helpers`. Make the bundling change in `wubble-bundle` and `package-macos.sh`. `install.sh` and `package-linux.sh` install the launcher. Docs: docs/release.md "Updating and rollback".

title: Live text in images: Vision backend on macOS, PP-OCR over ONNX Runtime on Linux and Windows
spec: TODO line 57, docs/research/ocr.md section 5. Implement the `OcrBackend` trait (from `ocr-pipeline-text-layer`) twice, in a new crate (for example `crates/wubble-ocr`, or a `wubble-ocr` helper process for crash isolation, as the research recommends). macOS: Apple Vision (`VNRecognizeTextRequest`, accurate level, languages from `supportedRecognitionLanguages`) through objc2-vision, returning line text and quads. Linux and Windows: PP-OCRv5 mobile detection, angle classifier and recognition over ONNX Runtime (`ort` crate, MIT/Apache). Either use oar-ocr after confirming its licence, or write a small in-repo pipeline (resize, DB post-processing, CTC decode). Bundle the models (about 25-30 MB) in the release packaging scripts (`scripts/release/`), with a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry per model traced to Paddle's Apache-2.0 release. Keep `auto-download` features off. Run on a low-priority 1-2 thread pool. Windows: the same ONNX backend.

title: Blocker scriptlets run at document start
spec:
uBO injects scriptlets (`##+js(...)`) at document_start, before any page script runs. In wubble the frame's `cosmetic.js` sends `hello` when its context is created; the browser answers, and only then runs the scriptlets with `run_script_in` (crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs `answer_cosmetic`, around line 1099). By then the page's own scripts have often run, so many scriptlets (set-constant, abort-on-property-read, json-prune, no-fetch-if) come too late. That is the "uBO scriptlet coverage" gap.

To build: when a view's main frame is about to navigate (`OnBeforeBrowse`/nav commit start in crates/wubble-engine/src/nav.rs or view.rs), ask the filter for the target URL's scriptlets (`filter.frame_cosmetic(top, url).script`, which comes from `Cosmetic::scriptlets` in crates/wubble-blocker/src/blocker.rs). Register them through the view's DevTools channel with `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` (with `runImmediately` where supported), and remove the previous identifier with `Page.removeScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`. Same-site subframes are covered by the same registration. For cross-site subframes, keep the current hello path as a fallback, and skip it when the document-start copy has already run (the scriptlet wrapper sets a guard global inside its closure scope, in the page world). Respect per-site off (`SiteOverrides`) and agent tabs. Add a page fixture to the block smoke with a set-constant rule that is checked by an inline script running before load. All platforms.

title: Experiments (flags-like) section: user-chosen Chromium features and switches
spec:
chrome://flags lets the user turn Chromium features on and off and asks for a relaunch. CEF does not serve a working flags page for wubble's browsers. wubble builds its command line from one table, PageFeatures::knobs in crates/wubble-engine/src/app.rs (Knob::Enable, Disable, Switch, merged into a single enable-features and disable-features).

1. Add a curated data table in wubble-core (new experiments.rs): id, Chromium feature or switch, description, platforms, default, and whether it needs a relaunch. Start with entries that prebuilt CEF 156 honours and that users ask for: ElasticOverscroll, SmoothScrolling (disable-smooth-scrolling), ParallelDownloading, OverlayScrollbar, ForceDarkMode for web contents (careful: wubble has page themes), WebGPU on Linux (enable-unsafe-webgpu), Vulkan, ignore-gpu-blocklist, enable-features=BackForwardCache variants. Check each name is a string in libcef, as the existing knobs comment does.
2. Add settings `experiments.enabled` (list of ids) and `experiments.custom` (a list-editor of raw `--switch[=value]` and `+Feature` or `-Feature` entries, validated by a pure fn that refuses switches wubble owns: remote-debugging, user-data-dir, the sandbox ones).
3. In app.rs, merge them into the one enable/disable list and the switches, with the table's knobs winning over a conflicting user entry, and log what was applied.
4. Settings section 'Experiments' at wubble://flags (alias chrome://flags), built from settings::ALL rows with toggles and a relaunch toast. Off by default, and a 'Reset all' button.

Unit tests for validation and merging.

title: Windows: precision touchpad pinch-zoom and history swipe
spec: Chrome on Windows uses DirectManipulation for precision touchpads. A pinch zooms the visual viewport smoothly (not page-zoom steps), and a two-finger horizontal overscroll navigates back or forward with the arrow bubble. In wubble on Windows, winit has no `PinchGesture`, and a precision touchpad pinch arrives as Ctrl+wheel. `zoom.js` and the engine pinch code treat it as a page-zoom step (`Action::ZoomIn/Out`) or a Touch-road pinch per wheel, and no history swipe is reported (host/gesture.rs). To build: in the Windows `Aux` worker (crates/wubble/src/wl/windows.rs, shared with win-ole-dnd; one owner), create a DirectManipulation manager and viewport per HWND as Chromium's `ui/base/win/direct_manipulation` / `content/browser/renderer_host/direct_manipulation_helper_win.cc` does (BSD-3, notice entry). Feed pointer hit-test contacts (`DM_POINTERHITTEST`) into it, and map viewport transform updates to `AuxEvent::Pinch(PinchInput)` (scale) and to `AuxEvent::Swipe` (horizontal pan with the page not consuming it), with the end on the ready state. Ctrl+wheel from a real mouse keeps the page-zoom step. A pure translation from DM transform deltas to gesture inputs goes in wubble-core with tests. Use the `windows` crate (MIT/Apache).

title: HTTPS-First and HTTPS-Only mode
spec:
Chrome's "Always use secure connections" setting tries https for every http navigation. If https fails, it shows an interstitial ("Connection is not secure" … "Continue to site") and remembers the choice per site for a while. Chrome also upgrades automatically with a silent fallback (HTTPS-Upgrades). wubble only upgrades typed scheme-less public hosts (decision "Typed local addresses") and has no mode.

Build:
- Add a setting `privacy.https_mode`: off|upgrade|only. The default is "upgrade", to match Chrome's automatic upgrades; it makes no new request to a new party. Put it in crates/wubble-core/src/settings.rs.
- Add a pure module `wubble_core::https`: `plan(url, mode, exempt) -> Upgrade|Keep` (exempt: IP literals, localhost, single labels, .local, non-default ports, the per-container allow list) and a lifecycle enum per navigation (Upgraded → Loaded | Failed → Fallback or Warn) with `transition`. Unit-test it.
- Engine path: main-frame Document requests go through the request filter (crates/wubble-engine/src/filter.rs `RequestAction::Redirect`). The host's ContentFilter (crates/wubble/src/blocking.rs) consults an Arc snapshot of the mode and the allow list and redirects http→https, recording the upgrade per browser_id.
- On a load or certificate error of an upgraded navigation: in upgrade mode, reload the http URL marked exempt for that navigation. In only mode, show a new `PageError::HttpsOnly { url }` in crates/wubble/src/page_error.rs with "Go back" and "Continue to site". Continue adds the host to the container's allow list (session plus 15 days, as Chrome does) and loads http.
- Set Chromium's own prefs `https_only_mode_enabled`/`https_upgrades` false so the two do not both act.

title: Keyboard Lock in fullscreen: system keys reach the page, hold Esc to exit
spec:
In Chrome, navigator.keyboard.lock() in fullscreen gives the page keys the browser would otherwise take (Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, Alt+Tab where the OS allows, Esc). The fullscreen bubble then says "Press and hold Esc to exit full screen" and names the site. Content's default RequestKeyboardLock accepts the lock, but wubble's shell still handles its own chords first (crates/wubble/src/input.rs routes, keys.rs), and the fullscreen hint is a generic toast (crates/wubble/src/screen.rs ScreenEffect::Hint, host/surfaces.rs "Press Esc to exit full screen").
Build: (1) Add a main-world content-script channel `kbdlock` (wubble-helper/src) that reports navigator.keyboard.lock(keys) and unlock() to the browser. (2) Add the lock to the pure fullscreen machine in crates/wubble/src/screen.rs: state Locked{keys} while the page is fullscreen and locked. Input routing then sends the shell's page-first and shell chords to the page, except the OS-reserved ones. Esc goes to the page, and a hold of 2 s (Chrome's kHoldEscapeTime is 2 s) leaves fullscreen. Unit-test the transitions. (3) Change the hint text: "Press and hold Esc to exit full screen" while locked, "<site> is now full screen" plus the Esc line, as Chrome's ExclusiveAccessBubble does, from the existing toast. (4) Ask for the KeyboardLock site permission (it already exists in site.rs) when the page locks outside a gesture, as Chrome does.

title: Media Session API and OS controls: seek, position, raise, active session
spec:
In Chrome, MPRIS, Now Playing and SMTC show a position bar and accept seeks. The action handlers seekbackward, seekforward, seekto, skipad, togglemicrophone, togglecamera and hangup are honoured, Raise focuses the tab, and the active session is the one that most recently started playing; a paused session stays controllable. In wubble, crates/wubble/src/media_keys.rs and kit.js have only play, pause, toggle, next, previous and stop. MediaKey::of drops souvlaki's Seek, SeekBy, SetPosition, Raise and SetVolume. kit.js does not wrap `navigator.mediaSession.setPositionState` or `playbackState`. Keys::show passes `progress: None` and `duration: None`. `key_target` in host/videos.rs takes the first audible tab in map order and loses a paused session. Windows gets `hwnd: None`, so souvlaki refuses and the keys are off.

What to build: (1) kit.js: wrap setPositionState and playbackState, report them in `meta` (duration, position, rate, state), and extend `act(action, details)` with seek actions (seekTime, seekOffset) that fall back to the video element. (2) Move the active-session choice into a pure machine in a new wubble-core/src/mediasession.rs: an enum of sessions per tab, events (started playing, paused, closed, user pressed) and the chosen tab, with unit tests. (3) media_keys.rs: map Seek, SeekBy, SetPosition and Raise. Raise focuses the tab's window and tab. Pass MediaPosition and the duration, and pick the artwork size closest to 256 px. (4) Windows: pass the main window's HWND from winit. (5) Media in an iframe: the poll asks each same-origin frame's kit through `View::run_script_in`.

title: Windows Hello passkeys via webauthn.dll
spec: Chrome on Windows hands WebAuthn to the OS (`webauthn.dll`, Windows Hello, synced passkeys, security keys, phones) through `device/fido/win`. Add a Windows platform authenticator behind the `webauthn-security-keys` trait: load `webauthn.dll` dynamically, check `WebAuthNGetApiVersionNumber`, call `WebAuthNAuthenticatorMakeCredential`/`WebAuthNAuthenticatorGetAssertion` with the top-level HWND of wubble's window and client data built from the frame's real origin, map options and results (windows-sys bindings; Chromium's `device/fido/win/webauthn_api.cc` as reference, BSD-3, credited). When the OS API is version 1+ prefer it for all transports (it shows Windows' own dialog, so wubble's sheet is skipped), else fall back to authenticator-rs. `isUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable` from `WebAuthNIsUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable`. Cancel through `WebAuthNCancelCurrentOperation` when the tab navigates or closes. Code lives in a windows-only module of crates/wubble (or crates/wubble-engine if it needs the CEF window handle). Windows only, CI-built; keep it compiling on Linux/macOS via cfg.

title: Chrome Web Store install and updates, behind an off-by-default setting
spec: Chrome installs from chromewebstore.google.com ("Add to Chrome" through `chrome.webstorePrivate`) and checks the update URL every few hours. wubble installs only from the user's files, with no Web Store and no updates (decisions "Extension install" and "Extension updates"; TODO M6 "install from the Web Store"). To build, all behind a new Bool setting `extensions.web_store` (default 0, `Section::Privacy`, label stating it contacts Google): (1) On chromewebstore.google.com pages, a document script (`View::set_document_scripts`) defines a `chrome.webstorePrivate` shim, ported from samuelmaddock/electron-browser-shell `electron-chrome-web-store` (MIT, with a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry): `beginInstallWithManifest3`, `completeInstall`, `getExtensionStatus` and `isInIncognitoMode` answered from wubble's list. It posts to the host through a `Runtime.addBinding` binding. (2) The host downloads `https://clients2.google.com/service/update2/crx?response=redirect&prodversion=156.0.8078.96&acceptformat=crx3&x=id%3D<id>%26uc` through `crates/wubble-engine/src/fetch.rs`. Check that `host-resolver-rules` in `engine/app.rs` does not block the hosts used; `*.gvt1.com` is blocked, so either follow the redirect via an allowed mirror or add a narrow exception only while the setting is on. Then install through the existing .crx path (`engine/extensions.rs`, `parse_crx`), showing the existing install prompt. (3) Verify the CRX3 signature for store installs: RSA-SHA256 over the signed header data, with `crx_id` matching the key, ported from Chromium `components/crx_file/crx_verifier.cc` (BSD), using an MIT/Apache RSA crate. (4) Updates: a pure `extensions::update` state machine (Idle, Checking, Downloading, Ready) driving a daily omaha `update2/crx` check for store-sourced entries. A new `Source::WebStore` keeps the update URL. Tests for the shim's answers and the update machine.

title: Linux system packages: .deb, .rpm and an AUR PKGBUILD with the setuid sandbox
spec: Chrome ships .deb and .rpm. They install to /opt with `chrome-sandbox` setuid root, so the sandbox works on Ubuntu 23.10+ where `apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns` blocks user namespaces. wubble ships only a tarball through `install.sh` (no sudo), and TODO.md M7 lists "Ubuntu's user-namespace limit vs the no-sudo sandbox" (the warning is `linux_sandbox_warning` in `wubble-engine/src/app.rs`). To build: `scripts/release/package-linux-system.sh`, which takes the bundle `package-linux.sh` makes (`dist/wubble-<V>-linux-x86_64.tar.xz`) and produces (1) a .deb (with `dpkg-deb`, a `DEBIAN/control` with the CEF runtime's library dependencies, which `dpkg-shlibdeps` can compute) and (2) an .rpm (a `.spec` in `scripts/release/linux/`, `rpmbuild -bb`). Both install `/opt/wubble/`, `/usr/bin/wubble` as a link, the desktop entry and the hicolor icons, `chrome-sandbox` as root:root 4755 (postinst/%post), and an AppArmor profile `/etc/apparmor.d/wubble` allowing `userns` (Chrome's own) loaded in postinst when AppArmor is present. (3) `scripts/release/linux/PKGBUILD` for the AUR, from the same tarball and sha256. A system-package install has no `release.json` in the managed layout, so `updater/install.rs` `classify` reports `InstallKind::Elsewhere` and Settings shows updates as managed elsewhere. Check that the wording fits a package manager. Add a section to docs/release.md, and run shellcheck by hand.

title: MCP tools inside frames: flattened DevTools sessions for out-of-process frames, live layout for same-process frames
spec: TODO lines 62, 71 and 72. In `crates/wubble/src/host/agent.rs`, `agent_act` uses DOM (`DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded`, `DOM.getContentQuads` by backendNodeId) only for the top document (`top`). A frame's element is placed from the accessibility mirror's boxes, which a scroll leaves stale. `type`'s focus check (`focus_script`) runs in the top document only. `upload_file` cannot reach a cross-site frame's input or chooser. Fix all three on one shared base. (1) In `crates/wubble-engine/src/cdp.rs` and `view.rs`, add `Target.setAutoAttach {autoAttach:true, waitForDebuggerOnStart:false, flatten:true}` on agent-driven views. Track `Target.attachedToTarget` and `detachedFromTarget` (pure bookkeeping: frame id or AX tree id to sessionId), and add `View::cdp_in(session, method, params)` that adds `sessionId` to the message. Map an AX tree (wubble_ax `TreeId`) to its frame's session. (2) A same-process frame's AX id is its backend node id: use the DOM path through the top session. An OOPIF uses its own session, and its quads are offset by the frame's box in the parent (`DOM.getBoxModel` of the iframe element). (3) Run the `type` focus check through `Runtime.evaluate` in the frame's session (or its execution context id from `Runtime.executionContextCreated`), and walk `document.activeElement` through open shadow roots; a closed shadow host no longer counts as editable. (4) For `upload_file`, enable `Page.setInterceptFileChooserDialog` and `DOM.setFileInputFiles` in the frame's session. Update the tool texts in `crates/wubble-mcp/src/tools.rs`.

title: Resolve __MSG_ names from extension _locales
spec:
Chrome shows an extension's localised name, description and action title: `__MSG_key__` placeholders in manifest.json are resolved from `_locales/<locale>/messages.json` (default_locale, then the UI locale with region fallback, keys case-insensitive). wubble shows them raw in the install prompt, the extension list and the footer popover (crates/wubble-core/src/extensions.rs:130 "a `__MSG_name__` placeholder is shown raw for now"; research/extensions.md "Acceptance", gap 1).

To build: a pure resolver in wubble-core (crates/wubble-core/src/extensions.rs or a new `extensions/locale.rs`): `fn resolve(text, messages: &Messages) -> String`, with `Messages::parse(json)` that follows Chromium's `extension_l10n_util` rules (an idea port of extensions/common/message_bundle.cc, BSD: case-insensitive keys, `$placeholder$` substitution from each message's `placeholders`, `$$` escape, unknown keys left as written). Add locale choice `fn pick(available, ui_locale, default_locale)` with fallback from `en_US` to `en`, then to default_locale. The I/O sits in crates/wubble/src/extensions.rs, where manifests are read at install and at start: read the chosen messages.json files (size-capped) and store the resolved name, description and `action.default_title` in `Installed`. Re-resolve when the OS locale changes at the next start. Unit tests with the Bitwarden manifest shapes. All platforms.

title: Reading list: save for later, read and unread, page and sidebar access
spec:
Chrome's reading list is a separate list from bookmarks. You add to it with 'Add to reading list' on the bookmark star, the tab context menu or the link context menu. It has 'Unread' and 'Read' sections, an item becomes read when you open it to the end or mark it, and items can be deleted. It lives in the side panel. wubble has nothing like it.

1. Store: migration crates/wubble-store/sql/017_reading_list.sql with `reading_list(id, url UNIQUE, title, added_ms, read_ms NULL)` and fns add, list, mark_read, mark_unread, delete and clear_read in a new wubble-store/src/reading.rs.
2. Core: InternalPage::ReadingList (wubble://reading-list, title 'Reading list') with a PageLink row, and a pure view fn in pages.rs that splits Unread and Read, sorts newest first and filters by query. Add Action::AddToReadingList and Action::OpenReadingList (FIXED table, PALETTE, keywords 'read later').
3. Marking read: when a reading-list URL commits in a tab, mark it read, as Chrome does on open. Do this in host/pages.rs, keyed by wubble_core::url::url_key.
4. UI: a list page from kit/pages (list-card, list-row, list-field) like History, with per-row Open, Mark read or unread and Delete. Add 'Add to reading list' rows in the tab row menu (wubble_core::tabmenu::ROWS), the link context menu (crates/wubble/src/menu.rs, group 1) and the bookmark sheet.
5. The command bar ranks reading-list items as candidates with Kind::Bookmark and subtitle 'Reading list'.

Import and export with bookmarks HTML is not needed. Unit tests for the view fn.

title: Secure DNS (DNS-over-HTTPS) setting
spec:
Chrome Settings > Security > "Use secure DNS" offers Off, "With your current service provider" (automatic upgrade), or a chosen provider (Cloudflare, Google, Quad9, CleanBrowsing, NextDNS, OpenDNS, …) or a custom template. wubble has no row, and Chromium's default (automatic) applies silently.

Build:
- Add a setting `privacy.secure_dns`: automatic|off|provider:<id>|custom:<template>. The default is automatic, matching Chromium's default (decision "Network stack: Chromium's defaults stay"); choosing a provider is the user's own act.
- wubble-core: a provider table ported from Chromium `net/dns/public/doh_provider_entry.cc` (BSD-3-Clause, with a source comment and a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md entry), with id, display name, template and privacy-policy link. Add `fn validate_template(s)` (https, parses as a URI template with `{?dns}` or a POST form, like Chromium's `dns_over_https_config`) and `fn prefs(setting) -> (mode: &str, templates: String)`. Unit-test it.
- Engine: these are local-state (global) prefs. Apply `dns_over_https.mode` ("off"/"automatic"/"secure") and `dns_over_https.templates` with `cef::preference_manager_get_global()` and `set_preference` after CEF starts and on change. Add `Engine::set_global_pref` in crates/wubble-engine/src/app.rs.
- UI: a Settings Privacy row with a select and a custom-template field (the kit select and input that already exist for settings rows), with an error text when invalid.
- net_audit.rs smokes must allow the chosen provider's host only when it is set; only note this, write no test.

title: EyeDropper API and the colour picker's eyedropper
spec:
In Chrome, new EyeDropper().open() (and the eyedropper button in the <input type=color> picker) lets the user pick a pixel from the screen and resolves {sRGBHex}. WebContentsDelegate::OpenEyeDropper defaults to nullptr, and AlloyBrowserHostImpl does not override it, so in wubble the promise rejects at once.
Build in the repo: (1) Add a main-world content-script channel `eyedropper` (wubble-helper/src) that replaces window.EyeDropper with a spec-shaped class. open({signal}) needs transient activation, sends a request to the browser, and resolves or rejects with AbortError on Esc or abort. (2) On the browser side, a pure machine (one enum and a transition, answered once). While it is open, the shell shows a magnifier loupe that follows the pointer over the window, built from kit parts (a derived piece; it goes on the owner's sheet because it may need a new primitive). It samples the colour from a one-off GPU-to-CPU copy of the window's current frame: one readback per pick, not a frame-path readback. A click resolves the hex, Esc cancels. (3) The sampling area is wubble's own window only (the whole screen would need OS capture). Say so in the code. (4) The colour popup's eyedropper button calls the same API, so it works once the shim exists.

title: Global media controls (Chrome's media hub)
spec:
While any tab has a media session, Chrome's toolbar shows a media button. Its dialog lists every playing or paused session across tabs, each with artwork, title, artist and source site, play/pause, previous/next (when the page has handlers), a seek bar with times, a Picture-in-picture button and a click that jumps to the tab. wubble has none: media keys act on one target tab, and the only per-tab media UI is the rail's sound badge (wubble_core::tabmarks) and the video strip.

What to build: (1) Core: a list model in the new or existing media-session module (wubble-core), `fn hub_rows(sessions, tabs) -> Vec<HubRow>`, from the kit's `meta` snapshots that host/videos.rs already polls. Poll paused-session tabs too, at the existing poll's rate, never more. Unit tests. (2) UI: a footer button in kit/chrome/side-bottom.slint, shown while there are sessions, opening a popover like downloads-popover.slint. Build it from kit parts: APopover, menu rows, IconButton, the video strip's seek track (video-controls.slint), and artwork as an image fetched by CEF's DownloadImage the way favicons are (decisions.md "Favicons": no HTTP client in wubble). The design has no media hub: it is a derived piece for docs/fidelity/derived-review.md, built only from existing primitives. (3) Host: route row actions to `kit.act` / `kit.cmd` in the right tab, PiP through the pip machine, and the jump through the model's focus command. (4) Gallery scene for the shot set. All platforms.

title: Apple Passwords passthrough (macOS helper protocol client)
spec: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Arc get iCloud Keychain logins through Apple's `PasswordManagerBrowserExtensionHelper` (native messaging, `com.apple.passwordmanager`). docs/research/apple-passwords.md (sections 0, 4.4, 4.6) recommends wubble speak that protocol directly from the main process, off by default. Build: (1) pure protocol crate code (a new module, e.g. crates/wubble/src/apple_passwords/ or a small crate) porting au2001/icloudkeys (Apache-2.0, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md): SRP-6a 3072-bit pairing with the 6-digit code, AES-GCM session, JSON commands `GET_CAPABILITIES` (require secretSessionVersion 1, else fail closed), `GET_LOGIN_NAMES_FOR_URL`, `GET_PASSWORD_FOR_LOGIN_NAME`, `GET_ONE_TIME_CODES`, `SET_PASSWORD_FOR_LOGIN_NAME_AND_URL`, `LAUNCH_PASSWORDS_APP`, behind a trait with a fake for tests. (2) State machine in wubble-core: `Unpaired -> Pairing{code} -> Ready -> Querying -> Picked`, plus `HelperUnavailable`, `Denied`, `SessionLost`, pure `transition` with unit tests. (3) Host: spawn the helper only when the user opens the key menu with the setting on; rows "From Apple Passwords" in the autofill dropdown (crates/wubble-core/src/autofill.rs `MenuRow::External`), fill through the existing fill path, bound to the frame's exact https origin; verification codes on one-time-code fields (`FieldClass::OneTimeCode`); save prompt gets a destination choice. (4) A pairing-code sheet (kit). Setting `passwords.apple_passwords` default off, macOS only. Requires the entitlement or an allow-list entry to run; code ships regardless.

title: Extensions: keyboard shortcuts (chrome.commands) and the shortcuts page
spec: Chrome reads manifest `commands` (`suggested_key` per platform, `_execute_action`, named commands, `global`). chrome://extensions/shortcuts lets the user set or clear each one, a chord fires `commands.onCommand(name, tab)`, and `_execute_action` opens the action popup. wubble has none. Core (pure, tested): `parse_manifest` reads `commands` into `Vec<ExtCommand { name, description, suggested: Option<Chord> }>`, with chord syntax per Chromium `extensions/common/command.cc` (`ParseImpl`: Ctrl/Alt/Shift/Command/MacCtrl plus a key; at most 4 suggested per extension; Ctrl+Alt refused). Bindings live in the keymap. `wubble_core::keys` gets a binding target `Target::Extension { id, command }` alongside `Action`, so conflicts with shell chords are detected by the existing conflict rules and shown in the shortcut editor. Engine patch `55-cef-ext-commands.patch`: table function `command_fire(extension_id, command_name, browser_id)`, which dispatches `commands.onCommand` through `extensions::EventRouter::DispatchEventToExtension`, with the tab object from the wubble registry. It also grants activeTab as `ExtensionKeybindingRegistry::ExecuteCommand` does. A second function `commands_updated(extension_id, json)` lets `commands.getAll` return wubble's bindings (via `CommandService` prefs). `_execute_action` needs no patch: it uses the existing `host/ext_ui.rs::extension_pressed`. `_execute_side_panel` goes to the side-panel feature. Host: the key path (`crates/wubble/src/input.rs`/`bind.rs`) resolves extension targets PageFirst. UI: a "Keyboard shortcuts" block in the Settings extensions section, reusing the shortcut editor's kit rows.

title: Flatpak package with zypak
spec: TODO.md M7 "Packaging: Flatpak/RPM". Chromium-based browsers on Flathub (Chrome, Brave, Chromium) run Chromium's sandbox inside Flatpak through zypak (BSD-3-Clause), which redirects the zygote's namespace sandbox to `flatpak-spawn --sandbox`. wubble has no manifest. To build: `scripts/release/flatpak/cc.wubble.Browser.yml` (choose the app id with the owner; the desktop entry and icons have to be renamed to it in the bundle), on `org.freedesktop.Platform` 24.08 with the `org.freedesktop.Platform.ffmpeg-full`-free path, wubble's own `wubble-ffmpeg` being in the bundle. Module `zypak` from its tag. A module that installs the release tarball (`dist/wubble-<V>-linux-x86_64.tar.xz` plus sha256) into `/app/wubble`, and a wrapper `/app/bin/wubble` running `zypak-wrapper /app/wubble/wubble "$@"`. finish-args: wayland, fallback-x11, pulseaudio, dri, network, `xdg-download`, `--talk-name=org.freedesktop.portal.*`, `org.freedesktop.secrets` (the password keyring), `org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.wubble` own-name (media_keys.rs `dbus_name`), `org.freedesktop.Notifications`. In code: detect Flatpak (`/.flatpak-info`) in a pure helper in `wubble-core`. Under Flatpak the updater is managed elsewhere (`updater/install.rs` `classify`), "Make default" is unsupported (default-browser feature), downloads go through the portal-visible folder, and the MCP manifest/socket root is `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/app/<id>`, so `instance::private_root` and agent harness paths have to account for it (the relay runs outside the sandbox). Add a docs/release.md section.

title: Accessibility mirror: correct boxes after the page scrolls (screen-reader pane and MCP)
spec: TODO line 62, second half. `wubble_ax` (crates/wubble-ax/src/lib.rs ~357) offsets a node's bounds by each container's `scrollX`/`scrollY`. Chromium sends no root scroll offset in the location-change events CEF passes, so after a page scroll the mirror's boxes are wrong for the screen-reader pane (`crates/wubble/src/host/ax.rs`, `render_ax`, `ax_action`) and for anything placed from them. Fix: keep the root document's (and each frame document's) scroll offset in the `PageTree`, from a cheap source. Use DevTools `Page.getLayoutMetrics` (`cssVisualViewport.pageX/pageY`) asked through `View::cdp` after a wheel, a scroll action or a `scroll` event. Or have the helper's probe script report `scrollX/scrollY` on a passive scroll listener, throttled to a frame, as a frame message. Apply it in `PageTree::flatten`/`viewport` (crates/wubble-ax/src/flat.rs) so `reach` and the item views use live positions. Keep wubble-ax pure: the offset comes in as data (`PageTree::set_scroll(tree, x, y)`). Add unit tests in crates/wubble-ax/src/tests.rs for pure logic only.

title: Port the remaining touch-kit pieces: pin, download button, dock, checkbox mask
spec:
The design's touch kit (`~/Dev/wubble-wt/ref/the-wallpaper-project/src/wubble/pages/touch.tsx`: `Pin` at about line 257, `Download` at 316, `Dock` at 377 with its gliding tooltip, `Checks` at 555 with the check box's mask grow; styles in touch.css) has pieces that the kit does not have yet (crates/wubble-ui/ui/kit/controls has check-box.slint without the mask grow, and no pin, download button or dock).

To build: `git pull` the design clone first. Port each piece into crates/wubble-ui/ui/kit/controls/ as its own file headed `// design: pages/touch.tsx:<lines> @<commit>` (and touch.css lines). Take the values from the generated `ui/kit/gen/*.slint` and `wubble_core::kit_gen` by rerunning `node tools/fidelity/extract.mjs` if new tokens appear. Put each loop's physics in `wubble_core::controls` (the existing registry pattern, decisions "Component physics"), with unit tests. The pieces: Pin (the pin toggle's press and settle), Download (the progress ring, done check and bounce), Dock (an icon row with the tooltip gliding between hovered icons on a spring), and the check box's mask-grow fill. Then use them: Pin in the tab row's pin affordance (kit chrome/tab-row.slint), Download as the sidebar footer's downloads button with live progress from host/downloads.rs, the check box wherever check-box.slint is used. Dock goes in the gallery only unless a shell place is decided. Add gallery scenes (crates/wubble/src/gallery_smoke.rs) and keep the kit lock passing. All platforms.

title: Bookmarks bar
spec:
Chrome's bookmarks bar is a strip under the toolbar. It shows the 'Bookmarks bar' folder's items as chips with favicons, with folders as drop-down menus and an overflow chevron. Mod+Shift+B toggles it, it shows on the new-tab page by default, items can be dragged in, out and around, and right-clicking a chip gives Open, Edit and Delete. wubble has no bookmarks bar (TODO M2 'Bookmarks: drag reorder, a bookmarks bar'), and no top toolbar by decision ('Layout'). Bookmarks have a single root (crates/wubble-store sql 001 bookmarks.parent_id NULL).
