1. Store and core: a special root folder, 'Bookmarks bar' (a well-known folder created on migration, its id in settings). Chrome HTML and profile imports map their bar folder to it. pages::bookmark_tree shows it first.
2. Setting `ui.bookmarks_bar`: Never, New tab only (default) or Always. Action::ToggleBookmarksBar bound to Mod+Shift+B in keys.rs.
3. Placement: the decision rules out a toolbar, so the bar is a slim strip across the top of the content area, above the page card and split-aware. Compose it from kit chrome parts (favs chips, menu for folders, the overflow as a menu) and mark it `// derived:` on docs/fidelity/derived-review.md. The owner must approve the look before merge.
4. A folder chip opens a Menu::Shell of its children (crates/wubble/src/menu.rs), nested. Chips take drops of links and tabs, through the drag machine in wubble_core::drag and dnd and the bookmark-drop path in the 'Drops onto the shell's pages' decision. The page area shrinks by the strip's height (host/panes.rs).

Unit tests for the overflow fit and the visibility rule.

title: Privacy preferences table: Do Not Track, preload pages, ad privacy, WebRTC IP
spec:
Chrome's privacy settings are profile prefs: "Send a Do Not Track request" (`enable_do_not_track`, off by default), "Preload pages" (`net.network_prediction_options`), "Allow sites to check if you have payment methods saved" (`payments.can_make_payment_enabled`), the Ad privacy toggles (`privacy_sandbox.m1.topics_enabled`, `privacy_sandbox.m1.fledge_enabled`, `privacy_sandbox.m1.ad_measurement_enabled`), and the WebRTC IP handling policy (`webrtc.ip_handling_policy`, with no UI in Chrome; Brave exposes it). wubble sets one pref only (`webkit.webprefs.minimum_font_size`, crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs:848) and exposes none of these.

Build:
- wubble-core: a data table `privacy::PREFS: &[(setting key, chromium pref, Value mapping)]` with matching SettingDefs in settings.rs (Section::Privacy). Defaults: DNT off (Chrome), preload "standard" (Chrome's default, since no request of wubble's own is added), can-make-payment on, Privacy Sandbox APIs off (Chrome asks for consent; wubble never shows the consent), WebRTC `default`. Unit-test that every row has a SettingDef and a valid mapping.
- Engine: a generic `Engine::set_profile_pref(container, name, value: PrefValue)` that lifts the `set_preference` code out of view.rs to a request-context helper in storage.rs or app.rs. Apply the whole table when each container context comes up (`Profiles::get`) and on each setting change, and keep the min-font-size path on the same helper.
- UI: the rows come from the settings table automatically.

title: <input type=color> on macOS (native colour panel)
spec:
On macOS, Chrome opens <input type=color> in the native NSColorPanel (ColorChooserMac, through WebContentsDelegate::OpenColorChooser). Linux and Windows use Blink's in-page popup, which wubble already draws as a popup widget (PageEvent::PopupShown, crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/popup-layer.slint). AlloyBrowserHostImpl does not override OpenColorChooser, and the default returns nullptr, so on the macOS build a colour input opens nothing.
Build in the repo: (1) On macOS only, add a main-world content-script channel `color` (wubble-helper/src). It catches a trusted click or Enter/Space activation on an enabled input[type=color], calls preventDefault, and posts {value, list suggestions} with a request id to the browser. (2) On the browser side, a pure machine answers once per request and closes on navigation or blur. It shows NSColorPanel through objc2 (crates/wubble already uses objc2 for macOS) with the starting colour, and sends each change back as `value` (the script sets .value and dispatches `input`). When the panel closes, the script dispatches `change`. (3) Leave Linux and Windows alone. (4) docs/macos.md: add colour input to the Mac console hand checks list.

title: Audible probe across iframes and WebAudio on a stock engine
spec:
Until a patched engine ships, wubble's audible probe (crates/wubble-engine/src/media.rs AUDIBLE_PROBE, run every 2 s as a main-frame eval) sees only `<audio>` and `<video>` in the top document. Embedded players (YouTube or Spotify iframes, which are cross-origin OOPIFs), media inside shadow roots and WebAudio games never light the sound badge or protect the tab from sleep.

What to build, without an engine change: (1) Shadow DOM. The probe walks open shadow roots as kit.js `shadowVideos` already does, capped as kit.js caps it. (2) WebAudio. kit.js wraps AudioContext and webkitAudioContext construction and `resume`, counting contexts in the `running` state with a non-zero destination connection. The probe reports `audible` when one is running and was started after a gesture. (3) iframes. The probe asks every frame, not just the main one: same-process frames through CEF frame iteration and `View::run_script_in`, and out-of-process frames through DevTools `Target.setAutoAttach {flatten:true}` and `Runtime.evaluate` with each attached session (the view's cdp() channel, crates/wubble-engine/src/cdp.rs). (4) Keep the ProbeState machine to one probe round in flight per view, and OR the per-frame answers in a pure fold with unit tests. When the engine audible patch exists (marker found), all of this is skipped. Measure by hand that the extra frames do not raise idle cost. Nothing in tests asserts timing. All platforms.

title: Import from Chrome, Chromium, Helium, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi and Arc: bookmarks, history, open tabs
spec: Chrome imports bookmarks, history and open tabs from other browsers; wubble-import (crates/wubble-import) reads only Firefox/Zen profiles and Arc's `StorableSidebar.json` (TODO.md: "Import: ... Arc history, Little Arc, Helium/Chromium"). Build in crates/wubble-import: (1) discovery `discover.rs`: a `Browser` table for Chromium-family roots per OS (Linux `~/.config/google-chrome`, `chromium`, `net.imput.helium`, `BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser`, `microsoft-edge`, `vivaldi`; macOS `Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome`, `Chromium`, `net.imput.helium`, `Arc/User Data`, ...; Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Google/Chrome/User Data`, ...), profiles from `Local State` JSON `profile.info_cache` (name, directory); extend `wubble_core::import::Source` with `Chrome, Chromium, Helium, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi` (Arc exists). (2) `chromium/bookmarks.rs`: the `Bookmarks` JSON (`roots.bookmark_bar/other/synced`, `date_added` in microseconds since 1601) to `BookmarkNode`. (3) `chromium/history.rs`: `History` SQLite copied to a temp file under the profile's cache first (as `snapshot_places` does, it is locked while the browser runs): `urls` + `visits` -> `ImportedVisit` (typed from `typed_count`/transition `TYPED`). (4) `chromium/session.rs`: SNSS `Sessions/Session_*` (or legacy `Current Session`), a port of `components/sessions/core/session_service_commands.cc` command ids (BSD-3): windows, tabs, pinned state, tab groups, current navigation URL/title -> `Layout` (one Space per window, a group becomes a folder). (5) Arc: history and tabs through the same readers from its `User Data`. Pure parsers on bytes, fixtures under crates/wubble-import/tests/fixtures, unit tests.

title: Extensions: chrome.contextMenus items in the page and action menus
spec: In Chrome, extension items created with `chrome.contextMenus.create` appear in the page context menu, filtered by `contexts`, `documentUrlPatterns` and `targetUrlPatterns`. More than one item per extension is grouped under the extension's name, radio and checkbox types and separators are honoured, and a click fires `contextMenus.onClicked(info, tab)`. Items with the `action` context appear in the action button's menu. wubble's page menu is its own table (`crates/wubble/src/menu.rs`, `ROWS`), and welding passes CEF's default model (`surface::menu_items`), which for Alloy-style windowless browsers carries no extension items. Patch `56-cef-ext-context-menus.patch`: table functions `menu_items(browser_id, json_params) -> json` and `menu_execute(browser_id, extension_id, item_id, json_params, checked)`. They are built on `extensions::MenuManager` and `ContextMenuMatcher` (`chrome/browser/extensions/context_menu_matcher.cc`, logic as in `RenderViewContextMenu::AppendAllExtensionItems`), and `MenuManager::ExecuteCommand` with a `content::ContextMenuParams` rebuilt from the JSON (link, src, selection, frame url, editable, media type). Plus a delegate notice `menus_changed`. wubble side: `ext_api.rs` wrappers. `wubble-engine::page::ContextMenu` already holds the fields that need serialising. Core/menu: `entries` gains an extension group (between groups 9 and 10) built from the returned items, with a submenu when an extension has more than one, using the kit menu's submenu support or flattened with the extension name as a header. A `Command::Extension { ext, item }` is answered through `menu_execute` and then a `None` CEF command. Add the action context to the ext-popup-shell row menu. Tests: pure entry building from item JSON.

title: Homebrew cask for macOS
spec: Mac users who live in the terminal install Chrome with `brew install --cask google-chrome`. wubble offers only `install.sh` and the DMG (`scripts/release/package-macos.sh`). To build: `scripts/release/macos/wubble.rb`, a cask that downloads `wubble-<V>-macos-<arch>.dmg` from the GitHub release with `sha256` per arch (`on_arm`/`on_intel`), `app "wubble.app"`, `auto_updates true` (wubble updates itself, so brew must not fight it), and a `zap` stanza for `~/Library/Application Support/wubble`, the caches and the preferences plist for `dev.wubble.browser`. Add a small step to `scripts/release/` (or `crates/wubble-release`) that rewrites the cask's version and sha256 lines from the dist/*.sha256 files when a release is packed. Publishing to a tap (`xuckless/homebrew-tap`) is the owner's step. Document it in docs/release.md next to the npm one. With `auto_updates true` the installed app updates through wubble's own updater: check that `updater/install.rs` `classify_mac` treats `/Applications/wubble.app` installed by brew as managed (it should, being the same layout) and say so in the cask's caveats.

title: Agent session tabs: drop back/forward cache and prerenders when a tab joins a session
spec: TODO line 63. A tab moved into an agent session's Space keeps its back/forward cache entries and any prerender made before. Activating either runs no navigation throttle, so the session's site guard is not asked, and only the commit backstop (`agent_backstop`/`agent_take_back` in `crates/wubble/src/host/agent.rs`) takes the tab back, after the page showed. Fix: when a tab joins a session (the Effect that binds a tab to a session in `wubble_core::agent`, executed in `agent_effect`), and for every tab the session opens, (1) send DevTools `Page.resetNavigationHistory`, which evicts the tab's bfcache entries along with its history, and (2) `Page.setPrerenderingAllowed {isAllowed:false}`, which cancels and blocks prerenders for that page. Both go through `View::cdp`; re-send after a renderer swap. Consider also turning speculation rules off in agent containers through the container's request-context preferences if CEF exposes them. Log each drop to the session's activity log. Add a probe step to the existing `--smoke mcp` scenario code only if it is a one-liner; no new test files.

title: Film rim on the remaining glass controls
spec:
The design draws a 1.5 px soap-film ring (`.wb-film`, core/wubble.css:33-40 in the design clone, angle `--wb-film-a`) on every glass control while it is touched, hovered, pressed, focused or open. The kit has it on button.slint (glass kind), the menu and select trigger (menu.slint:595), the field, search capsule, toggle, favs, address pill and some overlays (`kit/motion/film.slint`). The design also puts `wb-film` on the settings confirm button (`settings.tsx:366` `.st-confirm`), the start page's site-tile icons (`start.tsx:48`), the settings search field (`settings.tsx:558`), the found-glass tiers and the touch page's buttons. Some of these kit parts lack it: confirm-button.slint, icon-button.slint, the start page's tiles (kit/pages/start.slint) and the menu rows the TODO names.

To build: `git pull` the design clone. Grep the web source for `wb-film` and list each use against the kit component that translates it. For each one missing, add the `film` binding through the existing `kit/motion/film.slint` piece, lit on the same states the CSS uses (`:hover`, `:active`, `:focus-visible`, `.wb-on`). Update each file's `// design:` header with the lines it now translates. Menu rows get it only if the web source has it; if it does not, say so in the report rather than inventing one. Add a gallery shot of each touched surface, and keep the kit lock baseline from growing (crates/wubble-ui/tests/kit_lock.rs). All platforms.

title: Bookmarks: import and export the Netscape HTML file
spec:
Chrome's bookmark manager has 'Import bookmarks' and 'Export bookmarks', using the Netscape Bookmark File format (bookmarks_DATE.html: <DL><DT><A HREF ADD_DATE ICON>, <H3> folders, the PERSONAL_TOOLBAR_FOLDER attribute for the bar). Every browser reads and writes it. wubble's importers (crates/wubble-import: places for Firefox and Zen, arc, session) do not handle HTML, and there is no export.

1. crates/wubble-import: a new html.rs with `parse_netscape(&[u8]) -> Result<Vec<BookmarkNode>, ImportError>`. It is a tolerant tag scanner, since real files are not valid HTML: case-insensitive tags, entity decoding, no closing </DT>. It reads ADD_DATE in seconds into added_ms, takes javascript: and place: URLs only as kept-but-unopened, or drops them as is_web_url does, and marks the toolbar folder. Port from Firefox's BookmarkHTMLUtils (MPL-2.0) or write it new.
2. wubble-core: a pure `export_netscape(rows: &[BookmarkRow], now_ms) -> String` with Chrome's exact header (<!DOCTYPE NETSCAPE-Bookmark-file-1>, META charset, TITLE and H1 'Bookmarks') and HTML escaping. It has unit tests that round-trip with the parser.
3. Wiring: the bookmarks page header gets 'Import' and 'Export' kit buttons. Import uses the file chooser path the host already has (crates/wubble/src/chooser.rs) and applies the nodes into a new folder 'Imported' through the store's import apply (wubble-store/src/import.rs, import_marks so a file is not imported twice). Export uses a save dialog and writes the file.
4. Add the 'Import bookmarks', 'Export bookmarks' and 'bookmarks html' keywords to PALETTE.

title: Global Privacy Control (Sec-GPC header and navigator.globalPrivacyControl)
spec:
GPC sends `Sec-GPC: 1` on every request and exposes `navigator.globalPrivacyControl === true`. Brave and Firefox ship it, and Chrome has it behind a feature. wubble has neither.

Build:
- Add a setting `privacy.gpc` (bool, default off, Section::Privacy) in crates/wubble-core/src/settings.rs.
- First check whether the prebuilt libcef 156 has Chromium's feature: search the CEF binary for the feature name ("GlobalPrivacyControl") with `strings` on the downloaded libcef. If present, add it to the PageFeatures enable list in crates/wubble-engine/src/app.rs (it takes effect at the next start; say so on the row). Otherwise, use the embedder route:
  (a) A request header. Extend welding's request filter (vendor/welding/src, OnBeforeResourceLoad) and `wubble_engine::filter::RequestAction` with a header set. Simplest is an `extra_headers: &'static [(&str,&str)]` returned by a new `ContentFilter::headers(&RequestInfo)` that defaults to none, mark it a wubble change, and have crates/wubble/src/blocking.rs return Sec-GPC when the setting is on (an Arc atomic read on the IO thread).
  (b) The script: a main-world getter `navigator.globalPrivacyControl` installed in every frame at context creation through the helper's page scripts (crates/wubble/src/pagescripts.rs and wubble-helper), only when on. The engine passes the flag with the frame `hello`, like cosmetic.js.
- Write unit tests for the header decision.

title: HTTP sign-in sheet: fill from and save to the password vault
spec:
Chrome's HTTP auth dialog ("Sign in: <host> requires a username and password") is pre-filled from the password manager. After a successful sign-in Chrome offers to save the credentials, keyed by the scheme, host and realm (an HTML-less PasswordForm with scheme kBasic/kDigest). wubble draws the sheet (crates/wubble/src/prompt.rs Auth and AuthRequest, host/surfaces.rs) but does not consult the vault (wubble_core::autofill, crates/wubble/src/host/autofill.rs).
Build: (1) Key the vault entries for HTTP auth as signon_realm "<scheme>://<host>:<port>/<realm>", Chromium's form, with a unit test in wubble-core autofill. (2) When AuthEvent::Challenged opens the sheet, pre-fill the user and password fields from the one matching entry, or offer the key menu with several. A locked vault fills nothing and shows the existing unlock path. (3) After an answered challenge, if the next response for that URL is not another 401/407 for the same realm (a pure check fed by the next AuthRequested or LoadEnd), show the existing save prompt for that realm. (4) Proxy challenges (is_proxy) are saved under the proxy host. Agent sessions never get a save prompt, as decided. Passwords are never logged (the existing a_password_is_never_printed test extends to this).

title: Tab alert indicators: recording, screen capture, PiP
spec:
Chrome's tab strip shows one alert indicator per tab, in priority order: media recording (camera/mic, a red dot), desktop/tab capturing, audio playing, audio muted, Bluetooth, USB, HID, serial and VR connected, and picture-in-picture (chrome/browser/ui/tabs/tab_utils.cc GetTabAlertStatesForContents, BSD). The indicators have tooltips ("This tab is using your camera or microphone"). wubble's wubble_core::tabmarks has only the sound badge (Sound::Playing, Sound::Muted). The busy set (wubble_core::busy) already knows Reason::Capture (a live capture track, from the renderer probes) and Reason::Pip, but no tab row shows them.

What to build: (1) wubble-core/src/tabmarks.rs: a `TabAlert` enum with Chrome's priority (Recording, Capturing, Pip, Playing, Muted), derived in `Marks::of` from the busy set, the mute state and the pip owner. Split Capture into camera/mic versus display capture: extend the probes script (crates/wubble-helper/src/probes.js) to report `getDisplayMedia` tracks under a new key, plus a busy::Reason, kept in the one Reason table. Unit tests for the priority. (2) UI: the badge in the extended row and the rail (the kit's tab row parts) draws the right glyph and tint, with a tooltip and an accessible label. Recording uses Palette's alert tint. If the kit has no glyph for it, it is a derived piece and goes on derived-review.md; the badge press does nothing except for sound. (3) Gallery scenes for each state. All platforms.

title: Import passwords and cookies from Chromium-family browsers (os_crypt decryption)
spec: Chrome's importer brings saved passwords (and Edge/others bring cookies). wubble-import states "Passwords and cookies are out of scope" (crates/wubble-import/src/lib.rs). Build: (1) `os_crypt` decryption, a port of Chromium `components/os_crypt/sync` (BSD-3): Linux `v11` (key = PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1(password from Secret Service/KWallet item "<Browser> Safe Storage", "saltysalt", 1 iter, 16 bytes), AES-128-CBC, IV 16 spaces) and `v10` (`peanuts` fallback key); macOS (Keychain item "<Browser> Safe Storage", 1003 iterations; the user gets the system's allow prompt); Windows `v10` (AES-256-GCM key from `Local State` `os_crypt.encrypted_key`, DPAPI `CryptUnprotectData`); `v20` app-bound rows are reported as skipped (not decryptable outside the browser). Read the other browser's keyring entry through the existing `keyring` crate (crates/wubble-vault/Cargo.toml) behind a trait for tests; crates pbkdf2, sha1, aes, cbc (RustCrypto, MIT/Apache). (2) `Login Data` SQLite (copied first): `logins` origin_url, username_value, password_value, date_created, times_used, blacklisted_by_user (-> never-save decisions via `site_permissions`) -> `wubble_vault::ImportRow`, applied with `wubble_vault::apply` so duplicates/conflicts are reported. (3) `Cookies` SQLite: decrypt `encrypted_value` (DB meta version >= 24 strips the 32-byte SHA-256 host prefix), map to welding `Cookie` and write with `set_cookie` (vendor/welding/src/cookies.rs) into the default container's request context; skip expired, keep host-only/secure/httponly/samesite. Cookies are a separate, unchecked-by-default choice in the import UI with a note on what they are. Secrets zeroized; nothing logged.

title: Extensions: chrome.sidePanel in a wubble side pane
spec: Chrome shows an extension's `side_panel.default_path` page in the browser's side panel. `sidePanel.setOptions({tabId, path, enabled})` sets a per-tab page, `sidePanel.open({windowId|tabId})` opens it on a user gesture, `setPanelBehavior({openPanelOnActionClick})` makes the action button open it, and the side panel menu lists every extension with a panel. wubble has none. Bitwarden's default `sidepanel-disabled.html` is never shown (docs/research/extensions.md). wubble side (no patch needed for the default path): `parse_manifest` reads `side_panel.default_path`. A pane like the DevTools panel (`host/devtools.rs`, the `SourceSeam` right-edge pane with a new key, `SIDE_PANEL_TAB`) hosts a windowless view of `chrome-extension://<id>/<path>` in the visible tab's container. The lifecycle is a pure `extensions::side_panel` enum (Closed, Opening{ext}, Open{ext, tab}) with a transition, one per window, with tests, and the panel follows the visible tab, as `dock_follows_tab` does. Open it from the footer popover row menu and from the `_execute_side_panel` command. Patch `57-cef-side-panel.patch`: delegate `side_panel_open(extension_id, browser_id or window_id)`, called from `SidePanelOpenFunction` (`chrome/browser/extensions/api/side_panel/side_panel_api.cc`) when no `Browser` exists. A table function `side_panel_options(extension_id, browser_id) -> {path, enabled, open_on_action}` reads `SidePanelService`. A delegate notice on `OnPanelOptionsChanged` lets the pane change page. `action_click` consults `open_on_action` first. Mark the view via ext-tabs-getcurrent's `mark_view(kind = side panel)`.

title: Agent apps: VS Code, Copilot CLI, Goose and Windsurf on macOS as written formats; Windows paths
spec: TODO lines 65-66. `crates/wubble-core/src/agent/harness.rs` lists VS Code, Copilot CLI and Goose with `format: None` (found, never written), Windsurf on Linux only, and paths for Linux and macOS only (`files`/`detect` keyed by `Os`). Add from each app's documentation: VS Code user `mcp.json` with `{"servers": {name: {"type":"stdio","command","args"}}}` (path `["servers"]`, `Entry::Stdio`); Copilot CLI `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` `mcpServers` with `{"type":"local","command","args","tools":["*"]}` (a new `Entry` variant); Goose `~/.config/goose/config.yaml` `extensions.<name>: {type: stdio, cmd, args, enabled: true, name, timeout}`. Goose needs a new `Format::GooseYaml`, edited keeping the rest of the file byte for byte (a yaml-edit-preserving crate, or a narrow line-based edit of the `extensions:` block that refuses odd shapes); Windsurf on macOS is `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`. Windows: add `(Os::Windows, ...)` entries for every app (Claude desktop under `AppData/Roaming/Claude`, VS Code `AppData/Roaming/Code/User/mcp.json`, home-relative dotfiles as on Linux). The manifest's runtime dir (`crates/wubble-core/src/agent/manifest.rs`, `crates/wubble/src/instance.rs` `private_root`) uses `%LOCALAPPDATA%\wubble\mcp`. Extend the existing harness unit tests for the new formats (core logic).

title: Empty the kit lock baseline
spec:
The kit lock (crates/wubble-ui/tests/kit_lock.rs) still records about 100 violations in crates/wubble-ui/tests/kit_lock_baseline.txt. 60 are literals in `kit/derived.slint`; the rest are in shell files that the rules say must hold no visuals: components/raised.slint (9), components/folder-row.slint (9), components/border-beam.slint (5), app.slint (5), components/sidebar.slint (3), components/focus-ring.slint (3), kit/chrome/tab-row.slint (2) and kit/chrome/split-view.slint (2). TODO Design fidelity asks to empty it and to alias the value-equal `Shell` literals.

To build: (1) For each `derived.slint` literal, find the generated token with the same value in `ui/kit/gen/*.slint` and use it. Where none exists, add a named alias in one place. If it comes from the design, add it to the extractor (`tools/fidelity/extract.mjs`, then rerun it); never edit the gen files by hand. A truly wubble-only value becomes a single named constant recorded in docs/fidelity/derived-review.md. (2) Move the visuals in components/raised.slint, folder-row.slint, border-beam.slint and focus-ring.slint into kit components (a `// derived:` header naming the kit parts they compose) and make the shell files only lay them out. (3) Do the same for app.slint's five, and replace the `Shell` literals that equal a token. (4) Lower the baseline with `KIT_LOCK_WRITE=1 cargo test -p wubble-ui --test kit_lock` (the compile or test step) until it is empty, and leave the rule in force. Gallery shots before and after must match by eye. All platforms.

title: Bookmark editing: edit URL, open all, bookmark all tabs, folder delete confirmation and undo
spec:
Chrome's bookmark editor and manager do the following, and wubble is missing them:
- 'Edit…' changes both the name and the URL. BookmarkEdit in crates/wubble-core/src/pages.rs has Rename (title only), Move, Delete, Add and AddFolder.
- 'Open all (N)', 'Open all in new window' and 'Open all in Incognito', with a confirmation over 15 tabs.
- 'Bookmark all tabs…' (Mod+Shift+D) makes a folder of the window's tabs.
- Deleting a folder is undoable ('Undo' toast). TODO notes that wubble deletes a folder with its contents in one press.
- 'Copy' and 'Paste' of bookmarks, and 'Show in folder' from search results.

Build:
1. BookmarkEdit::Edit { id, title, url } and a store fn (crates/wubble-store/src/bookmarks.rs update_bookmark). The bookmark sheet (components/bookmark-sheet.slint, host/pages.rs sheet_view and sheet_edits) gets a URL field for the Edit kind, validated through omnibox::classify, which must be Intent::Url.
2. Action::BookmarkAllTabs (FIXED, PALETTE, keys.rs Mod+Shift+D). It opens the sheet in a new 'folder of tabs' kind and writes AddFolder plus Adds as one store transaction.
3. A row menu on bookmark and folder rows (Menu::Shell): Open in new tab, Open all (N) for folders, Edit, Move, Copy address, Delete. Open all opens Command::NewTab for each URL. Over 15 asks through the existing dialog-sheet.
4. Undo for deletes: a pure undo slot in wubble-core holding the deleted subtree (BookmarkRow list). A kit toast (components/toast.slint) with 'Undo' re-inserts it at the same parent and positions. The slot clears on the next edit.

Unit tests for subtree capture and restore, and for the sheet kinds.

title: Mark downloaded files with their origin (quarantine / MOTW / xattr)
spec:
Chrome annotates every finished download. On macOS it sets the `com.apple.quarantine` xattr (with the agent name and the origin URL, so Gatekeeper checks the file) and `kMDItemWhereFroms`. On Windows it writes the Mark-of-the-Web `Zone.Identifier` ADS (ZoneId=3, ReferrerUrl, HostUrl) through IAttachmentExecute. On Linux it sets `user.xdg.origin.url` and `user.xdg.referrer.url`. With CEF and wubble's download handling it is not known that these are written, and the media downloader (wubble-ffmpeg muxes) writes files itself without them.

Build:
- Add a pure `wubble_core::download::source_marks(url, referrer, platform) -> Vec<Mark>` that strips credentials from URLs, as Chromium's `quarantine` component does (components/services/quarantine, BSD-3-Clause, with a source comment). Unit-test it.
- Add one shared trait `Quarantine` with a per-platform implementation (AGENTS.md: per-platform code implements one shared trait) in crates/wubble (or wubble-sysmem-style OS code). Linux uses `xattr` setxattr (the `xattr` crate, MIT/Apache). macOS uses setxattr `com.apple.quarantine` with the `0081;<hex time>;wubble;<uuid>` format plus the WhereFroms plist. Windows writes `<path>:Zone.Identifier`. It runs only when the mark is missing, so a CEF-written mark is kept.
- Call it from crates/wubble/src/host/downloads.rs on the Complete transition and from the media downloader's finish.
- A failure is logged, never fatal.

title: Page Picture-in-Picture API and auto-PiP through wubble's Pip window
spec:
In Chrome, `HTMLVideoElement.requestPictureInPicture()` opens the PiP window and resolves with a PictureInPictureWindow (width, height, onresize). `document.pictureInPictureElement`, `exitPictureInPicture()` and the enterpictureinpicture and leavepictureinpicture events all work. The media session action `enterpictureinpicture` lets video calls auto-enter PiP on a tab switch. In wubble's windowless CEF the API rejects. wubble's own PiP (wubble_core::pip, host/videos.rs pip_event, kit.js `k.pip`) is started only from the strip, the setting PIP_ON_TAB_SWITCH, or the shell.

What to build: (1) kit.js: replace `HTMLVideoElement.prototype.requestPictureInPicture`, `document.exitPictureInPicture`, `pictureInPictureEnabled` and the `pictureInPictureElement` getter, plus the events. A request with a gesture (navigator.userActivation.isActive) records the element and returns a pending promise. The next snapshot reports `pipAsk`. The host feeds it into the pip machine as a new `PipInput::PageAsked(tab)`, and later answers with a kit call `k.pipDone(ok, w, h)` that resolves or rejects and fires the events. `disablePictureInPicture` refuses. (2) wubble-core/src/pip.rs: the new input and the effect `AnswerPage`, added to the transition table with unit tests. (3) Auto-PiP: a page that registered an `enterpictureinpicture` media session handler (kit.js already keeps handlers) is popped out on a tab switch even with PIP_ON_TAB_SWITCH off, as Chrome does for video calls. Its handler is called instead of the element fullscreen. All platforms.

title: Import passwords and cookies from Firefox and Zen directly (no CSV)
spec: Chrome and Firefox import saved logins straight from another profile; wubble only accepts a CSV the user exports by hand (TODO.md "Zen/Arc password import (CSV only)", crates/wubble-vault/src/import.rs). Build in crates/wubble-import: (1) `firefox/logins.rs`: parse `logins.json` (hostname, httpRealm, formSubmitURL, encryptedUsername, encryptedPassword, timeCreated, timesUsed) and decrypt with the key from `key4.db` (SQLite `metaData` password-check entry and `nssPrivate` a11): ASN.1 DER (crate `der`, Apache/MIT) PBES2 with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 + AES-256-CBC for modern profiles and PKCS#12 3DES (SHA-1 PBE) for older ones, then the per-entry 3DES-CBC/AES-CBC decrypt. Implement from NSS's published formats (NSS is MPL-2.0; any copied code credited in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md; do not copy GPL firefox_decrypt). A primary password set in Firefox is detected via the password-check entry and asked for in a wubble sheet; wrong password -> retry. Rows -> `wubble_vault::ImportRow`, applied with `wubble_vault::apply`; Firefox's `disabledSavingOrigins` in `permissions.sqlite` (`password-saving` type) -> never-save decisions. (2) `firefox/cookies.rs`: `cookies.sqlite` `moz_cookies` (plaintext) mapped by `originAttributes` userContextId to the imported containers (crates/wubble-import/src/containers.rs) where wubble has the container, else the default one; written through welding `set_cookie`. Both read from copied files (locked DB). Zen uses the same code. Unit tests with fixture key4.db/logins.json generated from a throwaway profile with a known password.

title: Extensions: chrome.omnibox keyword mode in the command bar
spec: In Chrome, an extension declares `omnibox.keyword`. Typing the keyword followed by Tab or Space enters keyword mode ("<Extension name> |"). `onInputStarted`, `onInputChanged(text, suggest)`, `onInputEntered(text, disposition)`, `onInputCancelled` and `onDeleteSuggestion` fire, and suggestions with description markup (`<match>`, `<dim>`, `<url>`) plus `setDefaultSuggestion` appear as results. wubble's command bar (`wubble_core::omnibox`, `suggest.rs`, `crates/wubble/src/bar.rs`) has no extension source. Core (pure, tested): `parse_manifest` reads `omnibox.keyword`. `omnibox::classify` recognises `<keyword><space>` against the enabled extensions' keywords and yields a `Mode::ExtensionKeyword { ext, text }`. A small state machine `omnibox::ext_session` (Idle, Started, Waiting(req id), Shown) turns typing into effects: Start, Changed(text, req), Entered(text, disposition), Cancelled. Description markup is parsed into styled runs for the kit result row (`ExtensionSuggestion` mapped onto an existing `CommandKind`). Patch `58-src-omnibox.patch`: table functions `omnibox_started(profile, ext)`, `omnibox_changed(profile, ext, text, req)`, `omnibox_entered(profile, ext, text, disposition)`, `omnibox_cancelled(profile, ext)` and `omnibox_delete(profile, ext, content)`, calling `ExtensionOmniboxEventRouter::On*` (`chrome/browser/extensions/api/omnibox/omnibox_api.cc`). A delegate `omnibox_suggestions(ext, req, json)` is fed from `OmniboxAPI`'s suggestions-ready path and `OmniboxSetDefaultSuggestionFunction`. Entered with disposition current tab, new foreground tab or new background tab maps to the extension's own handling, since the extension navigates itself.

title: Wheel over a nested scroller scrolls the pane, not the document (agent `scroll` and the user's wheel)
spec: TODO line 67. `scroll` with a direction over an `overflow:auto` pane sends `View::wheel` at the pane's point (`agent_wheel` in `crates/wubble/src/host/agent.rs`, 5 ticks of 20 ms). The event reaches the pane, but in most runs the document scrolls. The likely cause is Chromium's wheel scroll latching and hit-test: wubble sends no mouse move to the point first, so the latched scroll target and hover state come from the last pointer position, and the phase (`wheel_deltas` in `crates/wubble-engine/src/input.rs`) may start a new latch sequence on the document. Fix: before the first tick, send a mouse move to the point and fence it (`Fence::Pointer`). Then send the ticks as one gesture with Chromium's phase flags (began, changed, ended) where CEF exposes them through `MouseEvent` modifiers (`EVENTFLAG_PRECISION_SCROLLING_DELTA`), or move the agent path to DevTools `Input.dispatchMouseEvent {type:'mouseWheel'}` at the point. That event is hit-tested at its own coordinates and scrolls the innermost scroller as a user's would. Check that `View::wheel` for the user's own wheel moves the pointer first too (`crates/wubble/src/input.rs`). Update the `scroll` tool text in `crates/wubble-mcp/src/tools.rs`.

title: Voice glow shader in the kit (no microphone)
spec:
The design has a voice glow: low/mid/high bands with attack and release plus a flow phase (`core/voice.ts` `VOICE` constants and `VoiceBands` in the design clone), feeding uniforms of the glass shader and the listening bubble. In wubble the shader is ported, but `glass.wgsl` sends the voice uniforms as zero (crates/wubble-gfx/src/scene/mod.rs around lines 67-68), and nothing drives them. Decisions "No voice yet": the shader goes into the kit, with no microphone.

To build: (1) Port `VoiceBands` as a pure state machine in wubble-core (`voice.rs`, with a `// design: core/voice.ts:<lines> @<commit>` comment): `fn step(bands, input: Levels, dt) -> Bands` with the design's attack 18/s, release 4.5/s and flow 0.6 + 3.2·level rad/s. Generate the constants through `tools/fidelity/extract.mjs` into `wubble_core::kit_gen`, not by hand. Add the synthetic speech-like envelope the design uses for demos. Unit tests. (2) Add a scene input for the bands in wubble-gfx scene state (state.rs/render.rs) that feeds the existing voice uniforms in glass.wgsl, and the bubble if the design's listening bubble shares them. Effects run only while something sets non-zero bands, so idle cost stays zero (scene run state). (3) Add a kit-facing property, for example a `voice` struct on the glass layer, and a gallery scene driven by the synthetic envelope (crates/wubble/src/gallery_smoke.rs). No microphone, and no permission prompt. All platforms.

title: Dangerous-site interstitial for blocker badware/malware document blocks
spec:
Chrome shows a red full-page "Dangerous site" warning with "Back to safety" and, under Details, "visit this unsafe site". uBlock Origin's strict blocking does the same for `$doc` and badware rules. wubble's blocker ships the uBO badware list (crates/wubble-blocker/src/catalog.rs `ublock-badware`). A blocked main-frame document ends as ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT in the generic error panel (crates/wubble-core/src/neterror.rs -20), with no way through and no explanation.

Build:
- wubble-blocker: decisions for Document requests report which list matched (`Decision` in crates/wubble-blocker/src/decision.rs gets a `list: Option<&'static str>` or a `Category {Badware, Privacy, Ads}`). Unit-test it.
- crates/wubble/src/blocking.rs keeps the last document block per browser_id, holding the URL, list and rule.
- crates/wubble/src/page_error.rs: when the load error is -20 and a document block is recorded for that URL, the panel becomes `PageError::Blocked { url, category, rule }`. Its text is Chrome's register ("Dangerous site" for badware, "Page blocked" for others), with "Go back" (the default) and "Proceed anyway" under Advanced.
- Proceed adds a session exception (per container and host) that the filter consults for Document requests only, then reloads. The site's Shields toggle (`blocker.exceptions`) stays the permanent way.
- UI: reuse kit a-error-panel with a danger tint if the kit has one, else a derived piece on derived-review.md.
- No network lookups: Safe Browsing stays out.

title: Picture-in-Picture window controls parity
spec:
Chrome's video PiP window has play/pause and back and forward 10 s. It adds previous and next track when the page has those media session handlers, plus mute and unmute, a progress bar with the current and total time, Skip Ad (skipad), the video-call buttons (togglemicrophone, togglecamera, hangup), back to tab and close. The window can be resized from its edges, and its size and position are remembered. In wubble, components/pip-controls.slint has back 10 s, play, forward 10 s, return and close only (host/videos.rs pip_command: play, seek-by, return, close). Resize and placement memory are not handled.

What to build: (1) Host: feed the Pip window's controls from the same kit `meta` and `v` snapshot the strip uses, which already carries t, dur, muted and the next/prev flags. Extend kit.js `meta` with flags for skipad, togglemicrophone, togglecamera and hangup handlers. (2) pip-controls.slint: add the conditional buttons and a seek track. Reuse the video strip's track from video-controls.slint, and its kit parts, BDock and IconButton. Commands go out as new pip_command names: mute, next, prev, skipad, mic, camera, hangup, seek-to; route the media-session ones to `kit.act`. (3) Window: resizable from its edges, keeping the video's aspect ratio. Remember its size and position in settings (Section::Hidden) and restore them next time, clamped to the current display (wubble_core::window owns the Pip window's state). (4) Keys while the PiP window is focused: Space toggles, the arrows seek, M mutes. The design has no PiP (wubble-only.md §28), so add the new pieces to derived-review.md. All platforms.

title: Import: Zen legacy workspace tables, Little Arc, Arc pinned/favourites details
spec: TODO.md lists gaps in the existing importers: "Zen legacy tables, Arc history, Little Arc" (Arc history moves to `import-chromium-family`). Build in crates/wubble-import: (1) Zen legacy storage: before `zen-sessions.jsonlz4`, Zen kept workspaces and pins in `places.sqlite` tables (`zen_workspaces`, `zen_pins`, `zen_workspace_*`, depending on version) and in `sessionstore.jsonlz4` window extra data; extend crates/wubble-import/src/places.rs/session.rs to read those tables when present and map them to `ImportedSpace`/`ImportedFolder`/`ImportedTab` (essentials -> `Placement::Essential`, pinned -> `Pinned`, workspace container -> `container`), preferring the newest source and noting the fallback in `Imported::warnings`. Use Zen's own source (MPL-2.0) for the schema and credit it. (2) Little Arc: Arc keeps Little Arc windows' tabs in its sidebar data (`StorableSidebar.json` containers of type little-arc / `StorableWindows.json`); crates/wubble-import/src/arc.rs maps them to a Space named "Little Arc" (or into the active Space's unpinned tabs). (3) Arc's favourites (top apps), split-view items and folder colours: map what `wubble_core` has (favourites -> pinned/essential, splits -> wubble splits via `split_panes` if the store's merge supports it, else one tab each with a warning). Fixtures and unit tests for each format version. Verifying the macOS Zen and Windows Arc paths on real machines is hand work, not part of this.

title: Extensions: native messaging hosts found where desktop apps install them
spec: In Chrome, `runtime.connectNative`/`sendNativeMessage` find host manifests in the user-level dirs (`~/.config/google-chrome/NativeMessagingHosts`, `~/.config/chromium/NativeMessagingHosts`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/NativeMessagingHosts`) and the system dirs, and Windows uses the registry. Password-manager desktop apps (Bitwarden, 1Password, KeePassXC) write Chrome's and Chromium's dirs. In wubble, CEF overrides `DIR_USER_DATA`, so Chromium looks only under `<cache root>/NativeMessagingHosts` and the system Chromium paths (docs/research/extensions.md table row "nativeMessaging": "wubble's user dir needs them copied or linked (later)"). To build: (1) Core, pure: `extensions::native_hosts::plan(found: &[(source_dir, file_name, json)], installed_ids, existing_in_ours) -> Vec<HostOp>` keeps only valid manifests (`name`, `path`, `type: stdio`, and `allowed_origins` naming an installed extension id, or any `chrome-extension://` origin when the user allows it). It copies changed ones, removes ones whose source vanished and that wubble wrote (tracked by a marker field or a side list), and never overwrites a user's own file. Tests. (2) Engine: `crates/wubble-engine/src/extensions.rs` gains `sync_native_hosts(root)`, run before CEF starts next to the dictionary install, scanning the per-platform source dirs (Linux: google-chrome, chromium, BraveSoftware, microsoft-edge, vivaldi; macOS equivalents). On Windows, no copy is needed, since Chromium reads `HKCU\Software\Google\Chrome\NativeMessagingHosts` only for Chrome branding: add our own registry key mirroring entries. (3) Settings: a Bool `extensions.native_hosts_import` (default 1, local only, no network) and a list of imported hosts in the extensions section.

title: `wait_for load` follows in-page navigations' fetches: network idle through DevTools events
spec: TODO line 68. `Wait::Loaded` (crates/wubble/src/host/agent.rs) waits for no load running and a tree. A history-API navigation's fetches are not followed. Add Playwright's `networkidle`: in `crates/wubble-engine/src/cdp.rs`, a pure `NetIdle` reader (like `NavRequests`) that counts in-flight requests from `Network.requestWillBeSent`, `Network.loadingFinished`, `Network.loadingFailed` and `Network.webSocketCreated/Closed`, excluding data: URLs and long-polling event streams after 5 s, and records the time it last went to zero. Enable the Network domain only on agent-driven views (`Network.enable` with small buffer sizes, sent with the session's other setup) so ordinary tabs pay nothing. Expose `View::net_idle_since() -> Option<Instant>`. Add `Wait::Idle { tab }` (0 in flight for 500 ms) and a `network` (or `idle`) value for `wait_for` in `crates/wubble-mcp/src/tools.rs`. Make `load` wait for idle after a same-document navigation when the URL changed during the call. Update the tool description that documents the gap.

title: Feel pass: stretch and squash on every pressable and moving surface
spec:
The design's touch kit gives pressables and moving surfaces a spring stretch and squash (`stretchOf`, `squashAt` and `spr` in pages/touch-kit.tsx:43-80, the `sq-a`/`sq-b` press classes in touch.tsx, and the `.wb-press` rules in core/wubble.css). wubble has this on some controls (`wubble_core::stretch`, `wubble_core::controls`, kit/motion). TODO "Feel pass" asks for it on every one: menus, popovers, sheets, toasts, the command bar and the tab strip.

To build: (1) Write down the design's exact squash and stretch curves as pure functions in wubble-core (extending stretch.rs or controls.rs), with their values from kit_gen, and unit tests. (2) Make one kit motion piece (for example `kit/motion/squash.slint`, headed with the design lines) that any surface wraps: a press squash, an entry overshoot, and a stretch along the direction of motion driven by velocity. Drive it from the one vsynced rendering notifier, redrawing only while something moves (decisions "Shell animation"). (3) Apply it to every kit overlay and chrome surface that the list names: kit/overlay/a/* and b/* popovers, the menu, the sheet, toasts, the command bar (chrome/command-bar.slint) and tab rows while dragged or reordered. Reduced motion (`ui.reduce_motion`) turns it off. (4) Add gallery shots at mid-motion for each. Never drop a frame at 120 Hz: the physics is O(1) per surface. All platforms.

title: Auto-revoke permissions of unused sites (Safety check)
spec:
Chrome's Safety Hub (`UnusedSitePermissionsService`) removes granted permissions from sites not visited in 60 days. It tells the user under "Permissions removed from unused sites" with Undo, and the setting "Remove permissions from unused sites" is on by default. Notification grants for abusive sites are also revoked. wubble remembers grants forever (crates/wubble-core/src/site.rs, the store's `site_permissions.decided_at`).

Build:
- Add a setting `site.auto_revoke` (bool, default on) in settings.rs.
- wubble-core site.rs: add a pure `fn unused(rows: &[(container, origin, kind, decision, decided_at)], last_visit: impl Fn(container, origin) -> Option<i64>, now) -> Vec<Revocation>`. Only Allow decisions of prompt kinds (not Popups, ExternalLinks, SavePasswords or Block rows) are revoked, after 60 days without a visit and 60 days since the decision. Unit-test it.
- Host: at start, after the store loads (crates/wubble/src/persist.rs), compute it with the history store's last visit per origin (add a query in wubble-store history.rs: max visit time grouped by origin). Delete those rows, and record them in a new store table `revoked_permissions` (container, origin, kind, revoked_at) so they can be undone.
- UI: a Settings > Sites row "Permissions removed from unused sites" listing them, with Restore (put the row back) and Dismiss (forget the record).
- Depends on permissions-per-container for the container key.

title: Document Picture-in-Picture (CEF patch plus host window)
spec:
Chrome supports `documentPictureInPicture.requestWindow({width, height})`. It opens an always-on-top window with a blank same-origin document the opener fills (Google Meet, Spotify and YouTube mini-player use it), and it fires `enter` and the window's pagehide. In CEF windowless (Alloy style) the request fails: Chromium routes it through //chrome's DocumentPictureInPictureWindowController and PictureInPictureWindowManager, which open a Browser of type PICTURE_IN_PICTURE that CEF never creates for OSR.

What to build: (1) A patch, patches/chromium/5x-cef-document-pip.patch, in the queue's style. In CEF's WebContentsDelegate for Alloy-style browsers, treat the document-PiP WebContents creation as a popup: call CefLifeSpanHandler::OnBeforePopup with a new disposition flag, or with an exported marker table `cef_wubble_docpip_v1` that carries the requested size, and let it be windowless like other popups. Wire the controller's close to the browser close. List it in patches/README.md. (2) welding/engine: recognise that disposition (a `wubble change` in vendor/welding/src/popup.rs) and report `PageEvent::DocumentPip { size }`. (3) Model and host: show it in the existing Pip window kind (wubble_core::window WindowKind::Pip) as a CEF view with no strip, sized as asked, always on top, and closed when the opener navigates or closes. wubble_core::pip gets a `Document` variant so video PiP and document PiP never coexist. Unit tests. The patch cannot be built now; write it so that it applies to CEF 156.0.30.

title: Import UI: pick a browser and profile, choose data, apply, show the summary
spec: Chrome's "Import bookmarks and settings" dialog lists detected browsers and profiles, lets you tick Browsing history, Favourites/bookmarks, Saved passwords, Search engines, Autofill data, Cookies, then imports and reports. In wubble the parsers (crates/wubble-import) and the store's apply (crates/wubble-store/src/import.rs `ImportSummary`, `merge_spaces`) exist but nothing in the app calls them (TODO.md: "Import app wiring: pick a profile, apply, replace the live model, show the summary"); only the Passwords page imports a CSV. Build: (1) a pure lifecycle in wubble-core (`import_flow`: `Idle -> Scanning -> Choosing{profiles, kinds} -> Reading -> Applying -> Done{summary}|Failed`, one `transition`, unit tests) with data kinds as a table (Spaces and tabs, Bookmarks, History, Passwords, Cookies); (2) host module crates/wubble/src/host/import.rs: discovery (`discover::find_profiles`, `find_arc`, the Chromium-family finder) on a worker thread, reading on the worker, applying on the store thread through `StoreClient` (crates/wubble/src/persist.rs), then replacing the live `Model` with the merged one (the apply returns it) and re-rendering the sidebar; passwords through `VaultCommand` (unlocking first), cookies through the engine; (3) UI: an "Import from another browser" row in Settings (crates/wubble-core/src/settings.rs + crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/settings.slint) opening a sheet built from kit parts (list of profiles with browser icon, checkboxes `check-box.slint`, primary Import), and the summary from `ImportSummary` + `ApplyReport` (`import_summary` in crates/wubble-vault/src/command.rs) with skipped items; (4) a first-run offer on the start page when another browser is found (once, dismissable, stored setting). Gallery scenes for the sheet's states.

title: Extensions: the missing tabs/windows events, bounds and windows.create
spec: Chrome sends `tabs.onMoved`, `onAttached`, `onDetached`, `onReplaced` (a discarded tab coming back), `onHighlighted`, `onZoomChange`, and `windows.onCreated`/`onRemoved`/`onBoundsChanged`. It reports window bounds and state (normal, maximized, fullscreen), and supports `windows.create`/`update`/`remove` and `tabs.move`, `group`, `discard`, `duplicate`, `goBack`/`goForward`. wubble's patch queue covers query, get, update, remove, sendMessage, onCreated, onUpdated, onActivated, onRemoved and onFocusChanged. Moves are not diffed, bounds are 0, sleeping tabs vanish instead of sending onReplaced, and `windows.create` is refused (docs/research/extensions.md section 7; TODO M6; decision "windows.create"). Core: `extensions/projection.rs` gains a pure `diff(prev: &Projection, next: &Projection) -> Vec<ExtEvent>` (Moved{from,to}, Attached, Detached, WindowCreated, WindowRemoved, Replaced{old,new}). A sleeping tab stays listed with `discarded: true` (Chrome keeps discarded tabs) instead of being left out, and its wake sends Replaced. Window bounds come from the wubble window's position and size. Tests. Patch `59-src-tab-events.patch` extends `set_state` with bounds and state fields (already in `cef_wubble_ext_window_t`: x, y, width, height; add state). Add a function `dispatch_tab_event(kind, json)` that routes to `TabsEventRouter`'s `DispatchEvent` for moved, attached, detached and replaced, and to `WindowsEventRouter` for created and removed, bypassing `windows_event_router.cc:203-206, 227-230`'s Browser-only filter. New delegate requests: `move_tab`, `discard_tab`, `duplicate_tab`, `go_back`, `create_window(url, type, bounds)`, `update_window`, `remove_window`. wubble maps `create_window` type normal to a new Main window, and popup to a Popup window, in `host/ext_tabs.rs` via model `Command`s. That supersedes the "windows.create refused" decision, which the report should note.

title: `read_page` lists options, list boxes and multiple selects; `select` can add a choice
spec: TODO lines 69-70. `read_page` gives no ref for an `<option>`, a list box or a `<select multiple>`/`size>1`. A collapsed select's options are AX-invisible, and `listBox`/`listBoxOption` are no `wubble_ax` item kind (crates/wubble-ax/src/flat.rs). `select` (crates/wubble/src/host/agent.rs `agent_select`/`agent_selected`, wubble-core `agent/forms.rs`) sets one choice and clears the others. (1) In wubble-ax, add item kinds for listBox and listBoxOption (role, name, selected state) and include them in `flatten`/`line`. For a collapsed `<select>`, show its options as a comma list on the select's line (from the select's own DevTools resolution in forms.rs, `DOM.describeNode` with depth 1), so the agent sees choices without opening it. (2) `select` gains an `add: bool` argument (crates/wubble-mcp/src/tools.rs schema and `AgentCall` parsing). On a multiple select, `add:true` keeps the other selected options and toggles on the named one; `values: [..]` sets exactly that set. It dispatches `input` and `change` once, through the same per-call object group (`SELECT_GROUP`).

title: Feel pass: liquid glass under every floating surface
spec:
TODO "Feel pass" asks for liquid glass (the scene's blurred and refracted backdrop) under every floating surface, with the flat fallback kept. In wubble, glass is data: every kit `GlassPanel` reports a `GlassItem` to one registry, which the scene draws (decisions "Glass in the shell"), and over-page glass lives in the scene's over layers (`OverLayer::Card/Peek/Top`, crates/wubble-gfx/src/scene/pages.rs). Some floating surfaces still draw a Slint-only fill rather than registering glass: for example tooltips, the status bubble, toasts, the drag ghost, the extension popup card, the autofill chip, hover cards and the swipe chip.

To build: walk every kit overlay and chrome surface (crates/wubble-ui/ui/kit/overlay/**, kit/chrome/drag-ghost.slint, kit/controls/tooltip.slint, the status bubble and hover card components) and list each one that floats over the page or the sidebar without a `GlassPanel`. For each, compose the kit `material/glass.slint` panel so it reports a `GlassItem` with the right layer (Card for in-card overlays, Top for window-wide ones). Check that the flat fallback path (`Glass::SlintOnly`, `WUBBLE_GLASS=slint`, `Quality::Flat`) still draws them correctly. Mind the cost: the governor (`scene::quality::Governor`) must hold 8.33 ms, so a surface that animates at 120 Hz marks only its own rect. Add gallery shots of every surface with scene glass and with the fallback. All platforms.

title: Media context menu: Picture in Picture, Mute, video frame rows
spec:
Chrome's context menu on a video has Play/Pause, Mute/Unmute, Loop, Show controls, Picture in picture, Open video in new tab, Save video as, Copy video address, and since M120 Copy video frame and Save video frame as. wubble's crates/wubble/src/menu.rs ROWS has Play, Loop, Show Controls, the three address rows and the screenshot row. Picture in Picture is left out on purpose (comment at ~line 313 and TODO.md M1 "Page context menu: the Picture in Picture row"), and there is no Mute or frame row, even though wubble now has its own PiP (wubble_core::pip) and a frame grab (kit.js `k.frame`).

What to build in menu.rs, with its label tests updated: (1) A Mute/Unmute row: `MediaOp::Mute`, from the menu's MediaFlags muted bit, run through `media_script`. (2) A Picture in Picture row for videos with CAN_PICTURE_IN_PICTURE, or always for video when the flag is absent. It is a new Command that feeds `PipInput` for the tab, targeting the element under the pointer: pass its point, and the kit picks that element instead of `primary()`; add `k.pipAt(x, y)`. (3) Copy Video Frame and Save Video Frame As…: grab the frame at the point (extend `k.frame` with an element argument), then put a PNG on the clipboard through the screenshot worker (decisions.md "Copy Image" path) or write it to the downloads folder as a finished download (`add_finished_download`). A cross-origin video whose canvas is tainted falls back to a crop of the view's screenshot of the element's rect. (4) The rows follow Chromium's AppendMediaItems order. All platforms.

title: Sync engine: end-to-end encrypted, to a folder the user picks, off by default
spec: Chrome Sync keeps bookmarks, history, passwords, open tabs and settings in step across devices with optional passphrase (end-to-end) encryption. wubble has none (TODO.md "Sync (deferred)"; docs/decisions.md "Sync: Deferred, no design work yet"). The owner wants E2E encryption, a destination the user chooses (folder or WebDAV), off by default, nothing phoning home. Build a new crate `wubble-sync` (pure except its transports): (1) keys: a random 256-bit account key, wrapped by a key derived from the user's passphrase with Argon2id (RustCrypto argon2, MIT/Apache), stored wrapped in the destination (`keys.json`) and unwrapped key cached in the OS keyring (reuse `wubble_vault::KeyRing`); a printable recovery code. (2) Record format: per collection, per record id, an encrypted blob (XChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-256-GCM with collection+id as associated data), a Lamport/HLC timestamp and device id, tombstones; server-blind (file names are HMACs of ids). (3) Layout: append-only per-device change logs plus periodic compacted snapshots so a folder synced by Syncthing/Dropbox/iCloud Drive never sees write conflicts (each device writes only its own files). (4) Transport trait `Remote { list, get, put, delete }` with `FolderRemote` here. (5) Lifecycle in wubble-core `sync::State` (`Off -> Setup -> Unlocked -> Syncing -> Idle -> Error{retry_at}`, one `transition`, effects executed by the host), device registry record (name, platform, last seen). Merge rules per collection are pluggable (`sync-collections`). Setting `sync.enabled` default false; nothing runs until set up. Unit tests for crypto round trip, wrong passphrase, log merge and compaction.

title: Task manager: renderer pids under the sandbox and Chrome's process labels
spec: Chrome's task manager ties each tab, subframe, extension, service worker and utility process to its real pid and labels it ("Tab: …", "Subframe: https://…", "Extension: …", "Service Worker: …", "Utility: Network Service", "GPU Process", "Spare renderer"). In wubble on Linux with the sandbox, each renderer reports pid 1 from its PID namespace, so tab rows have no memory, CPU or End, and renderers show as "Zygote" (TODO line 91; `host/tasks.rs` uses `wubble_sysmem::host_pid`, which cannot tell renderers apart, and the frame hello comes from welding change 34). Patch `60-cef-process-info.patch`: export a separate C table `cef_wubble_proc_v1`, looked up like `ext_api::available()` but independent of the extension patches, with: `renderer_pid(browser_id)`, from `RenderFrameHost::GetProcess()->GetProcess().Pid()`, real pid; `child_processes(out json)`, from `BrowserChildProcessHostIterator` (process type, `metrics_name`, pid) plus `RenderProcessHost::AllHostsIterator` with each host's frames' sites, service worker scopes and extension ids. wubble side: a new `wubble-engine/src/proc_api.rs` with safe wrappers returning `ProcInfo { pid, kind, label }`. `host/tasks.rs::sample_tasks` prefers it over the frame-reported pid. `wubble_core::tasks::rows` gains `Kind::Subframe`, `Kind::Extension(id)` and `Kind::Worker` rows labelled as Chrome labels them (pure, tested), with extension names from the installed list. Without the table, today's behaviour stays.

title: `upload_file`: one path-check worker instead of a thread per call
spec: TODO line 73. `validate_upload_paths` (crates/wubble/src/host/agent.rs ~721) runs on a fresh thread per call with a 5 s answer limit (`UPLOAD_PATHS_WAIT`). A path on a hung mount fails the call at 5 s, but that thread stays blocked until the file system answers, and each further call leaks another. Replace it with one long-lived checker thread (lazily started and owned by the host's agent state) fed by a channel of `(nonce, paths)`, answering through the existing `agent_paths(nonce, result)` on the Slint thread. Track whether the worker is busy. While a check is outstanding past its limit, later calls fail at once with "a previous file check is still waiting on the file system (path X)", without spawning anything. When the worker answers late, the late answer is dropped (the nonce is gone) and the worker takes new work. Keep the pure parts (`validate_upload_paths` semantics, `upload_log`) unchanged.

title: Feel pass: glowing ring and border beam on focus, loading and new
spec:
The design laps a glowing border beam around the address pill on tab change and page load (ported: `wubble_core::beam`, scene shader beam.wgsl, decisions "Border beam") and draws a glowing ring on focus. TODO "Feel pass" asks for the ring and beam wherever something is focused, loading or newly opened: a loading tab row, a newly opened tab or Space, a focused field or sheet, the command bar on open, a download that just finished.

To build: (1) Generalise `wubble_core::beam` from the single address beam to a small table of beams keyed by surface (a `BeamTarget` enum: Address, TabRow(id), Field, CommandBar, Sheet, DownloadButton). Each has its own lap state and a pure transition from events (Focused, LoadStarted/Finished, Opened), with unit tests. (2) Let the scene draw several beam shapes. `set_beam_shape` in crates/wubble/src/backdrop.rs currently takes one, so it becomes a short list in wubble-gfx scene state and render. For Slint-only glass, use the Slint beam (components/border-beam.slint, to be moved into the kit; see kit-lock-baseline-empty). (3) Add a kit focus-ring piece that follows the design's ring (components/focus-ring.slint into the kit) and use it on every focusable kit control. (4) Beams and rings wake the scene only while lapping (`run.wake_if_still`), and reduced motion turns them off. Add gallery shots. All platforms.

title: HDR: CEF patch for F16 shared-texture capture
spec:
Chrome draws HDR video and HDR images in HDR on capable displays. wubble cannot: CEF's windowless accelerated paint (OnAcceleratedPaint) hands out 8-bit BGRA/RGBA shared textures in sRGB, so HDR content is tone-mapped to SDR before wubble sees it (decisions.md "Colour and HDR", TODO M6 "HDR output: researched and spiked; needs the own build (F16 capture) and a Slint renderer patch"). The surface spike is crates/wubble-gfx/examples/hdr_surface.rs.

What to build: (1) A patch, patches/chromium/5x-cef-osr-f16.patch, in the queue's style. In CEF's OSR video consumer (libcef/browser/osr/video_consumer_osr.cc), when the browser is created with a new windowless setting (or a command-line switch read by an exported marker `cef_wubble_hdr_v1`), request the frame sink video capturer in RGBA_F16 with an extended-linear-sRGB (or the content's) gfx::ColorSpace. Pass the colour space with the shared-texture info, extending cef_accelerated_paint_info_t through the marker table rather than changing the public struct. Cover Linux dmabuf, macOS IOSurface and Windows D3D11 handles. (2) List it in patches/README.md with its marker. (3) welding: read the marker. When present, mark NativeFrame with the pixel format (NativeFramePixelFormat gains Rgba16Float) and the colour space (`wubble change`). The patch cannot be built now; write it so that it applies to CEF 156.0.30. The shell side is a separate feature.

title: Sync collections: bookmarks, history, passwords, addresses, settings, open tabs
spec: With `sync-core` in place, map wubble's data to sync records the way Chrome's data types do. Build: (1) stable ids and change tracking in crates/wubble-store: migration adding a `guid` (random, unique) and `modified_ms` to `bookmarks`, `urls`/`visits` (or a visit guid), `logins`, `addresses` (if present), `settings`, plus a `sync_changes` table (collection, guid, op, at) written in the same transactions that change rows (or derived by comparing `modified_ms` with the last sync mark), and tombstones for deletes. (2) Per-collection adapters implementing a `Collection` trait from wubble-sync: `to_record`/`apply_record`/`merge(local, remote) -> resolution`: bookmarks (tree by parent guid + position, last-writer-wins per field, dedupe of identical url+parent as Firefox Sync does), history (union of visits, capped like Chrome to 90 days), passwords (decrypted on the store thread from wubble-vault and re-encrypted under the sync key only; never plaintext on disk; conflict -> newer `password_modified`), settings (only rows marked syncable in crates/wubble-core/src/settings.rs `SettingDef`, a new `sync: bool` field), Spaces/pinned tabs/open tabs per device as a `tabs` collection (read-only for other devices, feeds `send-tab-to-device`'s "tabs from other devices"). (3) The host applies remote changes through the existing owners (Model for Spaces, store for bookmarks/history, `VaultCommand` for logins) and re-renders. Choose per collection in the sync settings. Unit tests per adapter with merge cases.

title: Task manager: Chrome's columns, sorting and row actions
spec: Chrome's task manager shows Memory footprint, CPU, Network and Process ID by default. Optional columns (right-click the header) include GPU memory, JavaScript memory, image, script and CSS cache, SQLite, idle wake-ups, priority and keepalive count. Columns sort on click, a double-click on a row focuses its tab, and End process works on a multi-selection. wubble's page (`wubble_core::tasks`, `host/tasks.rs`, `TaskItem` in wubble-ui) shows title, state, RSS, CPU and busy reasons. It has no Network or JS memory column, no sort, no row activation and no multi-select. To build: (1) Network: per-tab bytes per second from the received byte counts that wubble's request path already sees. Use `CefResourceRequestHandler::OnResourceLoadComplete` `received_content_length` in the engine's request handler (`wubble-engine/src/filter.rs`), summed per view into a counter the meter reads each second. A pure rate calculation goes in `tasks.rs`. (2) JS memory: while the page is shown, `Runtime.getHeapUsage` per live tab over `View::cdp` once per sample, as "used (total)". (3) GPU memory for the GPU process: `SystemInfo.getInfo` is too heavy, so leave it out unless tm-renderer-pids' table provides it. (4) Sort: a pure `tasks::sort(rows, column, dir)` that keeps a tab's rows grouped as Chrome does, with tests. The column and direction live in host state. (5) Column picker: a kit menu on the header, with choices stored as a hidden List setting. (6) Double-click or Enter on a tab row activates that tab (`Command::Activate`). (7) Multi-select with Shift/Ctrl and End for all. All UI from kit components (list rows, menu, header) in `crates/wubble-ui/ui`.

title: `evaluate`: a DevTools object group per call, released on timeout and on session end
spec: TODO line 74. `agent_evaluate` (crates/wubble/src/host/agent.rs ~3374) puts every call's remote objects in one shared group `EVAL_GROUP` ("wubble-agent"). The group is not released when a call times out (`EVAL_GRACE`) or its session goes, so a long session's page holds every value an agent ever made. `select` already does it right (`SELECT_GROUP` per call, released via `agent_release_group` and `held_group(&Wait)`). Do the same for `evaluate`: name the group per call (for example `wubble-agent-eval-<id>`), carry it in `Wait::Eval`, and release it through `Runtime.releaseObjectGroup` when the answer is sent, when the wait times out (`agent_let_go`), and for every pending call of a session in `agent_forget`. Drop `agent_release_values`' reliance on the shared name. Extend the existing `held_group` unit test pattern if one already covers `select`.

title: Vault unlock off the store thread
spec:
Fetching the vault key from the OS keyring can block for a long time: macOS shows a Keychain prompt, and Linux's Secret Service waits for its unlock dialog. Today `VaultCommand::Unlock` runs on the store thread, which owns the database (crates/wubble-vault/src/command.rs:215, `self.unlock()`; keyring access in crates/wubble-vault/src/keyring.rs). While the prompt is open, every save, history write and query waits behind it (TODO M7 "Hardening: vault unlock off the store thread"). Chrome reads the OS key on a separate task runner.

To build: split unlock into two steps. (1) A `KeyFetch` worker thread, owned by the vault's host side (crates/wubble/src/host/pages.rs or a vault host module), calls `KeyRing::get_or_create` and sends the result back. (2) The store thread only applies the key it is given (`Vault::unlock_with(key)`: check the key against the rows, then report Ready, Unreadable, KeyLost or NewKey). Extend the vault's lifecycle (crates/wubble-vault/src/state.rs) with an explicit `Unlocking` state. Commands that need the key while Unlocking get `NotUnlocked` (the page shows "Waiting for the keyring"), and a second Unlock request while one is in flight is merged into it. Keep the rule "the vault never replaces a lost key": NewKey is created only by the worker after the store thread confirms there are no rows, as two steps with no race. Unit tests with `FakeKeyRing` for the new transitions, including a slow fetch with saves going through meanwhile. All platforms.

title: HDR: shell import, Skia renderer and surface colour space
spec:
This is the shell half of HDR output; the engine half (F16 capture) is a separate patch. Today crates/wubble-gfx/src/import.rs blits every page into an Rgba8Unorm target (TARGET_FORMAT), Slint's Skia renderer (vendor/i-slint-renderer-skia) draws to an 8-bit sRGB wgpu surface, and nothing asks the display for HDR. The spike (crates/wubble-gfx/examples/hdr_surface.rs) already picks the best (format, SurfaceColorSpace) the surface offers: HDR10, HLG, scRGB, extended sRGB, else SDR.

What to build: (1) wubble-gfx: an F16 import path. When a NativeFrame reports Rgba16Float with a colour space, import it into an Rgba16Float target with no 8-bit clamp, keeping the 8-bit path unchanged for SDR frames. Put the pure choice in a function with tests: frame format, surface mode → target format and the shader's encode step. (2) vendor/i-slint-renderer-skia, under its WUBBLE_CHANGES.md rules: create the surface with the HDR mode from the spike's `pick_mode`, render the Skia surface as RGBA_F16 with an SkColorSpace matching it (extended sRGB linear), and keep SDR UI colours at the SDR reference white (203 nits for PQ, 1.0 for scRGB). Extend the partial-render test. (3) A setting, `video.hdr` (default on where the display offers HDR, Section::Appearance), and a `--smoke codecs` report line saying which mode was chosen. (4) The glass and scene shaders (wubble-gfx/src/scene) stay correct in linear F16. Leave glass blur on 8-bit when HDR is off. Linux Wayland and macOS (EDR) first; Windows scRGB behind cfg.

title: Sync transport: WebDAV (Nextcloud, ownCloud, any DAV server)
spec: The owner wants sync to a place the user chooses, such as WebDAV, not a wubble server. Add `WebDavRemote` implementing `sync-core`'s `Remote` trait in crates/wubble-sync: PROPFIND depth 1 for list (parse the multistatus XML with quick-xml, MIT), GET, PUT with `If-Match`/`If-None-Match: *` ETags for safe snapshot replacement, DELETE, MKCOL for the base directory; Basic auth over https only (refuse plain http unless the host is loopback), credentials stored in the OS keyring via `wubble_vault::KeyRing` (a separate account name), never in the settings table; server certificate errors fail closed; timeouts and exponential backoff reported as `sync::State::Error{retry_at}`. HTTP through the workspace's `ureq` 3 dependency on a worker thread, never the UI or CEF IO thread. Requests go only to the URL the user typed and only while `sync.enabled` is on (the no-phone-home rule); add the transport to `net_audit.rs` expectations as an opt-in request so `--smoke data` stays clean on a fresh profile. Unit tests for the PROPFIND parser with Nextcloud and Apache mod_dav fixtures, and a loopback test server in tests is not required (owner: no new tests beyond unit level).

title: Screen reader detection on macOS and Windows
spec: Chrome turns its accessibility tree on when an assistive technology connects, on every platform. wubble's `a11y.web` auto mode (`wubble_core::apply::web_accessibility`) depends on `crates/wubble/src/screen_reader.rs`, which has a Linux AT-SPI source only. macOS and Windows use `NoReader` (always false), so on auto, VoiceOver and NVDA users get no page content until they find the setting. To build: implement the existing `ScreenReader` trait per platform in `screen_reader.rs`, read off the UI thread the way `os_motion.rs` reads reduced motion. macOS: `NSWorkspace.sharedWorkspace.isVoiceOverEnabled`, observed with KVO (`voiceOverEnabled`) through objc2-app-kit, already a dependency for `mac_app.rs` (check its feature list). Also treat `AXIsProcessTrusted` clients as on, as Chrome's `BrowserAccessibilityStateImplMac` does via `NSApplication accessibilityRequested`/`AXEnhancedUserInterface` (behaviour only). Windows: `SystemParametersInfoW(SPI_GETSCREENREADER)`, polled on the existing watcher cadence, plus the `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`/`SPI_SETSCREENREADER` notice if the event loop exposes it. Add a `windows` crate feature only if needed, compile-checked by CI. The pure decision stays `apply::web_accessibility`. Also make the Settings label of `a11y.web` say auto works on all three platforms.

title: Tab menu: two-level "Move tab to" listing user Spaces; moving out of an agent Space makes an ordinary tab
spec: TODO line 77 (owner, 2026-11-20). Today `wubble_core::tabmenu` (`Row::MoveToSpace`, ~line 179) adds one flat "Move to <Space>" row per other Space. Replace it with one row "Move tab to" with a ">" that opens a submenu on hover, the way Chrome's "Move tab to another window" does. The submenu lists user-created Spaces only (not agent Spaces, `Space::agent`), in sidebar order, the current one left out. Use the kit menu's submenu if it has one (`kit/controls/menu.slint`); if not, the submenu is a derived piece (menu rows in a second Menu positioned at the row's right edge) and goes on docs/fidelity/derived-review.md. Model it in the menu data (`Run::Submenu(Vec<Entry>)` or similar) in tabmenu.rs and its renderer in `crates/wubble/src/menu.rs`. Moving a tab out of an agent Space through it releases it from its session: run the agent effect that unbinds the tab (wubble_core::agent) so it becomes an ordinary tab of the target Space, with its container kept or switched to the Space's container as Chrome would (ask the core model; record the choice in the final report). Add unit tests in tabmenu.rs and model tests for core logic.

title: Opt-in crash reports that open a GitHub issue
spec:
Decisions "Network on its own": no telemetry; crash reports are opt-in and open a GitHub issue (TODO M7). Chrome uses Crashpad with an upload consent. wubble must not upload anything itself.

To build: (1) Capture. Add a panic hook in crates/wubble/src/main.rs that writes a crash record: version, OS, CEF version, GPU adapter (`GpuContext::describe`), the panic message, a symbol-only backtrace and the last trace stage. It goes to `<profile>/crashes/<time>.json`. For CEF's own processes, turn on CEF's crash dump writing to the same directory (CEF settings `crash_reporter.cfg` with no `ServerURL`, so nothing uploads; minidumps stay local). The run-state record already tells an unclean exit (the updater's failed-start counter). (2) A pure scrubber in wubble-core (`crash.rs`): remove the home directory and user name from paths, URLs and query strings, e-mail-like strings and profile names. It returns the issue body as text, and is unit-tested. (3) A setting `crash.offer_reports` (off by default). With it on, the next start finds the unsent records and shows a toast (kit) "wubble closed unexpectedly" with a Report button and a Dismiss button. Report opens a new tab at `https://github.com/<repo>/issues/new?title=...&body=...`, the scrubbed body in the URL and cut to GitHub's URL limit, so the user reviews and submits it; wubble sends nothing. The minidump stays local, and the body says where it is. All platforms.

title: Widevine CDM loader and Protected content setting
spec:
Chrome plays DRM video (Netflix, Spotify, Disney+, Prime) through the Widevine CDM, which the component updater fetches and keeps up to date. wubble's CEF build sets enable_widevine (scripts/build-cef.sh, docs/research/cef-codec-build.md) but ships no CDM and has no loader (TODO M6 "a CDM loader (installed CDM, else opt-in download)", decisions.md "DRM"). The permission bit PROTECTED_MEDIA_IDENTIFIER is denied (wubble_core::site has no such Permission).

What to build: (1) A pure planner in a new wubble-core/src/cdm.rs, `fn plan(found: &[CdmInstall], profile_hint: Option<..>) -> CdmPlan`. Candidate installs: Google Chrome's /opt/google/chrome/WidevineCdm, Chromium's and Brave's user-data WidevineCdm/<ver>, Firefox's gmp-widevinecdm/<ver>, and on macOS the Chrome app bundle's or profile's WidevineCdm. Pick the newest version whose manifest.json fits this architecture. Unit tests. (2) In crates/wubble/src/profile.rs, before CEF starts, write Chromium's hint file `<root_cache>/WidevineCdm/latest-component-updated-widevine-cdm` (JSON {"Path": dir}), the path chrome/common/media/cdm_registration.cc reads on Linux. On macOS and Windows, copy or symlink the version directory into `<root_cache>/WidevineCdm/<ver>`, where the component installer registers installed versions at start. Check each road against CEF 156's code and note which works. (3) An opt-in download (`media.widevine_download`, default off) through the component update protocol, with app id oimompecagnajdejgnnjijobebaeigek. It verifies the CRX3 and unpacks into the profile. (4) Permission::ProtectedContent and a Settings row "Sites can play protected content". (5) docs: DRM limits (L3; VMP-signed services refuse).

title: Sync settings: set up, passphrase, destination, data types, devices
spec: Chrome's "You and Google > Sync" page turns sync on, picks data types, sets an encryption passphrase, and lists devices. wubble needs the equivalent for `sync-core`: build a Settings section (crates/wubble-core/src/settings.rs new `Section::Sync` with `sync.enabled` default false and per-collection toggles bookmarks, history, passwords, addresses, settings, open tabs; rendered by crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/settings.slint) and a setup sheet from kit parts: (1) destination choice: "A folder" (OS folder chooser via `crate::chooser`, `Pick::Folder`) or "WebDAV" (URL, username, password fields), with a Test button; (2) passphrase: create (twice, strength from zxcvbn if `pw-checkup` added it) or, when the destination already holds `keys.json`, enter it to join; show and copy the recovery code once; (3) status row: last synced time, error text from `sync::State::Error`, "Sync now"; (4) devices list from the device registry with rename for this device and "Remove" (writes a tombstone so the removed device stops syncing on its next run); (5) "Turn off and forget" which removes the keyring entries and local sync marks but not data.
