Host wiring in a new crates/wubble/src/host/sync.rs that owns the `sync::State` and runs effects on a worker thread, with a periodic timer only while enabled (no idle polling when off, respecting the 0-to-2 slint_renders idle rule: status updates must not redraw while hidden). Gallery scenes for each sheet state; derived pieces listed on docs/fidelity/derived-review.md.

title: Caret browsing (F7)
spec: Chrome toggles caret browsing with F7, after a confirm dialog ("Turn on caret browsing?" with "Don't ask again"). A movable text caret then appears in page content for keyboard selection. The setting is also in Settings, Accessibility, "Navigate pages with a text cursor" (pref `settings.a11y.caretbrowsing.enabled`, pushed to Blink's `WebPreferences::caret_browsing_enabled` by `ChromeContentBrowserClient::OverrideWebkitPrefs`). wubble has neither. To build: (1) Settings: a Bool `a11y.caret_browsing` (default 0, Accessibility section) and a hidden `a11y.caret_browsing_no_ask`. (2) `wubble_core::action`: `Action::ToggleCaretBrowsing` bound to F7 (all platforms) in `keys.rs`, PageFirst. The first press shows a kit confirm sheet (reuse `controls::confirm`) unless no_ask is set. A pure transition decides ask, toggle or nothing, with tests. (3) Engine: generalise `View::set_minimum_font_size`'s request-context preference code into `View::set_preference(name, Value)` (bool, int, string and list variants) in `crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs`, and set `settings.a11y.caretbrowsing.enabled` on every container's request context at start and on change, through `wubble_core::apply`'s effect list. If CEF's Alloy-style windowless views do not pick the pref up (check by hand), fall back to DevTools `Emulation`... there is none, so instead send `Page.setWebLifecycleState`... no. In that case, report it as an engine patch needed in `OverrideWebkitPrefs` for Alloy browsers.

title: Clearing an agent Space with tabs asks first: Close anyway or Move tabs
spec: TODO line 78 (owner, 2026-11-20). The dustbin on an agent Space's row in the Spaces popup (`wubble_core::agent` ~line 982, `spacemenu.rs` `Row` with the dustbin) clears the Space at once. When it still has tabs, ask first. Show a confirm in the popup (kit confirm/sheet parts, derived if needed, on docs/fidelity/derived-review.md) with "Close anyway" and "Move tabs". "Move tabs" opens the list of user-created Spaces downward, in the popup. Picking one moves every tab there as ordinary tabs (the same unbind as `move-tab-to-space-submenu`), then clears the Space. Model it as one enum in core (for example `DustbinAsk { Idle, Asking(SpaceId), Picking(SpaceId) }` with a pure transition returning effects: StopSession, MoveTabs(to), DeleteSpace), executed in the host (`crates/wubble/src/host/agent.rs` where the dustbin is handled). A Space with no tabs still clears at once. Unit tests in wubble-core.

title: Cast a video to a Chromecast or DIAL device (CefMediaRouter)
spec:
Chrome's Cast… (menu, media hub) discovers Cast and DIAL sinks on the LAN and mirrors a tab or casts a site's media through the Cast SDK and the Presentation and Remote Playback APIs. Tab mirroring and the sites' Cast SDK (chrome.cast, provided by Chrome's media router component extension) are out of reach in windowless CEF without large engine work. CEF 156 does expose CefMediaRouter (cef_media_router.h: GetGlobalMediaRouter, AddObserver, NotifyCurrentSinks, CreateRoute, SendRouteMessage), and the cef crate has the bindings. wubble does no casting at all.

What to build: (1) welding or wubble-engine: a thin wrapper, crates/wubble-engine/src/cast.rs, the only file naming the CEF media router types. It covers observing sinks (name, icon type, cast or DIAL), routes and messages, with every event queued to the UI thread. (2) wubble-core/src/cast.rs: one enum and a pure transition for a cast session (Discovering → SinkChosen → Connecting → Playing/Paused → Ended/Failed). Effects are Cast v2 messages for the Default Media Receiver (app CC1AD845: LAUNCH, LOAD with the video's URL, content type and title, PLAY, PAUSE, SEEK, STOP), built and parsed as JSON. Unit tests. (3) Source: the primary video's plain URL from the media downloader's detection (wubble_core::media). A DRM, MSE or blob video says "This video cannot be cast". (4) UI: a Cast… row in the video strip's menu and in the media hub, and a sink picker popover from kit parts (derived, on the review sheet). (5) Discovery uses mDNS on the LAN, so it stays behind `media.cast`, default off. All platforms.

title: Send tab to your devices, and tabs from other devices, over sync
spec: Chrome's page and tab context menus offer "Send to your devices" (the other device shows a notification/omnibox chip to open it), and History shows "Tabs from other devices". Build on `sync-core`/`sync-collections`: (1) a `sent_tabs` collection: record {id, url, title, from_device, to_device, sent_ms, opened}, encrypted like others, expiring after 10 days (Chrome's TTL), deleted when opened or dismissed; pure merge and expiry logic with unit tests. (2) Sending: a "Send to your devices" row in the tab menu (crates/wubble-core/src/tabmenu.rs `ROWS`, data) and the page context menu (crates/wubble/src/menu.rs), opening a small device picker popover (kit `AMenuPopover` rows with device names from the registry), only shown when sync is on and another device exists; then an immediate sync push. (3) Receiving: on sync pull, a new record for this device shows a toast (crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/toast.slint) "<title> from <device>" with Open (new tab in the current Space) and Dismiss, plus a badge-less entry in the omnibox suggestions list until handled (crates/wubble-core/src/suggest.rs source). (4) Tabs from other devices: a section on the History native page (crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/pages.slint) listing each device's open tabs from the `tabs` collection, click to open. Host in crates/wubble/src/host/sync.rs. Nothing is sent anywhere but the user's own sync destination.

title: Spell check: Add to dictionary, a toggle, a custom word list and context-menu rows
spec: Chrome's context menu on a misspelled word shows the suggestions, "No spelling suggestions", "Add to dictionary" and a "Spell check" submenu ("Check spelling of text fields", languages, Language settings). Settings has "Spell check" on/off, a language list and "Customize spell check", a list of added words with remove. wubble shows only the suggestions (`crates/wubble/src/menu.rs`, group 0, ids 200-204). It has no Add to dictionary, no toggle and no word list (`settings.rs` has no spell row; decision "English spelling dictionary ships" says none existed). To build: (1) In `menu.rs`, CEF ids `MENU_ID_NO_SPELLING_SUGGESTIONS` (205, disabled row) and `MENU_ID_ADD_TO_DICTIONARY` (206, which CEF executes itself: `AddWordToDictionary`). Add a "Check spelling of text fields" toggle row in editable fields. Update menu tests. (2) Settings: a Bool `spell.enabled` (default 1), applied as pref `browser.enable_spellchecking` through a generalised `View::set_preference` (refactor of `set_minimum_font_size` in `wubble-engine/src/view.rs`) on each container's request context, through `wubble_core::apply`. (3) Custom words: Chromium keeps them in `<profile>/Custom Dictionary.txt`. Add a Settings list (kit list editor, `controls::list_editor`) that reads the file and removes words via `CefBrowserHost::RemoveWordFromDictionary` (welding passthrough on a live view), plus an add field (`AddWordToDictionary`). A pure diff of the list in `wubble_core::spell`, with tests. macOS: the system checker learns words through NSSpellChecker; the same CEF calls apply.

title: Autofill: offer the login form a page shows right after a submit
spec: TODO line 79. In `crates/wubble-core/src/autofill.rs`, `settled_after_submit` handles the report that follows a submit. Unless it is the same origin's sign-in form back (a failed sign-in), it goes to `check(p)` (`Phase::Checking`), so a login form on the next page (a second step, an SSO page, a different origin) gets no key chip or menu. The cause is that one `Phase` holds both the save flow and the offer. Fix: split the machine into two parts that run side by side, inside the one transition: `save: SavePhase` (Idle, Submitted, Checking, Prompt) and `offer: OfferPhase` (Idle, Offer, Menu). Each event updates both. The report after a submit both starts the save check and, through `offer(...)`, offers any login form it carries. `View` (`chip`, `menu`, `prompt`) reads both. When the prompt and the chip would show at once, Chrome shows both: keep both. Update the host (`crates/wubble/src/host/autofill.rs`) to the new state shape. Update the existing unit tests and add cases for a second-step login form and a cross-origin SSO form.

title: Live captions from on-device speech recognition
spec:
Chrome's Live Caption captions any audio a tab plays. It uses Google's closed SODA library, downloaded by the component updater, and a renderer-side audio tap in //chrome. Both are out of reach: SODA is proprietary and needs a download from Google, and its tap is not in windowless CEF. A wubble version can still be built from parts in reach. CEF's CefAudioHandler delivers a browser's PCM, but while capture runs it silences the page's own output (crates/wubble-engine/src/media.rs notes this). So wubble must play the captured audio itself.

What to build: (1) welding: wrap CefAudioHandler (OnAudioStreamStarted, OnAudioStreamPacket, OnAudioStreamStopped) behind a `wubble change`, queuing f32 planar packets per view. (2) Engine and host: while captions are on for a tab, start capture on it and play the PCM through a small output, the cpal crate (Apache-2.0). Keep A/V offset as low as the buffer allows, and say in the setting's text that sync may drift. (3) Recognition: whisper.cpp through whisper-rs (MIT/Unlicense) on a worker thread, fed 16 kHz mono chunks. The model is an opt-in download (`media.captions_model_download`, default off) or a file the user picks; nothing ships. (4) Core: a pure caption buffer in wubble-core (segments in, lines out, word-wrap, a 2-line window) with unit tests. (5) UI: a movable caption box over the page from kit parts (derived, on derived-review.md), a Settings row (Accessibility or Appearance), and a toggle in the media hub or video strip. Linux and macOS first.

title: Spell check in other languages: opt-in dictionary download and language list
spec: Chrome lets the user pick several spell-check languages (pref `spellcheck.dictionaries`) and downloads each `<lang>-<ver>.bdic` from redirector.gvt1.com. wubble bundles en-US only, Chromium's download host is refused (decision "Chromium's own requests", `host-resolver-rules`), and TODO "Spell check in other languages" asks for an opt-in download. To build: (1) Core (pure, tested): `wubble_core::spell` gains a table of the languages Chromium 156 supports, with their versioned file names, copied from `components/spellcheck/common/spellcheck_common.cc` `kSupportedSpellCheckerLanguages` and the version map in `chrome/browser/spellchecker/spellcheck_hunspell_dictionary.cc` (BSD, with a source comment). Add a `DictState` per language (Absent, Downloading, Ready, Failed) with a transition. `plan` is extended to multiple wanted languages, never deleting a user-wanted file. (2) Settings: a List `spell.languages` (default `["en-US"]`) and a Bool `spell.download` (default 0, `Section::Privacy`, the label naming the host). While the download setting is off, only installed languages can be picked. (3) Download through wubble's own fetch (`crates/wubble-engine/src/fetch.rs`, which goes through CEF's network stack, so pick a host that `host-resolver-rules` allows): `https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/deps/hunspell_dictionaries/+/refs/heads/main/<file>?format=TEXT` (base64), or a configurable mirror. Write to `<profile>/Dictionaries` atomically and check the size and a pinned SHA-256 from the table. (4) Apply the list as pref `spellcheck.dictionaries` through `View::set_preference` on each request context. On macOS, the list maps to system languages, so nothing is downloaded and the row says so.

title: Agent sign-ins: copy localStorage/IndexedDB, keep CHIPS partition keys, print the copy's report
spec: TODO lines 81-83 (docs/research/mcp-server.md 0.3). Signing a session in copies the owner's cookies for a site into the session's container (`agent_copy_cookies`/`agent_cookies_copied` in crates/wubble/src/host/agent.rs, `crates/wubble-engine/src/storage.rs`). Missing: (1) Site storage. MSAL, Firebase and SPA tokens live in localStorage and IndexedDB. Open a hidden view on the site's origin in the source container (or reuse a live tab of it). Read `DOMStorage.getDOMStorageItems` for the origin's storage id. Read IndexedDB through `IndexedDB.requestDatabaseNames`, `requestData` and a page script for structured values. Write them in a hidden view of the session's container (`DOMStorage.setDOMStorageItem`; an IndexedDB restore script). Close both views. (2) CHIPS. CEF's cookie struct has no partition key, so partitioned cookies arrive unpartitioned. Read with DevTools `Storage.getCookies` (it carries `partitionKey`) and write with `Network.setCookie {partitionKey}` in the session container's view, instead of the CEF cookie manager for those cookies. (3) The one-in-87 "sent: none" failure: print the copy's report (counts per domain, partitioned or not, timings) to stderr and to the session log every time, so the next failure can be traced. Keep it all inside `COPY_BOUND`.

title: Linux print handler: window.print() and the PDF viewer's print
spec:
In Chrome, a page's `window.print()`, the PDF viewer's Print button and Ctrl+P on a PDF all open print preview and print what is shown. wubble's welding implements no CefPrintHandler (no print_handler in vendor/welding/src/linux_cef). On Linux, CEF needs one for printing, so a page's window.print() does nothing. Ctrl+P on a PDF is worked around in crates/wubble/src/host/print.rs `print()`: an `is_pdf` tab is downloaded instead of printed ("printing the viewer gives a blank page").

What to build: (1) welding (Linux): a WeldPrintHandler (cef::wrap_print_handler!) registered beside the find handler in linux_cef/mod.rs, marked `wubble change`. OnPrintDialog holds its callback and reports `NavigationEvent::PrintRequested { id, has_selection }`. OnPrintSettings fills the settings from the host's answer. OnPrintJob hands the host the PDF path Chromium wrote, and the job callback is completed after the host is done. OnGetPdfPaperSize returns the chosen paper. (2) Engine: a PageEvent::PrintRequested and `View::answer_print(id, Option<PrintSettings>)`. (3) Core: wubble_core::print::Sheet gains an origin `FromPage(id)`, so the existing sheet answers the page instead of calling PrintToPDF. Its Effect becomes AnswerPrint, and a job PDF goes to `lp` (or to Downloads for Save as PDF). Unit tests for the new transitions. (4) Host: remove the is_pdf download workaround. Ctrl+P on any tab calls CefBrowserHost::Print, so the PDF viewer's own document is printed through the sheet. macOS uses CEF's native print panel and needs no change; Windows stays Save as PDF.

title: Read aloud with the OS voice (page, selection, Reader view)
spec: Chrome's Reading mode has Read aloud: play/pause, speed, voice choice, and word or sentence highlighting, with OS or network voices. Its context menu also reads selections aloud (ChromeOS select-to-speak). wubble has none (docs/research/tts.md is shelved; TODO "Read aloud with an on-device voice"). Build the OS-voice road from tts.md "If picked up": (1) Core: `wubble_core::read_aloud` gets one enum (Idle, Preparing, Speaking{sentence}, Paused{sentence}, Done) with a pure transition, plus sentence segmentation of the Reader's extracted text (Unicode sentence boundaries via `unicode-segmentation`, MIT/Apache). Speaking is refused while a screen reader runs (`screen_reader.rs`) unless the user asked explicitly. Tests. (2) A `Voice` trait in a new crate `wubble-voice` (OS APIs only, no CEF): `voices()`, `speak(text, voice, rate) -> utterance id`, `pause`, `resume`, `stop`, with word-boundary and end events. Implementations: Linux speech-dispatcher (the `speech-dispatcher` crate or `ssip-client-async`, licence checked), macOS `AVSpeechSynthesizer` (objc2-avf-audio) and Windows SAPI/`Windows.Media.SpeechSynthesis` (compile-checked by CI). (3) Text source: the Reader document (`wubble_core::reader`, `assets/reader.js`) returns sentences with DOM ranges, and highlighting is a CSS Highlight API (`::highlight`) set per sentence or word by `View::eval`. Without reader mode, use the selection or the Readability extraction run without replacing the page. (4) UI: `Action::ReadAloud` with a palette entry, a context-menu row "Read aloud" for a selection, and a kit mini player (play/pause, speed, voice select) in the Reader toolbar. Settings: voice and rate.

title: Agent views no window shows render at a trickle, at full rate only when asked
spec: TODO line 85. An agent session's tabs stay "visible" for CEF even when no window shows them, because a hidden view has no accessibility tree and no screenshot (crates/wubble/src/host/agent.rs ~1999 and ~5136). So they paint at the full windowless frame rate. Keep them unhidden, but drop the rate. When an agent tab is not in any window's panes, call `View::set_frame_rate(1)` (CEF `set_windowless_frame_rate`, crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs ~876). Raise it to the pane rate (`wubble_gfx::pacing::frame_rate_for`) for the length of any call that needs fresh pixels (`screenshot`, `capture`, a shot-based measure) or a fresh layout, then lower it again when the call ends. Also skip importing their frames into the GPU texture path (`wubble-gfx` import) while unshown, if the import runs per paint. Put the rule as a pure function in wubble-core (shown, call in flight, headless → rate) with unit tests, executed by the host. No timing tests.

title: "Download PDFs instead of opening them" site setting
spec:
Chrome's Settings → Privacy → Site settings → PDF documents offers "Open PDFs in Chrome" or "Download PDFs", stored as the pref plugins.always_open_pdf_externally. When it is on, a PDF navigation becomes a download that the system viewer can open. wubble always shows PDFs in Chromium's viewer (host/builtins.rs `pdf` set) and has no such setting.

What to build: (1) wubble-core/src/settings.rs: `PDF_DOWNLOAD` (key pdf.download, Bool, default "0", label "Download PDFs instead of opening them", Section::Privacy, matching Chrome's place), with settings tests. (2) Host: apply it to every request context (each container's) through the existing preference setter (crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs `set_preference`, ~line 865), with the name "plugins.always_open_pdf_externally". Apply it at start and live on change from host/settings.rs. (3) Downloads: a PDF downloaded this way follows the normal download path. If the auto-open feature has landed, it may open automatically, since PDF is a safe type. (4) Check by hand that CEF 156 honours the pref for Alloy-style windowless browsers. If it does not, fall back to the response hook: a top-level navigation answered with application/pdf is cancelled and started again as `View::start_download` in the same tab. Keep that decision a pure function with a unit test. All platforms.

title: Read aloud: bundled or opt-in on-device neural voice
spec: Where the OS has no voice (most Linux installs without speech-dispatcher), Chrome falls back to its network voices. wubble must make no request by default, so docs/research/tts.md proposes a small on-device model as a second `Voice` implementation: tiny-voca (Apache-2.0, about 15-27 MB, English only), compared with Piper (its eSpeak NG phonemizer is GPL-3.0-or-later, acceptable), Kokoro and KittenTTS. To build, on top of read-aloud-os-voice: (1) Pick one after reading the licences tts.md left unchecked (`dizione`, CMUdict, homograph data). Record the pick in the report. (2) Implement `Voice` in `wubble-voice` as `ModelVoice`. Inference runs through `ort` (shared with ocr-backends' ORT dependency) in a child process, with sentence-by-sentence synthesis to 24 kHz PCM. Playback through `cpal` (Apache/MIT), with word timing estimated from phoneme durations for highlighting. (3) Delivery: unless the model is small enough to ship (decide by size), download it only on a press, behind a Bool `read_aloud.model_download` (default 0), through `wubble-engine/src/fetch.rs`, with a pinned SHA-256. Use a pure state machine for the download (Absent, Downloading, Ready, Failed) in `wubble_core::read_aloud`, with tests. (4) The voice list in the read-aloud player marks model voices and the languages they cover. The OS voice is preferred when it exists.

title: Agent airlocks: ask the human for permissions, downloads, external links, popups and off-list navigation
spec: TODO lines 86-87, docs/research/mcp-server.md section 5 "Airlocks" and decision "Agent tabs fail closed". Today an agent-driven tab denies every permission request with no prompt, refuses downloads (also the media downloader's job) and external-protocol links, and blocks off-list navigation, each logged to the session. Build the prompt instead. Add a pure `wubble_core::agent::airlock`: `Airlock` (Idle, Asking{kind, origin, detail}, Answered) per tab with `transition` and effects (Allow, Deny, AllowForOrigin, AddSite). Kinds: Permission, Download{name,size,type}, External{scheme}, Popup{target}, Navigation{from,to,link}. Per-origin pre-approvals live in the session's `Grant` so a repeat does not ask again. The prompt is drawn outside the page's pixels from the kit's prompt family (`kit/overlay/a` permission prompt, `a-prompt`), never focused (no keyjacking), labelled "during an agent session". The call that triggered it waits (`Wait` in crates/wubble/src/host/agent.rs) with the session's `request_human` semantics, and answers allowed or refused. Hook it into the existing deny sites (permission handler, `can_download`/`on_before_download`, the external handler `wubble_core::external`, the popup path, the site guard). Log every answer to the activity log. Unit tests in core.

title: Print sheet: preview, two-sided, colour, pages per sheet, headers
spec:
Chrome's print preview shows the rendered pages and offers destination, pages, copies, layout, colour/black and white, paper size, pages per sheet, margins (including custom), scale, two-sided, headers and footers, and background graphics. wubble's sheet (wubble_core::print PrintSettings: destination, pages, landscape, paper, margins, scale, background, copies; components/print-sheet.slint; host/print.rs runs `lp`) has no preview, two-sided, colour mode, pages per sheet or headers and footers.

What to build: (1) Core (wubble-core/src/print.rs): add `two_sided: Sides { One, LongEdge, ShortEdge }`, `color: bool`, `per_sheet: u8` (1/2/4/6/9/16) and `headers: bool` to PrintSettings. Map them in the pure lp command line builder (`-o sides=…`, `-o print-color-mode=monochrome`, `-o number-up=N`) and in PdfOptions (CEF display_header_footer with Chromium's default header and footer templates: date, title, URL, page numbers). Hide the printer-only options for Save as PDF, as Chrome does. Unit tests for every mapping. (2) Preview: on each settings change, debounced, PrintToPDF into the sheet's temp dir. Show the result in a windowless CEF view inside the sheet, using Chromium's own PDF viewer with its toolbar hidden (`#toolbar=0`), so no PDF rasteriser is added. The preview's lifecycle is a Stage in the Sheet machine. (3) UI: the new rows in print-sheet.slint from kit controls (select, toggle) and the preview pane. Lay it out from the kit, and put the derived pieces on derived-review.md. (4) Remember the last-used printer and options per printer in settings. Linux and macOS (CUPS); Windows stays Save as PDF.

title: Reader mode: Chrome's reading-mode controls in a toolbar
spec: Chrome's reading mode has a toolbar with font (several faces), font size, line spacing (standard, loose, very loose), letter spacing (standard, wide, very wide), colour theme (default, light, dark, yellow, blue), links on/off and images on/off, plus Read aloud. Changes apply live, and it also follows a selection in the page. wubble's reader (`wubble_core::reader`, `ReaderPrefs`: size, width {narrow, medium, wide}, font {serif, sans}, theme {dark, light, sepia}; `assets/reader.js` with fixed line-height 1.65 and letter spacing) is set only from Settings rows (`READER_SIZE`, `READER_WIDTH`, `READER_FONT`, `READER_THEME` in `settings.rs`), with no in-page controls. To build: (1) Core: `ReaderPrefs` gains `line_spacing` (3 steps), `letter_spacing` (3 steps), `links: bool` and `images: bool`, and the themes gain yellow and blue, all with word tables like `WIDTH_WORDS` and new Settings defs. `css_vars` emits `--wb-line`, `--wb-letter` and the theme colours from generated kit tokens where they exist. Update the tests. (2) `reader.js` reads the new vars, and links off renders anchors as plain text and images off hides `figure`/`img`. (3) A toolbar: while reader is `On`, the address pill's reader glyph opens a kit popover (segmented controls for spacing, a slider for size, swatches for theme, toggles for links and images; reuse `controls::segmented`, `slider`, `swatches`, `toggle`). Each change writes the setting and re-applies `css_vars` through `View::eval` without a reload. Also show an estimated reading time under the title (words / 238 wpm, computed in core). (4) The Read aloud button joins this popover once read-aloud-os-voice lands.

title: Agent guardrails: hold non-GET requests after an action (write window) and flag hidden content
spec: TODO line 86 (plan section 5: "This click submits a form" and the hidden-content flags). (1) Write window: after each agent action, hold every non-GET request from the tab's frames for N seconds and ask through the airlock prompt (`agent-airlock-prompts`). Per-origin grants are on by default, and a "review all writes" mode is chosen in the session sheet. This needs the request method and a body summary on the resource-request path: a welding change in `vendor/welding/src/handlers.rs`/`surface.rs`, marked `wubble change` and listed in vendor/welding/WUBBLE_CHANGES.md, adding `method` and the first KB of the upload data to `ResourceRequest` and an asynchronous answer through CEF's `CefCallback` in `on_before_resource_load`. In agent containers, turn service workers off (Playwright's block-service-workers) so requests stay attributable, and keep WebRTC's non-proxied UDP off. (2) Hidden-content flags: `read_page` marks items with opacity 0, font-size 0, off-screen, clipped away, colour on its own background or aria-hidden but visible. Read computed style through a `Runtime.evaluate` in an isolated world (`Page.createIsolatedWorld`) for the listed refs, and add a `hidden` note per line (crates/wubble-core/src/agent/refs.rs, `line()` in host/agent.rs). Flags are a signal, not a defence; say so in the tool text.

title: Media downloader: multi-period DASH and codec-aware default quality
spec:
TODO.md: "Media downloader: a DASH manifest of several periods is refused ('Not supported'); the default quality takes the first row of a height whatever its codec (HEVC or AV1 before H.264)". In wubble-core/src/media/dash.rs, `let [period] = mpd.periods.as_slice() else { … "a manifest with several periods" }` refuses multi-period manifests. In wubble-core/src/media/select.rs, `choose` takes the first choice of the wanted height.

What to build: (1) dash.rs: for several periods, match representations across periods by AdaptationSet content type, then by Representation id, then by (height, codecs, bandwidth). Build one Variant per matched chain, whose segment list concatenates each period's segments, with time offsets from Period@start and @duration. Periods that match nothing (a pre-roll ad period) are skipped, and the row says "ad periods left out". Refuse only when no chain spans the main content. Port dash.js's period handling rules, BSD-3, with a source comment and a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md entry if code is copied. Unit tests with multi-period fixtures. (2) select.rs: at equal height, the default prefers the codec most players open: H.264 (avc1) first, then VP9, AV1 and HEVC. For audio, AAC then Opus. Only can_join and ffmpeg availability override this. Put the order in one data table, used by `choose`, and keep the menu's labels (codec_name) unchanged. Unit tests for the ladder. (3) The writer's join (crates/wubble-engine/src/save.rs) handles period-concatenated fMP4 init changes: a new init segment per period goes through ffmpeg's concat. All platforms.

title: Clipboard isolation for agent tabs on every platform
spec: TODO line 88, plan's clipboard airlock and open question 6. On Wayland the page clipboard goes through the helper's `clipboard.js` bridge (`crates/wubble-helper/src/clipboard.js`, `PageEvent::Clipboard`, crates/wubble/src/clipboard.rs). It cannot tell an agent's copy from the human's. On X11, macOS and Windows, Chromium writes the system clipboard itself. Build: (1) Agent containers get a private clipboard. Force the bridge on in agent containers' renderers on every platform (the helper decides per renderer from a switch or the frame's container, sent by the browser), and suppress Chromium's own writes there by denying the `clipboard-write` and `clipboard-read` permissions to agent containers and handling `execCommand('copy')` through the bridge. The host keeps one clipboard per session (an in-memory buffer). The agent's paste reads only it. (2) A copy out to the human's clipboard goes through the airlock prompt (`agent-airlock-prompts`), showing the truncated text and its origin. (3) A paste from the human's clipboard into an agent tab happens only through an explicit human action. Model the per-session clipboard as data in `wubble_core::agent` with a pure transition.

title: Media detection for service-worker answers and embedded YouTube
spec:
TODO.md review findings: "a video a service worker answers is not seen by the detection (the worker's own fetch has no tab; `--smoke media=probe` on fixtures `sw`): the save control says nothing was found" and "an embedded YouTube player (an iframe of youtube.com) has no lookup, since the lookup keys on the tab's own address". The response hook (host/media.rs, on CEF's IO thread) attributes responses by browser, and a service worker's fetch has none. The YouTube lookup (`media_youtube_page`) runs only for the tab's committed URL (youtube::video_id).

What to build: (1) Service workers: in the response hook, a response with no browser but with a service worker's scope or initiator origin is kept in a small per-origin queue. On the host side, it is credited to every live tab of the same container whose committed origin equals the worker's origin, and the newest active tab of that origin wins when several match. Put the attribution in a pure function in wubble_core::media::detect with unit tests. (2) Embedded YouTube: kit.js's `bigFrame()` also reports the iframe's `src` when it is a youtube.com or youtube-nocookie.com /embed/ID URL. The host feeds that ID to the existing lookup (behind media.youtube, still off by default) and lists the result for the tab as Kind::YouTube, so the strip's save control over the iframe works. Extend youtube::video_id with the embed forms and nocookie hosts, with unit tests. (3) Add the fixture rows to scripts/media-fixtures.py for hand runs. All platforms.

title: Built-in list pages: keyboard open, arrow keys, selection, delete selection, undo, copy address
spec: TODO lines 92 and 133 (Chrome's History and Bookmarks managers). History, Bookmarks, Downloads and Archive rows (`kit/pages/list-row.slint`, `list-table.slint`, models in `wubble_core::pages`, host in `crates/wubble/src/host/pages.rs`) cannot be opened from the keyboard: only a row's Delete is a Tab stop. Up/Down do nothing and a focused row is not scrolled into view. There is no selection, delete selection, undo, copy address or open in a new tab from the keyboard, and a bookmark folder is deleted with its contents by one press. Build: (1) The row itself is focusable (a kit `FocusKeys` on the row, derived, on docs/fidelity/derived-review.md). Enter opens it, Mod+Enter or Shift+Enter opens in a new tab or window, Up/Down/Home/End move focus, and the scroller follows the focused row (the kit scroller's `scroll-to`). (2) Selection as data in core: a `ListSelection` (anchor, set) with a pure transition for click, Shift+click, Mod+click, Shift+arrows and Mod+A. Delete removes the selection. (3) Undo: a deleted batch (or a folder with its contents) shows a toast with Undo (Mod+Z on the page), restored through wubble-store. (4) A row's context menu: Open in new tab, Copy address, Delete. Unit tests in core.

title: Video strip save button: wording and in-progress state
spec:
TODO.md review findings: "Video strip button reads 'Save video'; a second click mid-download re-enters the downloader". Chrome has no such control. The rules for this one come from wubble (decisions.md "Save control"). The strip's save state is wubble_core::video::Save (host/videos.rs video_save_now, video_save_state, video_save_redraw), and the click goes to `video_save(x, y)`, which starts the downloader again even while that video's job runs.

What to build: (1) Core (wubble-core/src/video.rs): make `Save` carry the job's state for this tab's video: Idle, Saving{fraction}, Saved, Failed. Derive it from the downloads entry the media job owns, which has one owner, the downloads list. The click maps to a pure effect: Idle → start the downloader; Saving → open the downloads popover at that row, never a second job; Saved → show in folder or open the menu; Failed → retry. Unit tests over the states. (2) Label: the button's accessible label and tooltip read from that state ("Save video", "Saving video, 40%", "Saved, show in folder", "Save failed, retry"), and the glyph shows progress with the kit's progress part. Settle the wording with the owner's decision on wording if one exists; otherwise use these and flag them. (3) video-controls.slint binds the new fields only (no new drawing outside kit parts). All platforms.

title: Agent sessions: no icon-table entries for their pages; the activity log can be cleared
spec: TODO line 97. Agent session pages are not history, but their origin and icon are filed in the profile's icon table (`crates/wubble-store/src/favicon.rs`, through the host's favicon path `crates/wubble/src/host` and `wubble_core::favicon`). (1) Skip the favicon store write for tabs an agent session drives and for agent Spaces' tabs (the same test as `Model::closes_into_recent`). Keep icons in memory for the session's own rows. (2) Clearing the activity log: the log is a memory ring (`wubble_core::agent::log::ActivityLog`) plus a store tail (`agent_log`, `STORE_MAX`). Add `ActivityLog::clear` (and per session), a store delete, and a "Clear activity" control on the agent activity page (kit button). Also clear it with "Clear browsing data" when its new checkbox "Agent activity" is ticked (`crates/wubble/src/host/data.rs`). Unit tests for the log's clear.

title: Spaces popup: rename and delete on a row, aligned to the Space tile's left edge
spec: TODO line 113. The Spaces popup (`wubble_core::spacemenu` rows, kit `kit/chrome/spaces-menu.slint`, `spaces-button.slint`) aligns differently from the design (the design puts it at the Space tile's left edge) and offers no rename or delete on a user Space's row (only an agent Space's dustbin). (1) Position: anchor the popup to the Space tile's left edge as in the design's web source (look up `browser/` in the design repo, pull first), with the kit popover's anchor math. (2) Row actions: on hover or keyboard focus, a user Space's row shows Rename (in place: the row's label becomes a kit field; Enter commits, Esc cancels) and Delete (confirm when the Space has tabs, as Chrome asks before closing a window with many tabs). Add `Row` actions in spacemenu.rs and the existing Space commands in `wubble_core::model` (`Command::RenameSpace`/`DeleteSpace` or equivalents). Derived kit pieces go on docs/fidelity/derived-review.md. Unit tests in spacemenu.rs.

title: Command bar: the shrinking panel no longer takes clicks during its exit
spec: TODO line 120. While the command bar's panel shrinks away (176 ms), it still takes pointer input, so a click on the page under it is lost. Check the design's exit in the web source (the design repo's `browser/` command bar CSS: whether it sets `pointer-events:none` on the leaving state). Then make the kit part (`crates/wubble-ui/ui/kit/chrome/command-bar.slint` and its overlay layer) stop taking input as soon as its `open` goes false. Gate the TouchArea and FocusScope with `enabled: root.open` (or the motion's target state, not its current value), and let the click fall through to the page view. Also check the host's layer routing (`crates/wubble/src/host/layers.rs`) so the page gets that click. Kit-lock rules apply; no literals in shell files.

title: In-place rename for a new Space in the sidebar
spec: TODO line 121, first half (Chrome names a new tab group in place). Creating a Space gives it a default name that is changed only in Settings. After "New Space", put the sidebar's Space header (`kit/chrome/sidebar.slint`, the Space title part) into an editing state: the title becomes a kit field (`kit/controls/field.slint`) with the text selected. Enter or blur commits through the model's rename command, Esc keeps the default. A double-click on the header renames too. Keep the editing state as data in core (for example `Option<SpaceId>` in the sidebar model with a pure transition), not a Slint boolean. The design has no such state, so this is a derived piece (docs/fidelity/wubble-only.md rules; add it to docs/fidelity/derived-review.md for the owner).

title: Shortcuts: both chords editable, rebinding keeps the second chord, Linux alternates where GNOME takes the chord
spec: TODO lines 121 (second half) and 131. `wubble_core::keys` (crates/wubble-core/src/keys.rs) holds the default table and user overrides (`keys.overrides`). Rebinding the sidebar shortcut also unbinds its second chord, Mod+Alt+S (once compact mode's), and the Settings shortcut editor shows only the first chord. Chrome lets each command keep several accelerators. (1) Make an override per chord slot: `overrides` maps an action to a list of chords, so editing slot 0 leaves slot 1. Settings' shortcut rows show every chord, each editable and removable, with "Add shortcut" (kit parts in `kit/settings`, host `crates/wubble/src/host/settings.rs`). Migrate stored overrides (old single-chord form → slot 0). (2) Linux: chords the desktop takes (GNOME's Super+…, Ctrl+Alt+Arrow workspace switching, Alt+F7/F8 and others) get a default alternate chord on Linux only. Keep the alternates as data in the default table with an `Os` column, so the binding still exists. Unit tests in keys.rs.

title: Start page tiles: the kit tile look and its hover spring
spec: TODO line 124. The start page's tiles (`crates/wubble-ui/ui/kit/pages/start.slint`, host `crates/wubble/src/host/start.rs`, core `wubble_core::start`) are stand-ins. Port the design's tile from the web source (the design repo's `pages/` start page and its CSS: size, radius, glass, favicon tile, label, and the hover spring's stiffness and damping). Its values come through `node tools/fidelity/extract.mjs` into `kit/gen/*.slint` and `wubble_core::kit_gen` (never hand-edited). Drive the hover spring through the existing controls registry (`wubble_core::controls`, the `Controls` slots pattern used by toggle and slider) if it is a physics spring, or through `kit/motion/*` if it is a CSS transition. The kit file starts with its `// design:` header. Lower the kit lock baseline if stand-in literals go away (`KIT_LOCK_WRITE=1` is a test run, so leave the baseline file for the compile step).

title: Settings: Reset per section, rows folding while searching, searchable Filter lists
spec: TODO lines 125 and 136. Against the web design (`pages/settings.tsx`, `settings.css` in the design repo): (1) Reset per section. The kit has `ResetButton` (`kit/settings/reset.slint`), but each section's header has no Reset that restores that section's settings to their defaults. Add it to the section header (`kit/settings/section.slint`), shown while any row in the section differs from its default (`changed` on rows in `wubble_core::pages::settings_page`), and a host action that writes the defaults for that section's keys (`crates/wubble/src/host/settings.rs`). (2) While searching, rows that do not match fold away with the design's fold motion (`kit/motion/fold.slint`), and sections with no match fold too, instead of being dropped from the model at once. (3) The search no longer finds "Your own filter lists": the setting moved to `Section::Hidden`, and the Filter lists section is not searchable. Index the Filter lists section's own rows (and the extensions section's) in the settings search (`wubble_core::pages` search filter) under their visible labels. Unit tests in core.

title: Gallery: scenes for the hover preview card and the sidebar's empty-area menu; a stable page-menu position
spec: TODO line 126. `--smoke gallery` (crates/wubble/src/gallery_smoke.rs, `crates/wubble/src/host/gallery.rs`, scenes listed in docs/smokes.md) has no scene for the tab hover preview card (`components/preview-card.slint`, host `host/preview.rs`, core `hovercard.rs`) or for the sidebar's empty-area context menu. The page menu's position also varies from run to run. Add two scenes that set up the state directly (a hovered tab with a snapshot, and the empty-area menu opened at a fixed point). Pin the page menu's anchor in its scene to a fixed point rather than the last pointer position. Follow the scene table's existing pattern and add the scene names to docs/smokes.md's gallery list. Do not run the gallery (owner rule).

title: Shell fields: Shift+Insert paste, Ctrl+Insert copy, Shift+Delete cut
spec: TODO line 128 (first half; the tests half is out under the owner's no-tests rule). Slint's TextInput has no Shift+Insert, Ctrl+Insert or Shift+Delete shortcuts. Chrome supports them in its omnibox and fields on Linux and Windows. In the key router (`crates/wubble/src/input.rs` `key_route`, where keys that go to a shell field are decided), map Shift+Insert to the paste action (through the host's clipboard path, `crates/wubble/src/clipboard.rs`, which on Wayland goes through the window's worker), Ctrl+Insert to copy and Shift+Delete to cut, for the focused shell field only. Pages get these keys as before. Put the mapping in the keybinding data (`wubble_core::keys` default table, Linux and Windows only, as Chrome does) rather than special-casing it in the router.

title: Fix the hue under the command bar in dark overlay mode
spec: TODO line 129. `--smoke overlay=dark` fails a hue check under the command bar. It failed before the glass fix too, so the glass fix did not cause it. Look at what the check samples (crates/wubble/src/overlay_smoke.rs), and at what the scene draws under the command bar in dark mode: the glass tint and the backdrop from `crates/wubble/src/backdrop.rs`, `wubble-gfx` `scene/render.rs`, and the dark tokens in `kit/gen/tokens.slint`. Compare with the design's dark command bar (the design repo's `browser/` CSS, the glass and command-bar rules). Find whether the tint takes the light palette's hue or the page's theme colour (`wubble_core::pagetheme`) where the design uses the shell's dark hue. Fix the source of the colour, not the check. Do not run the smoke; reason from code and the design.

title: Autofill key chip at the focused field, pane-aware in split view
spec: TODO line 130. Chrome anchors the password-manager key and dropdown to the focused field. wubble's key chip sits over the page's top left and is not pane-aware in split view (crates/wubble/src/host/autofill.rs; the chip in the autofill menu component `components/autofill-menu.slint`). Get the focused field's rect without an engine patch: the helper's `crates/wubble-helper/src/autofill.js` already reports forms. Add the focused field's `getBoundingClientRect()` (CSS px, top document coordinates, plus the frame offsets when the field is in an iframe), and re-report on focus, scroll and resize, throttled to a frame. Carry it in the autofill report (`wubble_core::autofill` `FormSnapshot` or a new focus event). Place the chip and the menu at that rect in the field's pane: convert with the pane's rect (`Host::pane_rects`) and the page zoom. Unit tests in core for the placement maths.

title: Narrow Settings: slider and select rows wrap to full width
spec: TODO line 132. At a content width of 759 px or less, the design's narrow block (`settings.css`:120-130 in the design repo's pages) wraps a row's control below its label at full width. wubble's slider and select rows do not (repro `WUBBLE_SHOT_SIZE=960x640 --smoke settings --shot`, which the owner runs, not you). In the kit settings row (`crates/wubble-ui/ui/kit/settings/*.slint` and the row parts that hold sliders and selects), add the narrow layout. Below the design's breakpoint (from `kit/gen/css.slint`, generated by `tools/fidelity/extract.mjs`; add it there if missing), put the control on its own line at full width with the design's gap. Keep it in kit files only, with the `// design:` header updated to the lines it now covers.

title: FocusKeys with native-button false fires only once on a held Enter or Space
spec: TODO line 134. `FocusKeys` (crates/wubble-ui/ui/components/focus-ring.slint ~33) with `native-button: false` fires its activation again on key repeat (a held Enter or Space). A native button activates once per press: Space on release, Enter on press without repeat. Slint's `KeyEvent` has a `repeat` field. In `key-pressed`, ignore events with `event.repeat` for Enter and Space. Activate Space on `key-released`, and Enter on its first press, as the platform buttons do. This is a component file. If it moves into the kit, it follows kit rules. Check that every user of `FocusKeys` keeps working (list rows, settings rows, menus).

title: A Space button opened by keyboard gives the Spaces menu the keyboard focus
spec: TODO line 137. Opening the Spaces popup from the Space button with the keyboard (Enter or Space on `kit/chrome/spaces-button.slint`) leaves the focus on the button. Chrome's menus take the keyboard on open, with the first or current item highlighted. When the popup opens by keyboard, move focus into the menu (`kit/chrome/spaces-menu.slint`), with the current Space's row focused. Up/Down move between rows, Enter opens, Esc closes and returns focus to the button. Record how it was opened (keyboard or pointer) as data in the overlay state (`wubble_core::overlay` or `spacemenu.rs`) so a pointer open does not show a focus ring. Kit rules apply.

title: Popover scroll thumbs no longer cover the rows' right edge
spec: TODO line 138. In popovers (downloads, extensions, menus), the scroll thumb's touch area (`crates/wubble-ui/ui/kit/controls/scroller.slint`) covers the rows' right edge, so clicks there grab the thumb instead of the row. Follow the design's scrollbar (the design repo's CSS for the popover scroll thumb: width, inset, hit area). Limit the thumb's TouchArea to the thumb's drawn rect plus the design's padding. Show the track's hit area only while the thumb is visible (hovered or scrolling), and let row clicks through elsewhere. Kit-only change, with the `// design:` header updated.

title: Settings Select fits its longest label (no clipped value)
spec: TODO line 139. The Settings Select (`crates/wubble-ui/ui/kit/controls/select.slint`) clips a long value at its fixed width: "Ask on first sea" for the search engine with none chosen. Follow the design's select (`pages/settings.css` / select source in the design repo). Either size the closed control to its widest option label (measure every option's text width in Slint through a hidden `Text` per option, or pass the max width from the model), capped at the row's available width, or elide with an ellipsis where the design elides. Prefer the design's behaviour. Keep it in the kit. The select's list (drawn by Slint, no blur) is a separate owner item; leave it.

title: A popover's entrance dirties only its own region, so partial rendering helps
spec: TODO line 140. During a popover's entrance, the glass's scene scale and alpha change each frame, and that marks the whole window dirty (`wubble-gfx` scene `state.rs`/`render.rs`, the partial renderer in `vendor/i-slint-renderer-skia`, the glass in `wubble_core::glass`). Make the glass layer's damage the union of its old and new bounds (scaled rect plus blur radius), not the window. Find where a change in a glass region's transform or opacity calls the full-window invalidate (probably the scene's backdrop or blur pass assuming a global change), and report the region instead. Check that the backdrop blur under the popover samples only the area it needs. After the change the owner measures (`--measure idle --seconds 4` must report 0 to 2 `slint_renders`, per AGENTS.md); do not run it yourself. No timing tests.

title: Transparent window with compositor blur: macOS vibrancy, KDE blur
spec: TODO line 144. The window is frameless with a transparent background and transparent corners (decisions "Frameless window", "Window platform flags", `crates/wubble/src/host/window.rs`, `crates/wubble/src/backdrop.rs`). There is no compositor blur behind it. Add: (1) macOS, an `NSVisualEffectView` behind the content view (material `.underWindowBackground` or `.sidebar`, state active), through objc2 on the winit `NSView` from the raw window handle. The window-vibrancy crate (MIT/Apache) is a source to copy from, with a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry. (2) KDE Plasma on Wayland: the `org_kde_kwin_blur_manager` protocol on the window's `wl_surface` (wubble's own Wayland worker `crates/wubble/src/wl/wayland.rs`, which already owns the display connection), with the region set to the sidebar and chrome areas. On X11 KDE, the `_KDE_NET_WM_BLUR_BEHIND_REGION` property. GNOME stays opaque. Then the shell's glass skips its own backdrop blur in the blurred regions (the scene's glass quality in `wubble-gfx/src/scene/quality.rs`). Detect support at run time, and add a setting to turn it off. One `WindowBlur` trait with per-platform implementations.

title: Windows CI: make the four failing tests pass or gate them
spec: TODO line 148 (run 44988591703). (1) `instance::tests::the_private_root_by_platform` (crates/wubble/src/instance.rs ~495): the test's temp dir `PathBuf::from("/tmp/me")` is not absolute on Windows, so `private_root_from` returns `/tmp`. Build the test paths so they are absolute on the host OS (for example from `std::env::temp_dir().join("me")`, with a drive prefix on Windows) and keep the per-OS expectations. (2) `updater::install::tests::linux_stages_switches_current_and_rolls_back` (crates/wubble/src/updater/install.rs) is Linux-only: gate it `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`. (3) `mcp::tests::a_connection_answers_discovery_and_hands_calls_to_the_host` and `a_stop_closes_open_connections_and_ids_never_repeat` (crates/wubble/src/mcp.rs): read the named-pipe transport path on Windows (interprocess local sockets under `\\.\pipe\`, `private_by_dir_impl`, socket naming from `runtime_dir`). Likely causes are a filesystem-path socket name that Windows does not accept, or a peer check (`peer_is_me`) unimplemented there. Fix the code so Windows uses a namespaced pipe name derived from the path. Do not run the tests here; CI runs them.

title: Input: kinetic wheel fling on Linux and real touch input
spec: TODO line 153 (first half). (1) Kinetic scroll. On Wayland and libinput touchpads, winit delivers wheel deltas with no momentum after the fingers lift. Chrome on Linux runs its own fling (`ui/events/gestures/fling_curve.cc`, BSD-3-Clause) from the scroll-stop event. Port the fling curve into a pure `wubble_core` module (state machine: Idle, Tracking(velocity), Flinging(curve, t0), with `transition` and unit tests). On winit's `TouchPhase::Ended` for pixel deltas, start the fling. Each frame, send its deltas through `View::wheel` (crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs) until it decays or a new touch or click cancels it. (2) Touch. Forward winit `WindowEvent::Touch` (Slint's winit backend hook, `crates/wubble/src/slint_backend.rs`/`input.rs`) over a page to CEF `send_touch_event` (welding `drag::send_touch` already wraps it, `view.rs` ~737), with ids, pressure and DIP coordinates per pane. Touches over the shell stay with Slint. Turn on Chromium's touch events through the command line (`--touch-events=enabled`) where needed.

title: Cursors: CSS url() images and zoom cursors; the AltGr modifier flag
spec: TODO line 153 (second half). (1) Cursors: `crates/wubble-engine/src/nav.rs` (`impl From<CursorShape> for Cursor`) maps ZoomIn/ZoomOut and every `Custom` shape (CSS `cursor:url(...)`) to Default, because Slint's MouseCursor has no such shapes. Add welding support for CEF's custom cursor (`on_cursor_change` with `CT_CUSTOM`'s `custom_cursor_info`: RGBA buffer, size, hotspot), as a `wubble change` in `vendor/welding/src/cursor.rs`/`surface.rs` (`CursorShape::Image{rgba,w,h,hot}`), listed in WUBBLE_CHANGES.md. In the host, set it on the winit window directly (`winit::window::CustomCursor::from_rgba`, and `CursorIcon::ZoomIn/ZoomOut` for zoom) through Slint's winit accessor while the pointer is over the page, and hand the cursor back to Slint when it leaves. Cache custom cursors by hash. (2) AltGr: `crates/wubble-engine/src/input.rs` notes `EVENTFLAG_ALTGR_DOWN` is lost. Track AltGraph from winit's logical key (`NamedKey::AltGraph`, seen in crates/wubble/src/input.rs ~97) as held state, and set the flag on key and mouse events. On Windows, Ctrl+Alt reported with text counts as AltGr (input.rs ~153).

title: IME: caret rect before the first composed character, underline styles and replacement range
spec: TODO line 154. `crates/wubble/src/ime.rs` maps winit `Ime` events to `View::ime_set_composition(text, selection)` (crates/wubble-engine/src/view.rs ~1643), which passes no underlines and no replacement range. The candidate window is placed only once CEF reports `OnImeCompositionRangeChanged`, which comes after the first composed character. (1) Caret rect before composition: when a page field gains focus (CEF `on_virtual_keyboard_requested` or the helper's focus report), get the caret rect from a page script: the focused element's selection range `getClientRects()`, or for input and textarea a mirror-div measurement. Then call winit `set_ime_cursor_area` with it. Update on selection change (`OnTextSelectionChanged`). (2) Underlines: winit's `Ime::Preedit` gives only a cursor range. Build CEF `CompositionUnderline`s: a thin underline over the whole preedit and a thick one over the selected clause (the cursor range when non-empty), as Chromium's GTK input method context does. (3) Replacement range: pass `Range{from,to}` as the invalid range (u32::MAX) unless winit reports a surrounding-text replacement. Keep the mapping pure in ime.rs with unit tests.

title: Engine patch: a real audible signal per tab (iframes, shadow DOM, WebAudio)
spec: TODO lines 122 and 162 (second half). The audible badge comes from a page probe that misses iframes, shadow DOM and WebAudio. CEF 156 has no audio-state callback: `CefAudioHandler` captures the stream and takes it from the output, so it cannot be used for a badge. Chrome uses `WebContentsObserver::OnAudioStateChanged` / `WebContents::IsCurrentlyAudible`. Write `patches/chromium/60-cef-audible.patch` (CEF side, `#if BUILDFLAG(ENABLE_CEF)`, wubble change marks, header per patches/README.md). Observe `OnAudioStateChanged` in CEF's browser host and call an exported callback registered through a new C table `cef_wubble_audible_v1` (set_callback(fn(browser_id, audible))), with its own marker symbol like patch 40. On the wubble side, look it up in `crates/wubble-engine/src/ext_api.rs` and turn it into `PageEvent::Audible(bool)`. Route it to the existing audible state (`wubble_core` tab facts, rail badge, media keys' first-sound trigger). Keep the probe as the fallback when the marker is absent. Do not build the engine (there are no Chromium rebuilds now).

title: Engine patch: macOS key repeats reach the page with repeat true
spec: TODO line 135. On macOS, CEF 156 builds its NSEvent from a `CefKeyEvent` with `isARepeat:NO`, so a held key's repeats reach the page with `KeyboardEvent.repeat == false` (YouTube's Space tap versus hold-for-2x breaks). Write a one-concern patch `patches/chromium/70-cef-mac-key-repeat.patch` (CEF side, `libcef/browser/osr/render_widget_host_view_osr_mac` or the key event conversion in `browser_platform_delegate_native_mac.mm`). Carry a repeat bit, either a new `EVENTFLAG` bit in `CefKeyEvent::modifiers` that wubble sets for winit's `repeat: true` or the existing `is_system_key` path, into `isARepeat:`. Mark it `wubble change`, give it a What/Why/Applies-in header, and list it in patches/README.md. In wubble, set the bit on repeats in `crates/wubble-engine/src/input.rs` only when the patch's marker is found. When it lands, drop parity's `A.space-repeat` Mac gap (`crates/wubble/src/parity.rs`). Do not build the engine.

title: Web content as a real accessibility subtree in the OS tree
spec: TODO line 163. `wubble_ax` maps a page's CEF accessibility tree to AccessKit (`PageTree::apply`, `graft_node(tree)`), but the subtree reaches only wubble's own screen-reader pane: Slint exposes no API to graft foreign AccessKit nodes under one of its items, and its winit backend owns the AccessKit adapter. Take the backend-patch road: vendor Slint's `i-slint-backend-winit` accesskit module under `vendor/`, as `vendor/i-slint-renderer-skia` is vendored (same rules: a WUBBLE_CHANGES.md and `wubble change` marks). Add a hook so the embedder can supply extra `TreeUpdate`s whose nodes are children of a given Slint item's AccessKit node (the page view item), merged into the adapter's updates. Route AccessKit action requests on those nodes back to the embedder (`PageTree::action` → `PageAction`, executed in crates/wubble/src/host/ax.rs). Feed it from host/ax.rs on every tree update and location change, with frame offsets per pane. Keep the version pins together (slint, wgpu).

title: Windows sandbox: wubble as a client DLL behind CEF's bootstrap.exe
spec: TODO line 164. CEF 156 on Windows runs the sandbox only when the executable is CEF's `bootstrap.exe` (or `bootstrapc.exe` for console) loading the application as a client DLL that exports `RunWinMain`/`RunConsoleMain` with the sandbox info (CEF's `cef_sandbox_win` changes since M1xx; `tests/cefsimple` shows the layout). Restructure on Windows: build the `wubble` binary's entry as a `cdylib` (a new crate or a `[lib] crate-type=["cdylib"]` target, for example `crates/wubble-win-client`) exporting `RunWinMain(HINSTANCE, LPTSTR, int, void* sandbox_info, cef_version_info_t*)`, which calls the existing main with the sandbox info passed into `CefInitialize`/`CefExecuteProcess`. The helper (`crates/wubble-helper`) does the same for subprocesses. Packaging (`scripts/release/` Windows step, `crates/wubble-bundle`) renames bootstrap.exe to wubble.exe and puts `wubble.dll` beside it. Keep Linux and macOS untouched. Windows is CI-only: it must compile in CI.
